children.text: dakṣaṃ prajāpatiṃ vastham aśvinau vākyam ūcatuḥ
children.translated_text: The two <s>Aśvins</s> spoke these words to <s>Dakṣa Prajāpati</s>:

children.text: kuto harītakī jātā tasyāstu kati jātayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From where did <s>harītakī</s> arise, and how many varieties does it have?

children.text: rasāḥ kati samākhyātāḥ kati coparasāḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: How many tastes are ascribed to it, and how many secondary tastes are remembered?

children.text: nāmāni kati coktāni kiṃvā tāsāṃ ca lakṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: How many names are stated, and what are their characteristics?

children.text: ke ca varṇā guṇāḥ ke ca kā ca kutra prayujyate
children.translated_text: What are their colors and qualities? Which one is used, and where?

children.text: kena dravyeṇa saṃyuktā kāṃś ca rogān vyapohati ||
children.translated_text: With what substance is it combined, and what diseases does it drive away?
Revered sir, you ought to answer this question just as it has been asked.
Having heard the words of the two <s>Aśvins</s>, <s>Dakṣa</s> spoke these words:
When <s>Śakra</s> was drinking nectar, a drop fell upon the earth.
From that divine drop arose <s>harītakī</s> of seven kinds.
<s>Harītakī</s> is called <s>Abhayā</s>, <s>Pathyā</s>, <s>Kāyasthā</s>, <s>Pūtanā</s>, and <s>Amṛtā</s>,
also <s>Haimavatī</s>, <s>Avyathā</s>, <s>Cetakī</s>, <s>Śreyasī</s>, and <s>Śivā</s>,

children.text: vayaḥsthā vijayā cāpi jīvantī rohiṇīti ca ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Vayaḥsthā</s>, <s>Vijayā</s>, <s>Jīvantī</s>, and <s>Rohiṇī</s>.
<s>Vijayā</s>, <s>Rohiṇī</s>, <s>Pūtanā</s>, <s>Amṛtā</s>, and <s>Abhayā</s>,

children.text: jīvantī cetakī ceti pathyāyāḥ sapta jātayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Jīvantī</s>, and <s>Cetakī</s>: these are the seven varieties of <s>Pathyā</s>.

children.text: vindhyādrau vijayā himācalabhavā syāccetakī pūtanā sindhau syādatha rohiṇī nigaditā jātā pratiṣṭhānake
children.translated_text: <s>Vijayā</s> grows on the <s>Vindhya</s> mountain; <s>Cetakī</s> comes from the <s>Himālaya</s>; <s>Pūtanā</s> is found in <s>Sindhu</s>; and <s>Rohiṇī</s> is said to arise at <s>Pratiṣṭhāna</s>.

children.text: campāyām amṛtābhayā ca janitā deśe surāṣṭrāhvaye jīvantīti harītakī nigaditā sapta prabhedā budhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: In <s>Campā</s> grow <s>Amṛtā</s> and <s>Abhayā</s>; in the country called <s>Surāṣṭra</s> grows <s>Jīvantī</s>. Thus the wise state the seven divisions of <s>harītakī</s>.

children.text: alābuvṛttā vijayā vṛttā sā rohiṇī smṛtā
children.translated_text: <s>Vijayā</s> is gourd-shaped; that which is round is remembered as <s>Rohiṇī</s>.
<s>Pūtanā</s> has a large stone and little flesh; <s>Amṛtā</s> is said to be fleshy.
<s>Abhayā</s> is declared to have five ridges; <s>Jīvantī</s> is golden in color.
<s>Cetakī</s> should be known by three ridges. This is the form of the seven.
<s>Vijayā</s> is used in all diseases; <s>Rohiṇī</s> heals wounds.
<s>Pūtanā</s> should be applied as a paste, and <s>Amṛtā</s> is beneficial for cleansing.
<s>Abhayā</s> is praised for eye disease; <s>Jīvantī</s> removes all diseases.
<s>Cetakī</s> is praised for use as a powder; one should employ each as appropriate.

children.text: cetakī dvividhā proktā śvetā kṛṣṇā ca varṇataḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Cetakī</s> is said to be of two kinds by color, white and black.

children.text: ṣaḍaṅgulāyatā śuklā kṛṣṇā tv ekāṅgulā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: The white is six <s>aṅgulas</s> long, while the black is remembered as one <s>aṅgula</s>.
Some cause purgation merely by taste; some cause it by smell.
Some cause purgation by touch, and others by sight. Thus <s>Śivā</s> purges in four ways.
Those people who enter the shade of a <s>Cetakī</s> tree,
together with animals, birds, deer, and the like, are purged at that very moment.

children.text: cetakī tu dhṛtā haste yāvattiṣṭhati dehinaḥ
children.translated_text: As long as <s>Cetakī</s> is held in the hand of an embodied being,
for that long he is purged by urges, through its special potency; there is no doubt about this.
For kings, delicate persons, the emaciated, and those who dislike medicine,
<s>Cetakī</s> is supremely praised; it is beneficial and a pleasant purgative.

children.text: saptānām api jātīnāṃ pradhānā vijayā smṛtā
children.translated_text: Among all seven varieties, <s>Vijayā</s> is remembered as the foremost.
It is easy to administer, easy to obtain, and recommended in all diseases.
<s>Harītakī</s> has five tastes, being without saltiness, and is especially astringent.
It is dry, hot, digestive-kindling, good for intellect, sweet in post-digestive effect, and rejuvenative.
It benefits the eyes, is light, promotes longevity, nourishes, and sets the downward movement in order.
It destroys dyspnea, cough, <s>prameha</s> (urinary disorder), hemorrhoids, skin disease, swelling, abdominal disease, and worms,
as well as hoarseness, <s>grahaṇī</s> disorder, constipation, and irregular fever,
abdominal lumps, distension, thirst, vomiting, hiccup, itching, and heart disease,
jaundice, colic, obstructive abdominal distension, disease of the spleen, and likewise of the liver,

children.text: aśmarīṃ mūtrakṛcchraṃ ca mūtrāghātaṃ ca nāśayet ||
children.translated_text: urinary stone, dysuria, and urinary retention.
Because it is sweet, bitter, and astringent, it removes <s>pitta</s>; and it removes <s>kapha</s>,
because it is pungent, bitter, and astringent. Because it is sour, auspicious <s>Śivā</s> removes <s>vāta</s>.
But, from pungency and sourness, would it not produce <s>pitta</s>; and would it not produce <s>vāta</s>? How then is <s>Śivā</s> auspicious?
The fact that it removes the <s>doṣas</s> through special potency is established; that is what is being explained.
It is now set out with reasons for the understanding of students, not created as something unprecedented.
A difference of action, despite equality of qualities, is observed because of difference in the substrate.
Therefore one should not think, 'It is not so,' as in the case of <s>dhātrī</s> and <s>lakuca</s>.
In the flesh of <s>Pathyā</s> the taste is sweet; in the sinews it is sour.

children.text: vṛnte tiktas tvaci kaṭur asthisthas tuvaro rasaḥ
children.translated_text: In the stalk it is bitter, in the skin pungent, and in the stone the taste is astringent.

children.text: snigdhā ghanā vṛttā gurvī kṣiptā ca yāmbhasi
children.translated_text: That fruit which is unctuous, solid, round, heavy, and, when thrown into water,
sinks, is praised and is said to bestow exceedingly good qualities.
When a fruit of <s>harītakī</s> possesses the qualities beginning with freshness and, in one specimen,
has the weight of two <s>karṣas</s>, that combination is called the best.
Chewed, it increases digestive fire; ground, it cleanses the wastes.

children.text: svinnā saṃgrāhiṇī pathyā bhṛṣṭā proktā tridoṣanut ||
children.translated_text: Boiled, <s>Pathyā</s> is constipating; roasted, it is said to remove the three <s>doṣas</s>.
Taken with food, <s>harītakī</s> opens the intellect, strength, and senses, and uproots <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, and <s>anila</s> (vāta),
and loosens urine, feces, and other wastes.
Administered after a meal, <s>harītakī</s> quickly removes
the disorders caused by food and drink and arising from <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>.

children.text: lavaṇena kaphaṃ hanti pittaṃ hanti saśarkarā
children.translated_text: With salt it destroys <s>kapha</s>; with sugar it destroys <s>pitta</s>.
With ghee it destroys diseases born of <s>vāta</s>; combined with jaggery it destroys all diseases.
In the seasons beginning with the rains, <s>Abhayā</s> should be taken, in order, with rock salt, sugar, dry ginger, <s>kaṇā</s> (long pepper), honey, and jaggery,
by one who seeks the qualities of a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative).

children.text: adhvātikhinno balavarjitaś ca rūkṣaḥ kṛśo laṅghanakarśitaśca
children.translated_text: One who is extremely tired from travel, devoid of strength, dry, emaciated, and wasted by fasting,

children.text: pittādhiko garbhavatī ca nārī vimuktaraktastvabhayāṃ na khādet ||
children.translated_text: and one with excess <s>pitta</s>, a pregnant woman, or one from whom blood has been released should not eat <s>Abhayā</s>.
<s>Vibhītaka</s> is of three genders; it is also called <s>Akṣa</s> and <s>Karṣaphala</s>.
It is also <s>Kalidruma</s>, <s>Bhūtavāsa</s>, and <s>Kaliyugālaya</s>.
<s>Vibhītaka</s> is sweet in post-digestive effect, astringent, and removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
It is hot in potency, cool to the touch, purgative, and destroys cough.
It is dry, beneficial for the eyes and hair, and destroys worms and hoarseness.
The kernel of <s>vibhītaka</s> removes thirst, vomiting, kapha, and vāta, and is light;
it is astringent and intoxicating; likewise the kernel of <s>dhātrī</s> has those same qualities.
<s>Āmalaka</s> is said in the three genders; it is also called <s>dhātrī</s>, <s>tiṣyaphala</s>, and <s>amṛtā</s>.
The fruit of <s>dhātrī</s> is equal to <s>harītakī</s>, but in particular
it removes raktapitta and prameha, and is an excellent virilifier and rasāyana.
Because of its sourness it destroys vāta; because of its sweetness and coolness it destroys pitta.
Because of its dryness and astringency it destroys kapha; thus the fruit of <s>dhātrī</s> conquers the three doṣas.

children.text: yasya yasya phalasyeha vīryaṃ bhavati yādṛśam
children.translated_text: Whatever potency any particular fruit has here,
the kernel too should be described according to that very potency.
With equal fruits of <s>pathyā</s>, <s>vibhīta</s>, and <s>dhātrī</s>, there is <s>triphala</s>;

children.text: phalatrikaṃ ca triphalā sā varā ca prakīrtitā ||
children.translated_text: the triad of fruits is <s>triphala</s>, and it is also renowned as <s>varā</s>.
<s>Triphala</s> removes kapha and pitta, cures prameha and skin disease, and is laxative;
it benefits the eyes, kindles digestion, improves appetite, and destroys irregular fever.

children.text: śuṇṭhī viśvā ca viśvaṃ ca nāgaraṃ viśvabheṣajam
children.translated_text: <s>Śuṇṭhī</s> is <s>viśvā</s>, <s>viśva</s>, <s>nāgara</s>, and <s>viśvabheṣaja</s>;
it is also <s>ūṣaṇa</s>, <s>kaṭubhadra</s>, <s>śṛṅgavera</s>, and <s>mahauṣadha</s>.
<s>Śuṇṭhī</s> is appetizing, removes āma and vāta, digests, and is pungent and light;
it is unctuous, hot, sweet after digestion, and removes kapha, vāta, and obstruction.
It is virilifying and good for the voice; it destroys vomiting, dyspnea, colic, cough, and heart disease,
as well as elephantiasis, swelling, piles, abdominal distension, abdominal disease, and vāta disorders.
Because, being rich in fiery qualities, it dries up the watery element,

children.text: saṃgṛhṇāti malaṃ tattu grāhi śuṇṭhyādayo yathā ||
children.translated_text: it consolidates the feces; that is called <s>grāhī</s>, as in the case of dry ginger and the like.

children.text: vibandhabhedinī yā tu sā kathaṃ grāhiṇī bhavet
children.translated_text: But how can something that breaks obstruction be <s>grāhī</s>?
Because its power lies in breaking obstruction, not in causing the stool to be expelled.
Fresh ginger is <s>ārdraka</s>, <s>śṛṅgavera</s>, <s>kaṭubhadra</s>, and also <s>ārdrikā</s>.

children.text: ārdrikā bhedinī gurvī tīkṣṇoṣṇā dīpanī matā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ārdrikā</s> is considered breaking, heavy, sharp, hot, and kindling to digestion.
It is pungent, sweet after digestion, dry, and removes vāta and kapha.
All the qualities that were stated for <s>śuṇṭhī</s> are also present in fresh ginger.
At the beginning of a meal, eating fresh ginger with salt is always wholesome;
it kindles the digestive fire, is appetizing, and cleanses the tongue and throat.
In skin disease, in the obscure disease called <s>ṣāṇḍva</s>, in dysuria, in raktapitta, in wounds, and in fever,
and in burning, in the hot season, and in autumn, fresh ginger is not at all commended.

children.text: pippalī māgadhī kṛṣṇā vaidehī capalā kaṇā
children.translated_text: <s>Pippalī</s> is <s>māgadhī</s>, <s>kṛṣṇā</s>, <s>vaidehī</s>, <s>capalā</s>, and <s>kaṇā</s>;
it is <s>upakulyā</s>, <s>uṣaṇā</s>, <s>śauṇḍī</s>, <s>kolā</s>, and <s>tīkṣṇataṇḍulā</s>.
<s>Pippalī</s> kindles digestion, is virilifying, sweet after digestion, and rejuvenating.
It is not very hot, is pungent and unctuous, removes vāta and kapha, and is light.
<s>Pippalī</s> is purgative and destroys dyspnea, cough, abdominal disorders, and fever,
as well as skin disease, prameha, abdominal tumors, piles, spleen disease, colic, āma, and vāta disorders.

children.text: ārdrā kaphapradā snigdhā śītalā madhurā guruḥ
children.translated_text: When fresh it increases kapha, and is unctuous, cool, sweet, and heavy;
then it pacifies pitta, but when dried it aggravates pitta.
<s>Pippalī</s> combined with honey destroys fat and kapha;
it removes dyspnea, cough, and fever, is virilifying, promotes intellect, and increases digestive fire.
<s>Guḍapippalī</s> is recommended in chronic fever and weakness of digestive fire.
It removes cough, indigestion, lack of appetite, dyspnea, heart disease, anemia, and worm disease.
Here physicians consider the jaggery to be twice the amount of the <s>pippalī</s> powder.
<s>Marica</s> is <s>vellaja</s>, <s>kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>ūṣaṇa</s>, and <s>dharmapattana</s>.
<s>Marica</s> is pungent, sharp, kindling to digestion, and conquers kapha and vāta;
it is hot, produces pitta, is dry, and removes dyspnea, colic, and worms.

children.text: tadārdraṃ madhuraṃ pāke nātyuṣṇaṃ kaṭukaṃ guru
children.translated_text: Its fresh form is sweet after digestion, not excessively hot, pungent, and heavy;
it has a somewhat sharp quality, promotes phlegm secretion, and is not pitta-aggravating.
<s>Viśva</s>, <s>upakulyā</s>, and <s>marica</s>, these three, are called <s>trikaṭu</s>;

children.text: kaṭutrikaṃ tu trikaṭu tryūṣaṇaṃ vyoṣa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: the pungent triad is <s>trikaṭu</s>, and it is called <s>tryūṣaṇa</s> and <s>vyoṣa</s>.
<s>Tryūṣaṇa</s> kindles digestion and destroys dyspnea, cough, and skin diseases,
as well as abdominal tumors, prameha, kapha disorders, corpulence, fat, elephantiasis, and chronic rhinitis.
<s>Pippalīmūla</s> is <s>granthika</s>, <s>uṣaṇa</s>, and <s>caṭakāśira</s>.
<s>Pippalīmūla</s> kindles digestion, is pungent, hot, digestive, and light.
It is dry, produces pitta, breaks obstruction, and removes kapha, vāta, and abdominal disease;
it destroys abdominal distension, spleen disease, abdominal tumors, and removes worms, dyspnea, and wasting.
<s>Tryūṣaṇa</s> together with <s>kaṇāmūla</s> is said to be <s>caturūṣaṇa</s>.
The qualities of <s>caturūṣaṇa</s> are said to be like those of <s>vyoṣa</s>, but stronger.

children.text: bhaveccavyaṃ tu cavikā kathitā sā tathoṣaṇā
children.translated_text: <s>Cavya</s> is <s>cavikā</s>; it too is said to be <s>uṣaṇā</s>.
<s>Cavya</s> has the qualities of <s>kaṇāmūla</s>, and especially removes diseases arising in the rectum.
The fruit of <s>cavikā</s> is called <s>gajapippalī</s> by the learned.
It is also <s>kapivallī</s>, <s>kolavallī</s>, <s>śreyasī</s>, and <s>vaśira</s>.
<s>Gajakṛṣṇā</s> is pungent, removes vāta and kapha, and increases digestive fire.
It is hot and destroys diarrhea, dyspnea, throat diseases, and worms.
<s>Citraka</s> is also named <s>anala</s>, <s>pīṭha</s>, <s>vyāla</s>, and <s>uṣaṇa</s>.

children.text: citrakaḥ kaṭukaḥ pāke vahnikṛt pācano laghuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Citraka</s> is pungent after digestion, produces digestive fire, digests, and is light.
It is dry and hot, and removes grahaṇī disease, skin disease, swelling, piles, worms, and cough.
It removes vāta and kapha, is <s>grāhī</s>, destroys vāta, and removes kapha and pitta.
Together with <s>pippalī</s>, <s>pippalīmūla</s>, <s>cavya</s>, <s>citraka</s>, and <s>nāgara</s>,
the five, each in the measure of a kola, are called <s>pañcakola</s>.
<s>Pañcakola</s> is considered pungent in taste and after digestion, and it creates appetite.
It is sharp, hot, digestive, excellent, kindling, and removes kapha and vāta;
it destroys abdominal tumors, spleen disease, abdominal disease, distension, and colic, and aggravates pitta.
<s>Pañcakola</s> together with <s>marica</s> is called <s>ṣaḍūṣaṇa</s>.
It has the qualities of <s>pañcakola</s>, is dry and hot, and removes poison.
<s>Yavānikā</s> is <s>ugragandhā</s>, <s>brahmadarbhā</s>, and <s>ajamodikā</s>;

children.text: saivoktā dīpyakā dīpyā tathā syād yavasāhvayā
children.translated_text: that same plant is called <s>dīpyakā</s>, <s>dīpyā</s>, and also <s>yavasāhvayā</s>.

children.text: yavānī pācanī rucyā tīkṣṇoṣṇā kaṭukā laghuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Yavānī</s> is digestive, appetizing, sharp and hot, pungent, and light.

children.text: dīpanī ca tathā tiktā pittalā śukraśūlahṛt
children.translated_text: It also kindles digestion, is bitter, increases <s>pitta</s>, and removes seminal pain.
It drives away <s>vāta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, abdominal disease, distention, <s>gulma</s>, splenic disease, and worms.

children.text: ajamodā kharāśvā ca māyūrī dīpyakas tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Ajamodā</s> is also called <s>Kharāśvā</s>, <s>Māyūrī</s>, and <s>Dīpyaka</s>,
and likewise is named <s>Brahmakuśā</s>, <s>Kāravī</s>, and <s>Locamastakā</s>.
<s>Ajamodā</s> is pungent, sharp, kindling, and reduces <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: uṣṇā vidāhinī hṛdyā vṛṣyā balakarī laghuḥ
children.translated_text: It is hot, burning, heart-friendly, aphrodisiac, strength-giving, and light.
It removes eye diseases, worms, vomiting, hiccup, and pain of the bladder.
<s>Pārasīkayavānī</s> is similar to <s>Yavānī</s> in its qualities.
In particular, it is digestive, appetizing, absorbent, intoxicating, and heavy.
<s>Jīraka</s> is <s>Jaraṇa</s>; <s>Ajājī</s> and <s>Kaṇā</s> are <s>Dīrghajīraka</s>.
<s>Kṛṣṇajīra</s> is also <s>Sugandha</s> and <s>Udgāraśodhana</s>.
<s>Kālājājī</s> is <s>Suṣavī</s>, <s>Kālikā</s>, and <s>Upakālikā</s>.
<s>Pṛthvīkā</s> is <s>Kāravī</s>, <s>Pṛthvī</s>, <s>Pṛthukṛṣṇā</s>, and <s>Upakuñcikā</s>,

children.text: upakuñcī ca kuñcī ca bṛhajjīraka ityapi ||
children.translated_text: as well as <s>Upakuñcī</s>, <s>Kuñcī</s>, and also <s>Bṛhajjīraka</s>.
The three kinds of <s>jīraka</s> are dry, pungent, hot, kindling, and light.
They are absorbent, increase <s>pitta</s>, support intelligence, and cleanse the womb.

children.text: jvaraghnaṃ pāvanaṃ vṛṣyaṃ balyaṃ rucyaṃ kaphāpaham
children.translated_text: They destroy fever, purify, act as aphrodisiacs, strengthen, improve appetite, and remove <s>kapha</s>.
They benefit the eyes and remove <s>vāta</s>-related distention, <s>gulma</s>, vomiting, and diarrhea.

children.text: dhānyakaṃ dhānakaṃ dhānyaṃ dhānā dhāneyakaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Dhānyaka</s> is <s>Dhānaka</s>, <s>Dhānya</s>, <s>Dhānā</s>, and <s>Dhāneyaka</s>,
as well as <s>Kunaṭī</s>, <s>Dhenukā</s>, <s>Chattrā</s>, <s>Kustumburu</s>, and <s>Vitunnaka</s>.
<s>Dhānyaka</s> is astringent, unctuous, non-aphrodisiac, diuretic, and light.

children.text: tiktaṃ kaṭūṣṇavīryaṃ ca dīpanaṃ pācanaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: It is bitter, pungent, hot in potency, and is remembered as kindling and digestive.
It destroys fever, is appetizing and absorbent, has a sweet post-digestive effect, and removes the three <s>doṣas</s>.
It drives away thirst, burning, vomiting, dyspnea, cough, emaciation, and worms.
When fresh, it has those qualities, is sweet, and especially destroys <s>pitta</s>.

children.text: śatapuṣpā śatāhvā ca madhurā kāravī misiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Śatapuṣpā</s> is <s>Śatāhvā</s>, <s>Madhurā</s>, <s>Kāravī</s>, and <s>Misi</s>,
also <s>Atilambī</s>, <s>Sitacchattrā</s>, and <s>Saṃhitachattrikā</s>.
<s>Chattrā</s>, <s>Śāleya</s>, <s>Śālīna</s>, <s>Miśreyā</s>, <s>Madhurā</s>, and <s>Misi</s> are further names.
<s>Śatapuṣpā</s> is light, sharp, pitta-producing, kindling, and pungent.
It is hot and removes fever, <s>vāta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, wounds, pain, and eye disease.
<s>Miśreyā</s> is said to have those same qualities and especially removes pain of the womb.
It removes weak digestive fire, is heart-friendly, removes constipation and worms, and reduces <s>śukra</s> (semen).
It is dry, hot, digestive, and removes cough, vomiting, <s>kapha</s>, and <s>vāta</s>.
<s>Methikā</s> is <s>Methinī</s>, <s>Methī</s>, <s>Dīpanī</s>, and <s>Bahupattrikā</s>,
as well as <s>Bodhinī</s>, <s>Bahubījā</s>, and <s>Jyotirgandhaphalā</s>.

children.text: vallarī cakrikā manthā miśrapuṣpā ca kairavī
children.translated_text: It is <s>Vallarī</s>, <s>Cakrikā</s>, <s>Manthā</s>, <s>Miśrapuṣpā</s>, and <s>Kairavī</s>,
also <s>Kuñcikā</s>, <s>Bahuparṇī</s>, <s>Pītabījā</s>, and <s>Municchadā</s>.
<s>Methikā</s> pacifies <s>vāta</s>, destroys <s>kapha</s>, and destroys fever.

children.text: tataḥ svalpaguṇā vanyā vājināṃ sā tu pūjitā ||
children.translated_text: The wild variety has fewer virtues than it, but it is esteemed for horses.
<s>Candrikā</s>, <s>Carmahantrī</s>, and <s>Paśumehanakārikā</s> are names of <s>Candraśūra</s>,
as are <s>Nandinī</s>, <s>Kāravī</s>, <s>Bhadrā</s>, <s>Vāsapuṣpā</s>, and <s>Suvāsarā</s>.
<s>Candraśūra</s> is beneficial for those with hiccup, <s>vāta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, and diarrhea.
It opposes disorders of the blood and <s>vāta</s>, and increases strength and nourishment.
<s>Methikā</s>, <s>Candraśūra</s>, <s>Kālājājī</s>, and <s>Yavānikā</s>,
these four taken together are known as <s>Caturbīja</s>, the four seeds.
The powder of that mixture, eaten daily, destroys diseases of <s>vāta</s>,
indigestion, colic, distention, pain in the side, and pain in the waist.
<s>Sahasravedhi</s>, <s>Jatuka</s>, <s>Vāhlīka</s>, <s>Hiṅgu</s>, and <s>Rāmaṭha</s> are names of asafoetida.
<s>Hiṅgu</s> is hot, digestive, appetizing, sharp, and removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>balāsa</s> (phlegmatic disease).
It kills pain, <s>gulma</s>, abdominal disease, distention, and worms, and increases <s>pitta</s>.
<s>Vacā</s> is <s>Ugragandhā</s>, <s>Ṣaḍgranthā</s>, <s>Golomī</s>, and <s>Śataparvikā</s>,

children.text: kṣudrapattrī ca maṅgalyā jaṭilogrā ca lomaśā ||
children.translated_text: also <s>Kṣudrapattrī</s>, <s>Maṅgalyā</s>, <s>Jaṭilā</s>, <s>Ugrā</s>, and <s>Lomaśā</s>.
<s>Vacā</s> or <s>Ugragandhā</s> is pungent, bitter, hot, emetic, and kindles digestive fire.
It destroys constipation, distention, and pain, and cleanses feces and urine.
It removes epilepsy, <s>kapha</s>, insanity, spirit-affliction, worms, and <s>vāta</s>.
The white Persian <s>vacā</s> is called <s>Haimavatī</s>.
<s>Haimavatī</s> is said to be like it and especially destroys <s>vāta</s>.
<s>Sugandhā</s>, also called <s>Ugragandhā</s>, especially removes <s>kapha</s> and cough.
It gives a good voice, improves appetite, and cleanses the heart, throat, and mouth.
The thick-knotted variety is <s>Sugandhā</s>; it is considered inferior in quality to the preceding one.
<s>Dvīpāntaravacā</s> is somewhat bitter and hot, and kindles digestive fire.
It destroys constipation, distention, and pain, and cleanses feces and urine.
It drives away <s>vāta</s> diseases, epilepsy, insanity, and pain in the body,
and especially removes them; it destroys <s>phiraṅga</s> disease.
<s>Havuṣā</s>, <s>Vapuṣā</s>, <s>Visrā</s>, and <s>Parāśvatthaphalā</s> are recognized names,
as are <s>Matsyagandhā</s>, <s>Plīhahantrī</s>, <s>Viṣaghnī</s>, and <s>Dhvāṅkṣanāśinī</s>.

children.text: havuṣā dīpanī tiktā mṛdūṣṇā tuvarā guruḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Havuṣā</s> is kindling, bitter, mildly hot, astringent, and heavy.
It removes <s>pitta</s>, abdominal disease, <s>vāta</s>, piles, <s>grahaṇī</s> disorder, <s>gulma</s>, and pain.
<s>Parā</s> too is said to have these qualities; the two differ in form.
<s>Viḍaṅga</s>, whether masculine or neuter, is <s>Kṛmighna</s> and <s>Jantunāśana</s>.
It is also called <s>Taṇḍulā</s>, <s>Vella</s>, <s>Amoghā</s>, and <s>Citrataṇḍulā</s>.

children.text: viḍaṅgaṃ kaṭu tīkṣṇoṣṇaṃ rūkṣaṃ vahnikaraṃ laghu
children.translated_text: <s>Viḍaṅga</s> is pungent, sharp, hot, dry, fire-kindling, and light.
It removes pain, distention, abdominal disease, <s>kapha</s>, worms, <s>vāta</s>, and constipation.
<s>Tumburu</s> is <s>Saurabha</s>, <s>Saura</s>, <s>Vanaja</s>, <s>Sānuja</s>, and <s>Andhaka</s>.
<s>Tumburu</s> is renowned as bitter; it is pungent and has a pungent post-digestive effect.

children.text: rūkṣoṣṇaṃ dīpanaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ rucyaṃ laghu vidāhi ca ||
children.translated_text: It is dry, hot, kindling, sharp, appetizing, light, and burning.
It destroys <s>vāta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, disorders of the eye, ear, lip, and head, heaviness, and worms,
as well as skin disease, pain, anorexia, dyspnea, splenic disease, and urinary difficulty.
It is called <s>vaṃśarocanā</s>, <s>vāṃśī</s>, <s>tugākṣīrī</s>, <s>tugā</s>, and <s>śubhā</s>.

children.text: tvakkṣīrī vaṃśajā śubhrā vaṃśakṣīrī ca vaiṇavī ||
children.translated_text: It is also <s>tvakkṣīrī</s>, <s>vaṃśajā</s>, <s>śubhrā</s>, <s>vaṃśakṣīrī</s>, and <s>vaiṇavī</s>.

children.text: vaṃśajā bṛṃhaṇī vṛṣyā balyā svādvī ca śītalā
children.translated_text: <s>Vaṃśajā</s> is nourishing, aphrodisiac, strengthening, sweet, and cooling.
It removes thirst, cough, fever, dyspnea, wasting, <s>pitta</s> disorders, blood disorders, and jaundice;
it removes skin disease, wounds, and pallor; it is astringent and overcomes <s>vāta</s> disorders and dysuria.
<s>Samudraphena</s> is also called <s>phena</s>, <s>ḍiṇḍīra</s>, and <s>abdhikapha</s>.
<s>Samudraphena</s> is beneficial to the eyes, scraping in action, and cooling.
It is astringent, counteracts poison and <s>pitta</s>, removes ear pain and <s>kapha</s>, and is laxative.
These are <s>jīvaka</s> and <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>, the two <s>medā</s>s, the two <s>kākolī</s>s, and <s>ṛddhi</s> with <s>vṛddhi</s>.
This <s>aṣṭavarga</s> (group of eight drugs), consisting of eight substances, was taught by <s>Caraka</s> and others.

children.text: aṣṭavargo himaḥ svādur bṛṃhaṇaḥ śukralo guruḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>aṣṭavarga</s> is cooling, sweet, nourishing, semen-promoting, and heavy.
It promotes the knitting of fractures and increases desire, strength, and bodily vigor.
It removes <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, blood disorders, thirst, burning, fever, urinary disease, and wasting.
<s>Jīvaka</s> and <s>ṛṣabhaka</s> should be known as growing on the peaks of the Himalaya.
Their tubers are like garlic bulbs, pithless, and furnished with small leaves.
<s>Jīvaka</s> is shaped like a tuft; <s>ṛṣabha</s> is like a bull's horn.
<s>Jīvaka</s> is also called <s>madhura</s>, <s>śṛṅga</s>, <s>hrasvāṅga</s>, and <s>kūrcaśīrṣaka</s>.

children.text: ṛṣabho vṛṣabho dhīro viṣāṇī drākṣa ityapi
children.translated_text: <s>Ṛṣabha</s> is also <s>vṛṣabha</s>, <s>dhīra</s>, <s>viṣāṇī</s>, and <s>drākṣa</s>.
<s>Jīvaka</s> and <s>ṛṣabhaka</s> are strengthening, cooling, and productive of semen and <s>kapha</s>.
They are sweet and remove <s>pitta</s>, burning, blood disorders, emaciation, <s>vāta</s>, and wasting.
The tuber called <s>mahāmedā</s> grows in <s>Moraṅga</s> and similar regions.
<s>Mahāmedā</s> is also <s>khanīmedā</s>, so the great sages have said.
The tuber resembles white fresh ginger, is creeper-born, and is very pale.
This should be known as the one called <s>mahāmedā</s>; now the mark of <s>medā</s> is stated.
It has a white tuber, can be cut with the nail, and exudes like adipose tissue.
That should be recognized as <s>medā</s> by people intent on careful inquiry.
<s>Medā</s> is called <s>śalyaparṇī</s>, <s>maṇicchidrā</s>, <s>medā</s>, <s>medobhavā</s>, and <s>adhvarā</s>.
<s>Mahāmedā</s> is called <s>vasucchidrā</s>, <s>tridantī</s>, and <s>devatāmaṇi</s>.
The pair of <s>medā</s> drugs is heavy, sweet, aphrodisiac, and productive of breast milk and <s>kapha</s>.
It is nourishing and cooling, and removes <s>pitta</s>, blood disorders, <s>vāta</s>, and fever.
<s>Kṣīrakākolī</s> grows in the place where <s>mahāmedā</s> arises.

children.text: yatra syāt kṣīrakākolī kākolī atra jāyate
children.translated_text: Wherever <s>kṣīrakākolī</s> is found, <s>kākolī</s> grows there too.
Its tuber resembles <s>pīvarī</s>, has milky sap, and possesses a pleasant fragrance.
That is called <s>kṣīrakākolī</s>; now the sign of <s>kākolī</s> is stated.

children.text: yathā syāt kṣīrakākolī kākolyapi tathā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: As <s>kṣīrakākolī</s> is, so too is <s>kākolī</s>.

children.text: eṣā kiṃcid bhavet kṛṣṇā bhedo 'yam ubhayor api
children.translated_text: This one is somewhat black; this is the distinction between the two.

children.text: kākolī vāyasolī ca vīrā kāyasthikā tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kākolī</s> is also <s>vāyasolī</s>, <s>vīrā</s>, and <s>kāyasthikā</s>.
That white one, <s>kṣīrakākolī</s>, is also <s>vayaḥsthā</s> and <s>kṣīravallikā</s>.
It is called <s>kṣīriṇī</s>, <s>dhīrā</s>, <s>kṣīraśuklā</s>, and <s>payasvinī</s>.
The pair of <s>kākolī</s> drugs is cooling, semen-promoting, sweet, and heavy.
It is nourishing and removes <s>vāta</s>, burning, blood disorders, <s>pitta</s>, wasting, and fever.
<s>Ṛddhi</s> and <s>vṛddhi</s> are two tubers found on the mountain in <s>Kośala</s>.
The tuber is furnished with white hairs, creeper-born, and porous.

children.text: sa eva ṛddhirvṛddhiśca bhedam apyetayor bruve
children.translated_text: That same plant is <s>ṛddhi</s> and <s>vṛddhi</s>; I shall also state the difference between them.
<s>Ṛddhi</s> resembles a cotton boll, and its fruit turns to the left.
<s>Vṛddhi</s>, however, is said by the great sages to have fruit turning to the right.

children.text: ṛddhir yogyaṃ siddhilakṣmyau vṛddher apyāhvayā ime ||
children.translated_text: <s>Yogyā</s>, <s>siddhi</s>, and <s>lakṣmī</s> are names of <s>ṛddhi</s>, and these are also appellations of <s>vṛddhi</s>.

children.text: ṛddhir balyā tridoṣaghnī śukralā madhurā guruḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Ṛddhi</s> is strengthening, destroys the three <s>doṣa</s>s, promotes semen, and is sweet and heavy.
It produces vitality and prosperity, and destroys fainting and <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorder).

children.text: vṛddhir garbhapradā śītā bṛṃhaṇī madhurā smṛtā
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛddhi</s> is said to promote conception, and is cooling, nourishing, and sweet.
It is aphrodisiac, pacifies <s>pitta</s> and blood disorders, and removes injury, cough, and wasting.
Since this <s>aṣṭavarga</s> is very difficult to obtain even for kings,
therefore the physician should take a substitute for it, one having its qualities.
A substitute is similar to the principal drug.
When the pairs of <s>medā</s>, <s>jīvaka</s>, <s>kākolī</s>, and <s>ṛddhi</s> are absent,
one should add, in order, <s>varī</s>, <s>vidārī</s>, <s>aśvagandhā</s>, and <s>vārāhī</s>.
In place of <s>medā</s> and <s>mahāmedā</s>, use the root of <s>śatāvarī</s>.
In place of <s>jīvaka</s> and <s>ṛṣabhaka</s>, use the root of <s>vidārī</s>.
In place of <s>kākolī</s> and <s>kṣīrakākolī</s>, use the root of <s>aśvagandhā</s>.
In place of <s>ṛddhi</s> and <s>vṛddhi</s>, one should add the tuber of <s>vārāhī</s>, equal to them in qualities.
<s>Yaṣṭīmadhu</s>, <s>yaṣṭīmadhuka</s>, and <s>klītaka</s> are names for it.
Another name is <s>klītanaka</s>; in water it is called <s>madhūlikā</s>.

children.text: yaṣṭī himā guruḥ svādvī cakṣuṣyā balavarṇakṛt
children.translated_text: <s>Yaṣṭī</s> is cooling, heavy, sweet, beneficial to the eyes, and productive of strength and complexion.
It is very unctuous, semen-promoting, good for the hair, good for the voice, and conquers <s>pitta</s>, wind, and blood disorders.
It removes wounds, swelling, poison, vomiting, thirst, fatigue, and wasting.

children.text: kāmpillaḥ karkaśaś candro raktāṅgo rocano 'pi ca
children.translated_text: <s>Kāmpilla</s> is also <s>karkaśa</s>, <s>candra</s>, <s>raktāṅga</s>, and <s>rocana</s>.
<s>Kāmpilla</s> destroys <s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, blood disorders, worms, abdominal masses, abdominal disease, and wounds.
It is purgative, pungent, and hot, and removes urinary disease, abdominal distension, poison, and calculi.
<s>Āragvadha</s> is <s>rājavṛkṣa</s>, <s>śamyāka</s>, and <s>caturaṅgula</s>.
It is <s>ārevata</s>, <s>vyādhighāta</s>, <s>kṛtamāla</s>, and <s>suvarṇaka</s>.
It is <s>karṇikāra</s>, <s>dīrghaphala</s>, <s>svarṇāṅga</s>, and <s>svarṇabhūṣaṇa</s>.
<s>Āragvadha</s> is heavy, sweet, cooling, and the best evacuative.
It removes fever, heart disease, <s>pitta</s>, blood disorders, <s>vāta</s>, <s>udāvarta</s> (upward-moving vāta), and pain.
Its fruit is evacuative, appetizing, and removes skin disease, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>.

children.text: jvare tu satataṃ pathyaṃ koṣṭhaśuddhikaraṃ param ||
children.translated_text: In fever it is always wholesome; it is supreme for cleansing the bowels.

children.text: kaṭvī tu kaṭukā tiktā kṛṣṇabhedā kaṭaṃbharā
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṭvī</s> is <s>kaṭukā</s>, <s>tiktā</s>, the black variety <s>kṛṣṇabhedā</s>, and <s>kaṭaṃbharā</s>.
It is <s>aśokā</s>, <s>matsyaśakalā</s>, <s>cakrāṅgī</s>, and <s>śakulādanī</s>.
It is <s>matsyapittā</s>, <s>kāṇḍaruhā</s>, <s>rohiṇī</s>, and <s>kaṭurohiṇī</s>.

children.text: kaṭvī tu kaṭukā pāke tiktā rūkṣā himā laghuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṭvī</s> is pungent in post-digestive effect, bitter, dry, cooling, and light.
It is purgative, kindles digestion, benefits the heart, and removes fever caused by kapha and pitta.
It drives away prameha, dyspnea, cough, disorders of the blood, burning, skin disease, and worms.
<s>Kirātatikta</s> is <s>Kairāta</s>, <s>Kaṭutikta</s>, and <s>Kirātaka</s>.
It is also <s>Kāṇḍatikta</s>, <s>Anāryatikta</s>, <s>Bhūnimba</s>, and <s>Rāmasenaka</s>.
Another <s>Kirātaka</s> is <s>Naipāla</s>; that half-bitter one ends fever.

children.text: kirātaḥ sārako rūkṣaḥ śītalas tiktako laghuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kirāta</s> is laxative, dry, cooling, bitter, and light.
It removes saṃnipāta fever, dyspnea, kapha, pitta, blood disorders, and burning.
It drives away cough, swelling, thirst, skin disease, fever, wounds, and worms.
The seed of <s>Kuṭaja</s> is said to be <s>Yava</s> and also <s>Indrayava</s>.

children.text: kaliṅgaṃ cāpi kāliṅgaṃ tathā bhadrayavā api ||
children.translated_text: It is also <s>Kaliṅga</s> and <s>Kāliṅga</s>, and likewise <s>Bhadrayava</s>.
In some places, the very name of <s>Indra</s> may designate it.
Its fruits are <s>Indrayava</s>, and likewise <s>Bhadrayava</s>.
<s>Indrayava</s> pacifies the three doṣas; it is absorbent, pungent, and cooling.
It removes fever, diarrhea, bleeding piles, vomiting, erysipelas, and skin disease.
It kindles digestion and conquers rectal growths, blood disorders, vātarakta, and colic due to phlegm.
<s>Madana</s> is <s>Chardana</s>, <s>Piṇḍa</s>, <s>Naṭa</s>, and likewise <s>Piṇḍītaka</s>.
It is <s>Karahāṭa</s>, <s>Maruvaka</s>, <s>Śalyaka</s>, and <s>Viṣapuṣpaka</s>.
<s>Madana</s> is sweet and bitter, hot in potency, scraping, and light.
It causes vomiting, removes abscesses, and ends catarrh and wounds.
It is dry and removes skin disease, kapha, abdominal distension, swelling, tumors, and wounds.

children.text: rāsnā yuktarasā rasyā suvahā rasanā rasā
children.translated_text: <s>Rāsnā</s> is <s>Yuktarasā</s>, <s>Rasyā</s>, <s>Suvahā</s>, <s>Rasanā</s>, and <s>Rasā</s>.

children.text: elāparṇī ca surasā sugandhā śreyasī tathā ||
children.translated_text: It is also <s>Elāparṇī</s>, <s>Surasā</s>, <s>Sugandhā</s>, and <s>Śreyasī</s>.
<s>Rāsnā</s>, also <s>Apācinī</s>, is bitter, heavy, hot, and conquers kapha and vāta.
It removes swelling, dyspnea, vāta, blood disorders, vāta-related colic, and abdominal disease.
It removes cough, fever, poison, chills, vāta disorders, and sidhma skin eruption.
<s>Nākulī</s> is <s>Surasā</s>, <s>Nāgasugandhā</s>, and <s>Gandhanākulī</s>.
It is <s>Nakuleṣṭā</s>, <s>Bhujaṃgākṣī</s>, <s>Sarpāṅgī</s>, and <s>Viṣanāśinī</s>.
<s>Nākulī</s> is astringent, bitter, pungent, and hot; it destroys
the poisons of snakes, spiders, scorpions, and mice, as well as fever, worms, and wounds.
<s>Mācikā</s> is <s>Prasthikā</s>, <s>Ambaṣṭhā</s>, and also <s>Ambālikā</s> and <s>Ambikā</s>.
It is <s>Mayūravidalā</s>, <s>Keśī</s>, <s>Sahasrā</s>, and <s>Bālamūlikā</s>.

children.text: mācikāmlā rase pāke kaṣāyā śītalā laghuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Mācikā</s> is sour in taste and post-digestive effect, astringent, cooling, and light.
It removes ripe diarrhea, pitta, blood disorders, kapha, and diseases of the throat.
<s>Tejasvinī</s> is <s>Tejavatī</s>, <s>Tejohvā</s>, and also <s>Tejanī</s>.
<s>Tejasvinī</s> removes kapha, dyspnea, cough, diseases of the mouth, and vāta.
It is digestive, hot, pungent, and bitter, and it stimulates taste and digestive fire.
<s>Jyotiṣmatī</s> is <s>Kaṭabhī</s>, <s>Jyotiṣkā</s>, and <s>Kaṅgunī</s>.
<s>Pārāvatapadī</s>, <s>Piṇyā</s>, <s>Latā</s>, and <s>Kakundanī</s> are also stated as its names.
<s>Jyotiṣmatī</s> is pungent, bitter, fluid-moving, and conquers kapha and vāta.
It is very hot, emetic, sharp, and bestows digestive fire, intellect, and memory.
<s>Kuṣṭha</s> is <s>Rogāhvaya</s>, <s>Vāpya</s>, <s>Pāribhavya</s>, and also <s>Utpala</s>.

children.text: kuṣṭhamuṣṇaṃ kaṭu svādu śukralaṃ tiktakaṃ laghu
children.translated_text: <s>Kuṣṭha</s> is hot, pungent, sweet, semen-promoting, bitter, and light.
It destroys vātarakta, erysipelas, cough, skin disease, vāta, and kapha.

children.text: uktaṃ puṣkaramūlaṃ tu pauṣkaraṃ puṣkaraṃ ca tat
children.translated_text: <s>Puṣkaramūla</s> is said to be <s>Pauṣkara</s> and <s>Puṣkara</s>.
It is also <s>Padmapattra</s> and <s>Kāśmīra</s>; they call this a variety of <s>Kuṣṭha</s>.
<s>Pauṣkara</s> is pungent, bitter, and hot, and it destroys vāta, kapha, and fever.
It removes swelling, loss of appetite, and dyspnea; especially, it removes pain in the side.
<s>Kaṭuparṇī</s> is <s>Haimavatī</s>, <s>Hemakṣīrī</s>, and <s>Himāvatī</s>.
It is also <s>Hemāhvā</s> and <s>Pītadugdhā</s>; its root is called <s>Coka</s>.
<s>Hemāhvā</s> is purgative, bitter, breaking, and causes nausea.
It removes worms, itching, poison, abdominal distension, kapha, pitta, blood disorders, and skin disease.
<s>Śṛṅgī</s> is <s>Karkaṭaśṛṅgī</s> and <s>Kulīraviṣāṇikā</s>.

children.text: ajaśṛṅgī tu cakrā ca karkaṭākhyā ca kīrtitā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ajaśṛṅgī</s> is also proclaimed as <s>Cakrā</s> and <s>Karkaṭākhyā</s>.
<s>Śṛṅgī</s> is astringent, bitter, and hot; it removes kapha, vāta, wasting disease, and fever.
It removes dyspnea, upward-moving vāta, thirst, cough, hiccup, loss of appetite, and vomiting.

children.text: kaṭphalaḥ somavalkaś ca kaiṭaryaḥ kumbhikāpi ca
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṭphala</s> is <s>Somavalka</s>, <s>Kaiṭarya</s>, and also <s>Kumbhikā</s>.
It is <s>Śrīparṇikā</s>, <s>Kumudikā</s>, <s>Bhadrā</s>, and <s>Bhadravatī</s>.
<s>Kaṭphala</s> is astringent, bitter, and pungent; it destroys vāta, kapha, and fever.
It removes dyspnea, prameha, piles, cough, throat diseases, and loss of appetite.
<s>Bhārgī</s> is <s>Bhṛgubhavā</s>, <s>Padmā</s>, <s>Phañjī</s>, and <s>Brāhmaṇayaṣṭikā</s>.
It is also <s>Brāhmaṇī</s>, <s>Aṅgāravallī</s>, <s>Kharaśāka</s>, and <s>Hañjikā</s>.

children.text: bhārgī rūkṣā kaṭustiktā rucyoṣṇā pācanī laghuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Bhārgī</s> is dry, pungent, bitter, appetizing, hot, digestive, and light.
It kindles digestion, is astringent, and certainly destroys gulma tumors and blood disorders.
It destroys swelling, cough, kapha, dyspnea, coryza, fever, and vāta.
<s>Pāṣāṇabhedaka</s> is <s>Aśmaghna</s>, <s>Giribhid</s>, and <s>Bhinnayojinī</s>.
<s>Aśmabheda</s> is cooling, bitter, astringent, and cleansing to the bladder.
It is breaking and purgative; it destroys doṣas, piles, gulma tumors, dysuria, stone disease, and heart pain.
It also destroys diseases of the womb, prameha, spleen disease, colic, and wounds.

children.text: dhātakī dhātupuṣpī ca tāmrapuṣpī ca kuñjarā
children.translated_text: <s>Dhātakī</s> is <s>Dhātupuṣpī</s>, <s>Tāmrapuṣpī</s>, and <s>Kuñjarā</s>.

children.text: subhikṣā bahupuṣpī ca vahnijvālā ca sā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: It is remembered as <s>Subhikṣā</s>, <s>Bahupuṣpī</s>, and <s>Vahnijvālā</s>.
<s>Dhātakī</s> is pungent, cooling, mildly laxative, astringent, and light.
It conquers thirst, diarrhea, pitta, blood disorders, poison, worms, and erysipelas.
<s>Mañjiṣṭhā</s> is <s>Vikasā</s>, <s>Jiṅgī</s>, <s>Samaṅgā</s>, and <s>Kālameṣikā</s>.
It is <s>Maṇḍūkaparṇī</s>, <s>Bhaṇḍīrī</s>, <s>Bhaṇḍī</s>, and also <s>Yojanavallī</s>.
It is <s>Rasāyanī</s>, <s>Aruṇā</s>, <s>Kālā</s>, <s>Raktāṅgī</s>, and <s>Raktayaṣṭikā</s>.
It is <s>Bhaṇḍītakī</s>, <s>Gambhīrī</s>, <s>Mañjūṣā</s>, and <s>Vastrarañjinī</s>.
<s>Mañjiṣṭhā</s> is sweet, bitter, and astringent, and it improves voice and complexion.
It is heavy and hot; it removes poison, kapha, swelling, and diseases of the womb, eyes, and ears.
It removes bloody diarrhea, skin disease, blood disorders, erysipelas, wounds, and urinary disease.
<s>Kusumbha</s> is also <s>Vahniśikha</s> and <s>Vastrarañjaka</s>.
<s>Kusumbha</s> promotes vāta and removes dysuria, raktapitta, and kapha.
<s>Lākṣā</s> is <s>Palaṃkaṣā</s>, <s>Alakta</s>, <s>Yāva</s>, and tree-born resin.

children.text: lākṣā varṇyā himā balyā snigdhā ca tuvarā laghuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lākṣā</s> improves complexion, is cooling and strengthening, unctuous, astringent, and light.
It is not hot and removes kapha, pitta, blood disorders, hiccup, cough, and fever.
It removes wounds, lesions of the chest, erysipelas, worms, and skin disease.
<s>Alaktaka</s> is similar in qualities, and especially destroys facial discoloration.
<s>Haridrā</s> is <s>Kāñcanī</s>, <s>Pītā</s>, <s>Niśākhyā</s>, and <s>Varavarṇinī</s>.
It is <s>Kṛmighnī</s>, <s>Haladī</s>, beloved of women, and <s>Haṭṭavilāsinī</s>.
<s>Haridrā</s> is pungent and bitter, dry and hot, and removes kapha and pitta.
It improves complexion and removes skin disorders, prameha, blood disorders, swelling, anemia, and wounds.
<s>Āmragandhā</s>, a variety of <s>Dārvī</s>, is also <s>Surabhīdāru</s> and <s>Dāru</s>.
It is <s>Karpūrā</s>, <s>Padmapattrā</s>, <s>Surīmat</s>, and <s>Suratārakā</s>.

children.text: āmragandhir haridrā yā sā śītā vātalā matā
children.translated_text: The turmeric called <s>Āmragandhā</s> is considered cooling and vāta-producing.
It removes pitta, is sweet and bitter, and destroys every kind of itching.
The rhizome of wild turmeric removes skin disease, vāta, and blood disorders.

children.text: dārvī dāruharidrā ca parjanyā parjanīti ca
children.translated_text: <s>Dārvī</s> is <s>Dāruharidrā</s>, <s>Parjanyā</s>, and also <s>Parjanī</s>.
It is also <s>Kaṭaṃkaṭerī</s>, <s>Pītā</s>, and <s>Pacampacā</s>.
The same is called <s>Kālīyaka</s>, and likewise <s>Kāleyaka</s>.
It is <s>Pītadru</s>, <s>Haridra</s>, <s>Pītadāru</s>, and <s>Pītaka</s>.
<s>Dārvī</s> has the qualities of <s>Niśā</s>, but it removes diseases of the eyes, ears, and mouth.

children.text: dārvīkvāthasamaṃ kṣīraṃ pādaṃ paktvā yadā ghanam
children.translated_text: When milk equal to a decoction of <s>Dārvī</s> is boiled down to a quarter and becomes thick,
then that is called <s>Rasāñjana</s>; it is supremely beneficial for the eyes.
<s>Rasāñjana</s> is <s>Tārkṣyaśaila</s>, <s>Rasagarbha</s>, and <s>Tārkṣyaja</s>.
<s>Rasāñjana</s> is pungent and removes phlegm, poison, and eye disorders.
It is hot, rejuvenating, bitter, cutting, and removes disorders of wounds.
<s>Avalguja</s> is <s>Vākucī</s>, <s>Somarājī</s>, and <s>Suparṇikā</s>.
It is <s>Śaśilekhā</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇaphalā</s>, <s>Somā</s>, and <s>Pūtiphalā</s>.
It is known as <s>Somavallī</s>, <s>Kālameṣī</s>, and <s>Kuṣṭhaghnī</s>.
<s>Vākucī</s> is sweet and bitter, pungent in post-digestive effect, and rejuvenating.
It removes obstruction, is cooling, appetizing, laxative, and removes phlegm, blood disorders, and pitta.
It is dry and good for the heart, and removes dyspnea, skin disease, prameha, fever, and worms.
Its fruit increases pitta, removes skin disease, kapha, and vāta, and is pungent.
It is good for the hair and skin, and removes worms, dyspnea, cough, swelling, āma, and anemia.
<s>Cakramarda</s> is <s>Prapunnāṭī</s>, <s>Dadrughna</s>, and <s>Meṣalocana</s>.
It is <s>Padmāṭa</s>, <s>Eḍagaja</s>, <s>Cakrī</s>, and also <s>Puṃnāṭa</s>.
<s>Cakramarda</s> is light, sweet, and dry, and removes pitta and vāta.
It is good for the heart, cooling, and removes kapha, dyspnea, skin disease, ringworm, and worms.
Its fruit is hot and destroys skin disease, itching, ringworm, poison, and vāta.
It is remembered as pungent and as destroying gulma tumors, cough, worms, and dyspnea.

children.text: viṣā tv ativiṣā viśvā śṛṅgī prativiṣāruṇā
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣā</s> is <s>Ativiṣā</s>, <s>Viśvā</s>, <s>Śṛṅgī</s>, <s>Prativiṣā</s>, and <s>Aruṇā</s>.
It is <s>Śuklakandā</s>, <s>Upaviṣā</s>, <s>Bhaṅgurā</s>, and <s>Ghuṇavallabhā</s>.

children.text: viṣā soṣṇā kaṭustiktā pācanī dīpanī haret
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣā</s> is slightly hot, pungent, bitter, digestive, and kindles digestion; it removes
kapha, pitta, diarrhea, āma, poison, cough, vomiting, and worms.
<s>Lodhra</s> is <s>Tilva</s>, <s>Tirīṭa</s>, <s>Śāvara</s>, and also <s>Gālava</s>.
The second variety is <s>Paṭṭikālodhra</s>, <s>Kramuka</s>, and <s>Sthūlavalkala</s>.
It is <s>Jīrṇapattra</s>, <s>Bṛhatpattra</s>, <s>Paṭṭī</s>, and <s>Lākṣāprasādana</s>.
<s>Lodhra</s> is absorbent, light, cooling, beneficial for the eyes, and removes kapha and pitta.
It is astringent and removes raktapitta, blood disorders, fever, diarrhea, and swelling.
<s>Laśuna</s> is <s>Rasona</s>, <s>Ugragandha</s>, and <s>Mahauṣadha</s>.
It is <s>Ariṣṭa</s>, <s>Mlecchakanda</s>, <s>Yavaneṣṭa</s>, and <s>Rasonaka</s>.
When <s>Vainateya</s> carried away amṛta from the best of the gods,
then a drop fell from it, and that became <s>Rasona</s> on earth.

children.text: pañcabhiś ca rasair yukto rasenāmlena varjitaḥ
children.translated_text: It is endowed with five tastes and lacks the sour taste.
Therefore it is called <s>Rasona</s> by those who know the qualities of substances.
In the roots it is pungent, and in the leaves it is found as bitter.

children.text: nāle kaṣāya uddiṣṭo nālāgre lavaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: In the stalk it is said to be astringent, and at the tip of the stalk it is remembered as salty.

children.text: bīje tu madhuraḥ prokto rasas tadguṇavedibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the seed, however, its taste is said by those who know its qualities to be sweet.

children.text: rasono bṛṃhaṇo vṛṣyaḥ snigdhoṣṇaḥ pācanaḥ saraḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rasona</s> is nourishing, semen-promoting, unctuous, hot, digestive, and laxative.

children.text: rase pāke ca kaṭukastīkṣṇo madhurako mataḥ ||
children.translated_text: In taste and post-digestive effect it is pungent, sharp, and considered somewhat sweet.
It heals fractures, is good for the throat, heavy, and increases pitta and blood.
It promotes strength and complexion, benefits intelligence, is good for the eyes, and is rejuvenating.
It destroys heart disease, chronic fever, abdominal colic, constipation, gulma tumors, loss of appetite, cough, and swelling,
as well as severe piles, skin disease, sluggish digestion, worms, vāta, dyspnea, and kapha.

children.text: madyaṃ māṃsaṃ tathāmlaṃ ca hitaṃ laśunasevinām
children.translated_text: Wine, meat, and sour foods are beneficial for those who use garlic.
Exercise, sun heat, anger, excessive water, milk, and jaggery
should always be avoided by a man who is eating <s>Rasona</s>.
<s>Palāṇḍu</s> is <s>Yavaneṣṭa</s>, foul-smelling, and defiling to the mouth.
<s>Palāṇḍu</s> should be known by the wise as similar in qualities to <s>Rasona</s>.
It is sweet in taste and post-digestive effect, not hot, kapha-producing, and not very pitta-producing.
It removes only vāta, promotes strength and virility, and is heavy.
<s>Bhallātaka</s> is stated in the three genders; it is <s>Aruṣka</s>, <s>Aruṣkara</s>, and <s>Agnika</s>.
It is also <s>Agnimukhī</s>, <s>Bhallī</s>, <s>Vīravṛkṣa</s>, and <s>Śophakṛt</s>.
The ripe fruit of <s>Bhallātaka</s> is sweet in post-digestive effect and taste, and light.

children.text: kaṣāyaṃ pācanaṃ snigdhaṃ tīkṣṇoṣṇaṃ chedi bhedanam ||
children.translated_text: It is astringent, digestive, unctuous, sharp, hot, cutting, and breaking.
It benefits intelligence, kindles digestive fire, and removes kapha, vāta, wounds, and abdominal disease.
It removes skin disease, piles, grahaṇī disorder, gulma tumors, swelling, distension, fever, and worms.
Its kernel is sweet, semen-promoting, nourishing, and removes vāta and pitta.
The stalk of <s>Aruṣkara</s> is sweet, pitta-removing, good for the hair, and kindles digestive fire.
<s>Bhallātaka</s> is astringent, hot, semen-promoting, sweet, and light.
It destroys diseases of vāta and kapha, abdominal disease, distension, skin disease, piles, and grahaṇī disorder,
and it destroys gulma tumors, fever, vitiligo, weak digestive fire, worms, and wounds.
<s>Bhaṅgā</s> is <s>Gañjā</s>, <s>Mātulānī</s>, <s>Mādinī</s>, <s>Vijayā</s>, and <s>Jayā</s>.

children.text: bhaṅgā kaphaharī tiktā grāhiṇī pācanī laghuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Bhaṅgā</s> removes kapha; it is bitter, absorbent, digestive, and light.
It is sharp and hot, causes pitta, induces stupefaction and sluggish speech, and increases digestive fire.
A variety of sesame is remembered as <s>Khasatila</s> and also as <s>Khākhasa</s>.
The husk produced from the <s>Khākhasa</s> fruit is cooling and light.

children.text: grāhi tiktaṃ kaṣāyaṃ ca vātakṛt kaphakāsahṛt ||
children.translated_text: It is absorbent, bitter, and astringent; it produces vāta and removes kapha and cough.
It dries up the bodily tissues, is dry, causes intoxication, and promotes speech.
It repeatedly causes bewilderment, is appetizing, and through use destroys virility.
The latex of the <s>Khasa</s> fruit is called <s>Āphūka</s> and <s>Ahiphenaka</s>.
<s>Āphūka</s> is drying, absorbent, phlegm-destroying, and productive of vāta and pitta.
It is also said to be generally like the husk produced from the <s>Khasa</s> fruit.
The seeds of <s>Khasa</s> are also called <s>Khākhasatila</s>.
The seeds of <s>Khasa</s> are strengthening, aphrodisiac, and very heavy.
They generate kapha and pacify samīraṇa, that is, vāta.
<s>Saindhava</s> is not feminine in gender; it is <s>Śītaśiva</s>, <s>Māṇimantha</s>, and <s>Sindhuja</s>.

children.text: saindhavaṃ lavaṇaṃ svādu dīpanaṃ pācanaṃ laghu
children.translated_text: <s>Saindhava</s> salt is sweet, kindles digestion, digests, and is light.

children.text: snigdhaṃ rucyaṃ himaṃ vṛṣyaṃ sūkṣmaṃ netryaṃ tridoṣahṛt ||
children.translated_text: It is unctuous, appetizing, cooling, aphrodisiac, subtle, beneficial for the eyes, and removes all three doṣas.
The salt from <s>Śākambharī</s> is called <s>Guḍākhya</s> and also <s>Raumaka</s>.

children.text: guḍākhyaṃ laghu vātaghnam atyuṣṇaṃ bhedi pittalam
children.translated_text: <s>Guḍākhya</s> is light, vāta-destroying, very hot, laxative, and productive of pitta.

children.text: tīkṣṇoṣṇaṃ cāpi sūkṣmaṃ cābhiṣyandi kaṭupāki ca ||
children.translated_text: It is also sharp, hot, subtle, channel-clogging, and pungent in post-digestive effect.

children.text: sāmudraṃ yattu lavaṇam akṣībaṃ vaśiraṃ ca tat
children.translated_text: The salt called <s>Sāmudra</s> is <s>Akṣība</s> and <s>Vaśira</s>.
It is <s>Samudraja</s>, <s>Sāgaraja</s>, and that which arises from the salt ocean.

children.text: sāmudraṃ madhuraṃ pāke satiktaṃ madhuraṃ guru
children.translated_text: <s>Sāmudra</s> is sweet in post-digestive effect, slightly bitter, sweet, and heavy.

children.text: nātyuṣṇaṃ dīpanaṃ bhedi sakṣāram avidāhi ca
children.translated_text: It is not excessively hot, kindles digestion, is laxative, alkaline, and non-burning.
It produces kapha, removes vāta, is sharp, not dry, and not very cooling.

children.text: viḍaṃ pākaṃ ca kṛtakaṃ tathā drāviḍamāsuram
children.translated_text: <s>Viḍa</s> is <s>Pāka</s>, <s>Kṛtaka</s>, <s>Drāviḍa</s>, and <s>Āsura</s>.
<s>Viḍa</s> is alkaline and regulates kapha upward and vāta downward.
The meaning is that it moves kapha upward and vāta downward.

children.text: dīpanaṃ laghu tīkṣṇoṣṇaṃ rūkṣaṃ rucyaṃ vyavāyi ca
children.translated_text: It kindles digestion, is light, sharp, hot, dry, appetizing, and diffusive.
It removes constipation, abdominal distension, obstruction, heart pain, heaviness, and colic.

children.text: sauvarcalaṃ syād rucakaṃ manthapākaṃ ca tanmatam
children.translated_text: <s>Sauvarcala</s> is <s>Rucaka</s>, and it is considered <s>Manthapāka</s>.

children.text: rucakaṃ rocanaṃ bhedi dīpanaṃ pācanaṃ param ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rucaka</s> promotes appetite, is laxative, and is excellent for kindling and digestion.
It is very unctuous, removes vāta, is not greatly productive of pitta, is clear, and is light.
It purifies belching, is subtle, and conquers constipation, distension, and colic.
<s>Audbhida</s> is earthy salt, that which arises by itself from the ground.

children.text: kṣāraṃ guru kaṭu snigdhaṃ śītalaṃ vātanāśanam ||
children.translated_text: It is alkaline, heavy, pungent, unctuous, cooling, and destructive of vāta.
<s>Caṇakāmlaka</s> is very hot, kindles digestion, and sets the teeth on edge.
It has a salty secondary taste, is appetizing, and removes colic, indigestion, and constipation.
The prepared alkali is <s>Yavakṣāra</s>, <s>Yāvaśūka</s>, and <s>Yavāgraja</s>.
The alkali is also remembered as <s>Svarjikā</s>, <s>Kāpota</s>, and <s>Sukhavarcaka</s>.
<s>Suvarcikā</s> is said by specialists to be a variety of <s>Svarjikā</s>.
<s>Yavakṣāra</s> is light, unctuous, very subtle, and kindles digestive fire.
It destroys colic, vāta, āma, kapha, dyspnea, and diseases of the throat.
It destroys anemia, piles, grahaṇī disorder, gulma tumors, distension, spleen disease, and heart ailments.
<s>Svarjikā</s> should be understood as having fewer qualities than that; it removes gulma tumors and colic.
<s>Suvarcikā</s> should be understood by people as like <s>Svarjikā</s> in its qualities.
<s>Saubhāgya</s>, <s>Ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, an alkali, is called <s>Dhātudrāvaka</s>, the metal-melter.
<s>Ṭaṅkaṇa</s> produces digestive fire, is dry, removes kapha, and produces vāta and pitta.
<s>Svarjikā</s> and <s>Yāvaśūka</s> are called the two alkalis.
When that is joined with <s>Ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, it is declared to be the three alkalis.
Combined, it produces the stated qualities and is especially supreme at removing gulma tumors.
Those produced from <s>Palāśa</s>, <s>Vajrī</s>, <s>Śikharī</s>, <s>Ciñcā</s>, <s>Arka</s>, and sesame stalks,
together with that produced from barley and with <s>Svarjikā</s>, are called the group of eight alkalis.
These alkalis are equal to fire and are very powerful removers of gulma tumors and colic.
<s>Bhukta</s>, <s>Sahasravedhi</s>, <s>Rasāmla</s>, and <s>Śukla</s> are also names.
<s>Cukra</s> is very sour and hot, and is excellent for kindling and digestion.
It removes colic, gulma tumors, constipation, āma, vāta, and kapha, and is fluid-moving.
It removes vomiting, thirst, bad taste in the mouth, heart pain, and weak digestive fire.

children.text: puṃsi klībe ca karpūraḥ sitābhro himavālukaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Karpūra</s>, masculine or neuter, is <s>Sitābhra</s> and <s>Himavāluka</s>.
It is remembered as <s>Ghanasāra</s>, known as <s>Candra</s>, and also called <s>Hima</s>.
<s>Karpūra</s> is cooling, aphrodisiac, beneficial for the eyes, scraping, and light.
It is fragrant, sweet, and bitter, and removes kapha, pitta, and poison.
It destroys thirst, bad taste in the mouth, fat, and foul odor.
<s>Karpūra</s> is said to be of two kinds, divided into prepared and unprepared.
They say that the unprepared is richer in qualities than prepared camphor.
The camphor called <s>Cīnaka</s> is remembered as reducing kapha.
It also removes skin disease, itching, and vomiting, and it has a bitter taste.
<s>Mṛganābhi</s>, <s>Mṛgamada</s>, and <s>Sahasrabhit</s> are stated as names.

children.text: kastūrikā ca kastūrī vedhamukhyā ca sā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: It is remembered as <s>Kastūrikā</s>, <s>Kastūrī</s>, and <s>Vedhamukhyā</s>.
The musk produced in <s>Kāmarūpa</s> is black, while the <s>Nepālī</s> has a blue color.
The <s>Kāśmīrī</s> has a tawny hue; musk is remembered as threefold.
That produced in <s>Kāmarūpa</s> is best, while the <s>Nepālī</s> is middling.
Musk produced in the land of <s>Kāśmīra</s> is considered inferior.

children.text: kastūrikā kaṭus tiktā kṣāroṣṇā śukralā guruḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kastūrikā</s> is pungent, bitter, alkaline and hot, semen-promoting, and heavy.
It removes kapha, vāta, poison, vomiting, coldness, foul odor, and wasting.

children.text: latā kastūrikā tiktā svādvī vṛṣyā himā laghuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Latākastūrikā</s> is bitter, sweet, aphrodisiac, cooling, and light.
It benefits the eyes, is cutting, and removes kapha, thirst, and diseases of the bladder and mouth.
The substance called <s>Gandhamārjāravīrya</s> promotes virility and removes kapha and vāta.
It removes itching and skin disease, benefits the eyes, is fragrant, and removes the odor of sweat.
<s>Śrīkhaṇḍa</s>, <s>Candana</s>, <s>Bhadraśrī</s>, and <s>Tailaparṇika</s> are names of sandalwood.
It is also <s>Gandhasāra</s>, <s>Malayaja</s>, and <s>Candradyuti</s>.

children.text: svāde tiktaṃ kaṣe pītaṃ chede raktaṃ tanau sitam
children.translated_text: Sandalwood that is bitter in taste, yellow when rubbed, red when cut, and white in body,
and that is furnished with knots and hollows, is said to be the best.

children.text: candanaṃ śītalaṃ rūkṣaṃ tiktam āhlādanaṃ laghu
children.translated_text: <s>Candana</s> is cooling, dry, bitter, refreshing, and light.
It removes fatigue, wasting, poison, kapha, thirst, pitta, blood disorders, and burning.
<s>Kālīyaka</s> is also <s>Kālīya</s>, the yellowish <s>Haricandana</s>.
It is <s>Haripriya</s>, <s>Kālasāra</s>, and also <s>Kālānusāryaka</s>.
<s>Kālīyaka</s> has the qualities of the red variety and especially removes skin blemishes.
<s>Raktacandana</s> is called <s>Raktāṅga</s> and <s>Kṣudracandana</s>.
It is remembered as <s>Tilaparṇa</s>, <s>Raktasāra</s>, and <s>Pravālaphala</s>.
The red sandalwood is cooling, heavy, and sweet; it removes vomiting, thirst, blood disorders, and pitta.
It is bitter, beneficial to the eyes, aphrodisiac, and removes fever, wounds, and poison.

children.text: pataṃgaṃ raktasāraṃ ca suraṅgaṃ rañjanaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Pataṅga</s> is <s>Raktasāra</s>, <s>Suraṅga</s>, and also <s>Rañjana</s>.
It is called <s>Paṭṭarañjaka</s>, <s>Pattūra</s>, and <s>Kucandana</s>.
<s>Pataṅga</s> is sweet and cooling; it removes pitta, kapha, wounds, and blood disorders.
It should be understood as like <s>Haricandana</s>, especially as destroying burning.
All the sandalwoods are similar in taste and the other properties.

children.text: gandhena tu viśeṣo'sti pūrvaḥ śreṣṭhatamo guṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: But there is a distinction in fragrance; the first is the best of all in qualities.

children.text: aguru pravaraṃ lohaṃ rājārhaṃ yogajaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Aguru</s> is <s>Pravara</s>, <s>Loha</s>, <s>Rājārha</s>, and also <s>Yogaja</s>.
It is also <s>Vaṃśika</s>, <s>Kṛmija</s>, <s>Kṛmijagdha</s>, and <s>Anāryaka</s>.

children.text: agurūṣṇaṃ kaṭu tvacyaṃ tiktaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca pittalam
children.translated_text: <s>Aguru</s> is hot, pungent, good for the skin, bitter, sharp, and pitta-producing.
It is light, destroys diseases of the ears and eyes, and drives away cold, vāta, and kapha.
Its black variety is superior in qualities and sinks in water like iron.
Oil produced from <s>Aguru</s> is regarded as equal to black <s>Aguru</s>.

children.text: devadāru smṛtaṃ dārubhadraṃ dārv indradāru ca
children.translated_text: <s>Devadāru</s> is remembered as <s>Dārubhadra</s>, <s>Dāru</s>, and <s>Indradāru</s>,
and as <s>Mastadāru</s>, <s>Drukilima</s>, <s>Kilima</s>, and <s>Surabhūruha</s>.

children.text: devadāru laghu snigdhaṃ tiktoṣṇaṃ kaṭupāki ca
children.translated_text: <s>Devadāru</s> is light, unctuous, bitter, hot, and pungent in post-digestive effect.
It conquers constipation, abdominal distension, swelling, āma, drowsiness, hiccup, fever, and blood disorders.
It removes prameha, coryza, kapha, cough, itching, and vāta.
<s>Sarala</s> is <s>Pītavṛkṣa</s> and also <s>Surabhidāruka</s>.
<s>Sarala</s> is sweet and bitter, with pungent post-digestive effect and taste, and it is light.
It is remembered as unctuous and hot, removing diseases of the ears, throat, and eyes, and warding off harmful influences.
It removes kapha, vāta, sweat, burning, cough, fainting, and wounds.
The first kind of tagara is named <s>Kālānusārya</s>, <s>Tagara</s>, <s>Kuṭila</s>, <s>Nahuṣa</s>, and <s>Nata</s>.
The other is <s>Piṇḍatagara</s>, <s>Daṇḍahastī</s>, and <s>Barhiṇa</s>.
The two kinds of <s>Tagara</s> are hot, sweet, unctuous, and light.
They remove poison, epilepsy, pain, eye disease, and the three doṣas.
<s>Padmaka</s> is <s>Padmagandhi</s> and is also remembered as <s>Padmāhvaya</s>.

children.text: padmakaṃ tuvaraṃ tiktaṃ śītalaṃ vātalaṃ laghu ||
children.translated_text: <s>Padmaka</s> is astringent, bitter, cooling, vāta-producing, and light.
It removes erysipelas, burning, blisters, skin disease, kapha, blood disorders, and pitta.
It stabilizes pregnancy, is appetizing, and removes vomiting, wounds, and thirst.

children.text: guggulur devadhūpaś ca jaṭāyuḥ kauśikaḥ puraḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Guggulu</s> is <s>Devadhūpa</s>, <s>Jaṭāyu</s>, <s>Kauśika</s>, and <s>Pura</s>.
It is also the neuter <s>Kumbholūkhalaka</s>, and <s>Mahiṣākṣa</s> and <s>Palaṃkaṣa</s>.
<s>Mahiṣākṣa</s>, <s>Mahānīla</s>, <s>Kumuda</s>, and also <s>Padma</s>,

children.text: hiraṇyaḥ pañcamo jñeyo gugguloḥ pañca jātayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: with <s>Hiraṇya</s> as the fifth, are known as the five varieties of <s>Guggulu</s>.
The one colored like black collyrium is remembered as <s>Mahiṣākṣa</s>.
<s>Mahānīla</s> should be understood as having marks corresponding to its own name.
<s>Kumuda</s> has the appearance of a kumuda flower; <s>Padma</s> resembles a ruby.
<s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s> has the appearance of gold; thus the marks of the five have been stated.
<s>Mahiṣākṣa</s> and <s>Mahānīla</s> are both beneficial for lordly elephants.
<s>Kumuda</s> and <s>Padma</s> are supreme for horses, bringing well-being and health.
<s>Kanaka</s> is especially praised for human beings.
Sometimes <s>Mahiṣākṣa</s> too is considered by some to be suitable for people.

children.text: guggulur viśadas tikto vīryoṣṇaḥ pittalaḥ saraḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Guggulu</s> is clear, bitter, hot in potency, pitta-producing, and flowing.

children.text: kaṣāyaḥ kaṭukaḥ pāke kaṭū rūkṣo laghuḥ paraḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is astringent, pungent in post-digestive effect, pungent, dry, light, and excellent.
It joins fractures, is aphrodisiac, subtle, good for the voice, and rejuvenating.
It kindles digestion, is slimy and strengthening, and removes kapha, vāta, wounds, and apacī swellings.
It conquers disorders of fat, prameha, stones, vāta disorders, excess moisture, skin disease, āma, and vāta.
It also conquers pustules, nodules, swelling, piles, gaṇḍamālā swellings, and worms.
Because of its sweetness it pacifies vāta, and because of its astringency it removes pitta.
Because of its bitterness it conquers kapha; therefore <s>Guggulu</s> removes all doṣas.

children.text: sa navo bṛṃhaṇo vṛṣyaḥ purāṇas tv atilekhanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When new it is nourishing and aphrodisiac, but when old it is excessively scraping.
Unctuous, resembling gold, and like a ripe jambu fruit,
fragrant and sticky: such <s>Guggulu</s> is said to be new.
Dry, foul-smelling, and having lost its natural color,

children.text: purāṇaḥ sa tu vijñeyo guggulur vīryavarjitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Guggulu</s> should be known as old and devoid of potency.
Sour and sharp substances, indigestion, sexual intercourse, exertion, and heat,
as well as wine and anger, should be properly avoided by one who uses <s>Pura</s> and seeks its benefits.
<s>Śrīvāsa</s> is <s>Saralasrāva</s>, <s>Śrīveṣṭa</s>, and <s>Vṛkṣadhūpaka</s>.
<s>Śrīvāsa</s> is sweet, bitter, unctuous, hot, astringent, and flowing.
It produces pitta and removes vāta, diseases of the head, eyes, and voice, and kapha.
It is <s>rakṣoghna</s> (warding off harmful beings) and removes bad odor from sweat, lice, itching, and wounds.
<s>Rāla</s> is remembered as <s>Śālaniryāsa</s> and also as <s>Sarjarasa</s>.
It is <s>Devadhūpa</s>, <s>Yakṣadhūpa</s>, and also <s>Sarvarasa</s>.

children.text: rālo himo gurus tiktaḥ kaṣāyo grāhako haret
children.translated_text: <s>Rāla</s> is cooling, heavy, bitter, astringent, and absorbent; it removes
the doṣas, blood disorders, sweating, erysipelas, fever, wounds, and fissures of the feet.
It also removes graha affliction, fractures, and burns, and destroys colic and diarrhea.
<s>Kunduru</s> is <s>Mukunda</s>, <s>Sugandha</s>, and also <s>Kunda</s>.
<s>Kunduru</s> is sweet, bitter, sharp, beneficial to the skin, and pungent; it removes
fever, sweating, graha affliction, misfortune, diseases of the mouth, kapha, and vāta.
<s>Sihlaka</s> is <s>Turuṣka</s>, because it is produced in the country of the <s>Yavanas</s>.
It is also counted as <s>Kapitaila</s> and likewise called <s>Kapi</s>.
<s>Sihlaka</s> is pungent, sweet, unctuous, and hot, and it produces semen and beauty.
It is aphrodisiac and good for the throat, and it removes sweating, skin disease, fever, burning, and graha affliction.
<s>Jātīphala</s> is <s>Jātikośa</s> and also <s>Mālatīphala</s>.

children.text: jātīphalaṃ rase tiktaṃ tīkṣṇoṣṇaṃ rocanaṃ laghu
children.translated_text: <s>Jātīphala</s> is bitter in taste, sharp, hot, appetizing, and light.
It is pungent, kindles digestion, is absorbent, benefits the voice, and removes kapha and vāta.
It destroys bad taste in the mouth, foul odor, and dark discoloration.
It also destroys worms, cough, vomiting, dyspnea, wasting disease, coryza, and pain in the heart.
The rind of <s>Jātīphala</s> is called <s>Jātīpattrī</s> by the best physicians.
<s>Jātīpattrī</s> is light, sweet, pungent, hot, and improves taste and complexion.
It removes kapha, cough, vomiting, dyspnea, thirst, worms, and poison.
<s>Lavaṅga</s> is <s>Devakusuma</s>, called <s>Śrī</s>, and <s>Śrīprasūnaka</s>.

children.text: lavaṃgaṃ kaṭukaṃ tiktaṃ laghu netrahitaṃ himam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lavaṅga</s> is pungent, bitter, light, beneficial to the eyes, and cooling.
It kindles digestion, promotes digestion, is appetizing, and destroys kapha, pitta, and blood disorders.
It quickly destroys thirst, vomiting, distension, and colic.

children.text: kāsaṃ śvāsaṃ ca hikkāṃ ca kṣayaṃ kṣapayati dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: It certainly destroys cough, dyspnea, hiccup, and wasting disease.

children.text: elā sthūlā ca bahulā pṛthvīkā tripuṭāpi ca ||
children.translated_text: Large <s>Elā</s> is <s>Bahulā</s>, <s>Pṛthvīkā</s>, and also <s>Tripuṭā</s>.

children.text: bhadrailā bṛhadelā ca candrabālā ca niṣkuṭiḥ
children.translated_text: It is <s>Bhadrailā</s>, <s>Bṛhadelā</s>, <s>Candrabālā</s>, and <s>Niṣkuṭi</s>.
<s>Sthūlailā</s> is pungent in post-digestive effect and in taste, kindles digestive fire, and is light.
It is dry and hot, and removes kapha, pitta, blood disorders, itching, dyspnea, and thirst.
It dispels nausea, poison, pain of the bladder, mouth, and head, vomiting, and cough.
Small <s>Elā</s> is <s>Upakuñcikā</s>, <s>Tutthā</s>, <s>Koraṅgī</s>, <s>Drāviḍī</s>, and <s>Truṭi</s>.
Small <s>Elā</s> removes kapha, dyspnea, cough, piles, and dysuria.

children.text: rase tu kaṭukā śītā laghvī vātaharī matā ||
children.translated_text: In taste it is pungent, cooling, light, and regarded as removing vāta.

children.text: tvakpattraṃ ca varāṅgaṃ syad bhṛṅgaṃ cocaṃ tathotkaṭam
children.translated_text: <s>Tvakpattra</s>, <s>Varāṅga</s>, <s>Bhṛṅga</s>, <s>Coca</s>, and <s>Utkaṭa</s> are its names.

children.text: tvacaṃ laghūṣṇaṃ kaṭukaṃ svādu tiktaṃ ca rūkṣakam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tvak</s> is light, hot, pungent, sweet, bitter, and dry.
It promotes pitta, destroys kapha and vāta, and removes itching, āma, and loss of appetite.
It removes heart and bladder diseases, vāta, piles, worms, coryza, and diminishes śukra.
<s>Tvaksvādvī</s> is <s>Tanutvak</s>, and it is also considered <s>Dārusitā</s>.
<s>Dārusitā</s> is said to be sweet and bitter, and it removes vāta and pitta.
It is fragrant, semen-promoting, improves complexion, and removes dryness of the mouth and thirst.

children.text: pattrakaṃ tamālapattraṃ ca tathā syāt pattranāmakam
children.translated_text: <s>Pattraka</s> is <s>Tamālapattra</s> and likewise bears the name <s>Pattra</s>.

children.text: pattrakaṃ madhuraṃ kiṃcit tīkṣṇoṣṇaṃ picchilaṃ laghu
children.translated_text: <s>Pattraka</s> is somewhat sweet, sharp, hot, slimy, and light.
It destroys kapha, vāta, piles, nausea, loss of appetite, and coryza.
<s>Nāgapuṣpa</s> is remembered as <s>Nāga</s>, <s>Kesara</s>, and <s>Nāgakesara</s>.
It is called <s>Cāmpeya</s>, <s>Nāgakiñjalka</s>, and <s>Kāñcanāhvaya</s>.
<s>Nāgapuṣpa</s> is astringent, hot, dry, light, and removes āma.
It destroys fever, itching, thirst, sweating, vomiting, and nausea.
It removes foul odor, skin disease, erysipelas, kapha, pitta, and poison.
Equal parts of <s>Tvak</s>, <s>Elā</s>, and <s>Pattraka</s> are <s>Trisugandhi</s>, called <s>Trijātaka</s>.
When combined with <s>Nāgakesara</s>, it is called <s>Cāturjātaka</s>.
Both of these are appetizing, dry, sharp, hot, and remove bad odor from the mouth.
They are light, produce pitta and digestive fire, improve complexion, and remove kapha, vāta, and poison.

children.text: kuṅkumaṃ ghusṛṇaṃ raktaṃ kāśmīraṃ pītakaṃ varam
children.translated_text: <s>Kuṅkuma</s> is <s>Ghusṛṇa</s>, <s>Rakta</s>, <s>Kāśmīra</s>, <s>Pītaka</s>, and <s>Vara</s>.
It is <s>Saṃkoca</s>, <s>Piśuna</s>, <s>Dhīra</s>, <s>Vāhlīka</s>, and called <s>Śoṇita</s>.
The <s>Kuṅkuma</s> that grows in a field in the country of <s>Kāśmīra</s>
has fine filaments, is reddish, smells like a lotus, and is the best.
The <s>Kuṅkuma</s> produced in the country of <s>Vāhlīka</s> is remembered as pale.
It has the fragrance of ketakī and fine filaments; that is the middle grade.
The <s>Pārasīka</s> <s>Kuṅkuma</s> is said to have the fragrance of honey.
It is slightly pale in color and has coarse filaments; that is the lowest grade.
<s>Kuṅkuma</s> is pungent and unctuous, and conquers headache, wounds, and living pests.
It is bitter, removes vomiting, improves complexion, and removes dark facial marks and the three doṣas.

children.text: gorocanā tu maṅgalyā vandyā gaurī ca rocanā
children.translated_text: <s>Gorocanā</s> is <s>Maṅgalyā</s>, <s>Vandyā</s>, <s>Gaurī</s>, and <s>Rocanā</s>.
<s>Gorocanā</s> is cooling, bitter, complexion-promoting, and gives auspiciousness and luster.
It removes poison, misfortune, graha affliction, insanity, miscarriage, wounds, and blood disorders.
<s>Nakha</s> is <s>Vyāghranakha</s>, <s>Vyāghrāyudha</s>, and <s>Cakrakāraka</s>.
Small <s>Nakha</s> is called <s>Nakhī</s> and <s>Hanuhaṭṭavilāsinī</s>.
The substance <s>Nakha</s> removes graha affliction, kapha, vāta, blood disorders, fever, and skin disease.
It is light, hot, semen-promoting, complexion-promoting, sweet, and removes wounds and poison.
It removes misfortune and bad odor from the mouth; it is pungent in post-digestive effect and in taste.
<s>Bāla</s> is <s>Hrīvera</s>, <s>Barhiṣṭha</s>, <s>Udīcya</s>, and also called <s>Keśāmbu</s>.
<s>Bālaka</s> is cooling, dry, light, kindles digestion, and promotes digestion.
It conquers nausea, loss of appetite, erysipelas, heart disease, āma, and diarrhea.
<s>Vīraṇa</s> is <s>Vīrataru</s>, <s>Vīra</s>, and <s>Bahumūlaka</s>.
<s>Vīraṇa</s> promotes digestion, is cooling, removes vomiting, is light, and is bitter.
It is stambhana (checking discharge), removes fever, conquers giddiness and intoxication, and removes kapha and pitta.
It removes thirst, blood disorders, poison, erysipelas, dysuria, burning, and wounds.

children.text: vīraṇasya tu mūlaṃ syāduśīraṃ naladaṃ ca tat
children.translated_text: The root of <s>Vīraṇa</s> is <s>Uśīra</s>; that is also <s>Nalada</s>.

children.text: amṛṇālaṃ ca sevyaṃ ca samagandhikam ityapi ||
children.translated_text: It is also called <s>Amṛṇāla</s>, <s>Sevya</s>, and <s>Samagandhika</s>.

children.text: uśīraṃ pācanaṃ śītaṃ stambhanaṃ laghu tiktakam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Uśīra</s> is digestive, cooling, styptic, light, and slightly bitter.
It is sweet, removes fever, vomiting, and intoxication, and conquers kapha and pitta.
It removes thirst, blood disorders, poison, erysipelas, burning, dysuria, and wounds.
<s>Jaṭāmāṃsī</s> is <s>Bhūtajaṭā</s>, <s>Jaṭilā</s>, and <s>Tapasvinī</s>.

children.text: māṃsī tiktā kaṣāyā ca medhyā kāntibalapradā
children.translated_text: <s>Māṃsī</s> is bitter and astringent, and gives intellect, beauty, and strength.
It is sweet and cooling, and removes the three doṣas, blood disorders, burning, erysipelas, and skin disease.
<s>Śaileya</s> is <s>Śilāpuṣpa</s>, <s>Vṛddha</s>, and <s>Kālānusāryaka</s>.
<s>Śaileya</s> is cooling, cordial, kapha- and pitta-removing, and light.
It removes itching, skin disease, urinary stone, burning, poison, and rectal bleeding.

children.text: mustakaṃ na striyāṃ mustaṃ triṣu vāridanāmakam
children.translated_text: The word <s>Mustaka</s> is not feminine; <s>Musta</s>, also called <s>Vārida</s>, is used in all three genders.
<s>Kuruvinda</s> is also recorded, and another name is <s>Kroḍakaseruka</s>.

children.text: bhadramustaṃ ca gundrā ca tathā nāgaramustakaḥ
children.translated_text: It is also <s>Bhadramusta</s>, <s>Gundrā</s>, and likewise <s>Nāgaramustaka</s>.

children.text: mustaṃ kaṭu himaṃ grāhi tiktaṃ dīpanapācanam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Musta</s> is pungent, cooling, absorbent, bitter, digestive, and carminative.
It is astringent and removes kapha, pitta, blood disorders, thirst, fever, loss of appetite, and worms.
The <s>Mustaka</s> that grows in marshy country is praised.
Even among these, the sages have declared <s>Nāgaramustaka</s> the best.
<s>Karcūra</s> is also <s>Vedhamukhya</s>, <s>Drāviḍa</s>, <s>Kalpaka</s>, and <s>Śaṭī</s>.

children.text: karcūro dīpano rucyaḥ kaṭukastikta eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Karcūra</s> stimulates digestion, promotes relish, and is pungent and bitter.
It is fragrant, pungent in post-digestive effect, and removes skin disease, piles, wounds, and cough.
It is hot and light, and removes dyspnea, gulma tumors, vāta, kapha, and worms.
<s>Murā</s> is <s>Gandhakuṭī</s>, <s>Daityā</s>, <s>Surabhi</s>, and <s>Śālaparṇikā</s>.

children.text: murā tiktā himā svādvī laghvī pittānilāpahā
children.translated_text: <s>Murā</s> is bitter, cooling, sweet, light, and removes pitta and vāta.
It destroys fever, blood disorders, spirits and demons, skin disease, and cough.
<s>Śaṭhī</s> is <s>Palāśī</s>, <s>Ṣaḍgranthā</s>, <s>Suvratā</s>, and <s>Gandhamūlikā</s>.
It is <s>Gāndhārikā</s>, <s>Gandhavadhū</s>, <s>Vadhū</s>, and <s>Palāśikā</s>.
<s>Gandhapalāśī</s> is astringent, absorbent, and light.
It is bitter, sharp, pungent, not hot, and removes impurities of the mouth.
It removes swelling, cough, wounds, dyspnea, colic, sidhma skin disease, and graha disorders.

children.text: priyaṅguḥ phalinī kāntā latā ca mahilāhvayā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Priyaṅgu</s> is <s>Phalinī</s>, <s>Kāntā</s>, <s>Latā</s>, and <s>Mahilāhvayā</s>.
It is <s>Gundrā</s>, <s>Gandhaphalā</s>, <s>Śyāmā</s>, and <s>Viṣvaksenāṅganāpriyā</s>.
<s>Priyaṅgu</s> is cooling, bitter, astringent, and removes vāta and pitta.
It removes excessive bleeding, foul odor, sweating, burning, and fever.
It destroys gulma tumors, thirst, poison, and delusion; <s>Gandhapriyaṅgukā</s> acts in the same way.

children.text: tatphalaṃ madhu rūkṣaṃ kaṣāyaṃ śītalaṃ guru
children.translated_text: Its fruit is sweet, dry, astringent, cooling, and heavy.
It causes constipation, abdominal distension, and strength; it is absorbent and conquers kapha and pitta.

children.text: reṇukā rājaputrī ca nandinī kapilā dvijā
children.translated_text: <s>Reṇukā</s> is <s>Rājaputrī</s>, <s>Nandinī</s>, <s>Kapilā</s>, and <s>Dvijā</s>.
It is remembered as <s>Bhasmagandhā</s>, <s>Pāṇḍuputrī</s>, <s>Kauntī</s>, and <s>Hareṇukā</s>.

children.text: reṇukā kaṭukā pāke tiktānuṣṇā kaṭur laghuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Reṇukā</s> is pungent in post-digestive effect, bitter, mildly hot, pungent, and light.
It increases pitta, kindles digestion, promotes intellect, digests, and causes miscarriage.
It also produces balāsa (phlegmatic disease) and vāta, while removing thirst, itching, poison, and burning.

children.text: granthiparṇaṃ granthikaṃ ca kākapucchaṃ ca gucchakam
children.translated_text: <s>Granthiparṇa</s> is <s>Granthika</s>, <s>Kākapuccha</s>, and <s>Gucchaka</s>.
It is called <s>Nīlapuṣpa</s>, <s>Sugandha</s>, and <s>Tailaparṇaka</s>.
<s>Granthiparṇa</s> is bitter, sharp, pungent, hot, digestive, and light.
It destroys kapha, vāta, poison, dyspnea, itching, and foul odor.
<s>Sthauṇeyaka</s> is <s>Barhibarha</s>, <s>Śukabarha</s>, and <s>Kukkura</s>.
It is also <s>Śīrṇaromaśuka</s>, <s>Śukapuṣpa</s>, and <s>Śukacchada</s>.

children.text: sthauṇeyakaṃ kaṭu svādu tiktaṃ snigdhaṃ tridoṣanut ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sthauṇeyaka</s> is pungent, sweet, bitter, unctuous, and removes the three doṣas.
It promotes intellect and semen, gives relish, wards off demons, and conquers fever and worms.
It destroys skin disease, blood disorders, thirst, burning, foul odor, freckles, and dark spots.
It is <s>Niśācara</s>, <s>Dhanahara</s>, <s>Kitava</s>, and <s>Gaṇahāsa</s>.

children.text: corakaḥ śaṅkitaś caṇḍo duṣpattraḥ kṣemako ripuḥ
children.translated_text: It is <s>Coraka</s>, <s>Śaṅkita</s>, <s>Caṇḍa</s>, <s>Duṣpattra</s>, <s>Kṣemaka</s>, and <s>Ripu</s>.

children.text: rocako madhurastiktaḥ kaṭuḥ pāke kaṭur laghuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rocaka</s> is sweet, bitter, pungent, pungent in post-digestive effect, and light.
It is sharp, cordial, and cooling; it removes skin disease, itching, kapha, and vāta.
It destroys demons, ugliness, sweat, fat, blood disorders, fever, odor, poison, and wounds.

children.text: tālīśam uktaṃ pattrāḍhyaṃ dhātrīpattraṃ ca tatsmṛtam
children.translated_text: <s>Tālīśa</s> is called <s>Pattrāḍhya</s>; it is remembered as <s>Dhātrīpattra</s>.
<s>Tālīśa</s> is light, sharp, and hot; it destroys dyspnea, cough, kapha, and vāta.
It removes loss of appetite, gulma tumors, āma (undigested residue), weak digestive fire, wasting disease, and other illnesses.

children.text: kaṅkolaṃ kolaṃ proktaṃ cātha kośaphalaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṅkola</s> is called <s>Kola</s>, and also remembered as <s>Kośaphala</s>.

children.text: kaṅkolaṃ laghu tīkṣṇoṣṇaṃ tiktaṃ hṛdyaṃ rucipradam
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṅkola</s> is light, sharp, hot, bitter, cordial, and gives relish.
It removes bad odor of the mouth, heart disease, kapha and vāta disorders, and blindness.
<s>Gandhakokilā</s> is unctuous, hot, kapha-removing, bitter, and fragrant.
<s>Gandhamālatī</s> should be understood as equivalent to <s>Gandhakokilā</s>.
<s>Lāmajjaka</s> is <s>Sunāla</s>, <s>Amṛṇāla</s>, <s>Lava</s>, and <s>Laghu</s>.
It is <s>Iṣṭakāpathaka</s>, <s>Savya</s>, <s>Nalada</s>, and <s>Vidātaka</s>.
<s>Lāmajjaka</s> is cooling, bitter, light, and conquers the three doṣas and blood disorders.
It removes skin disease, sweating, dysuria, burning, pitta, and blood diseases.
<s>Elavāluka</s> is <s>Aileya</s>, <s>Sugandhi</s>, and <s>Harivāluka</s>.
