<s>Ailavāluka</s>, <s>Elālu</s>, <s>Kapittha</s>, and <s>Pattra</s> are stated as its names.

children.text: elālu kaṭukaṃ pāke kaṣāyaṃ śītalaṃ laghu
children.translated_text: <s>Elālu</s> is pungent in post-digestive effect, astringent, cooling, and light.
It destroys itching, wounds, vomiting, thirst, cough, loss of appetite, and heart pain.
It removes balāsa (phlegmatic disease), poison, pitta, blood disorders, skin disease, urinary disease, and worms.
<s>Kuṭannaṭa</s>, <s>Dāsapura</s>, <s>Bāleya</s>, and <s>Paripelava</s> are names of it.
So too are <s>Plavagopura</s>, <s>Gonarda</s>, <s>Kaivartī</s>, and <s>Mustaka</s>.
<s>Vitunnaka</s> is like <s>Mustā</s>, has a delicate sheath, and resembles a parrot.

children.text: vitunnakaṃ himaṃ tiktaṃ kaṣāyaṃ kaṭu kāntidam
children.translated_text: <s>Vitunnaka</s> is cooling, bitter, astringent, pungent, and gives beauty.
It drives away kapha, pitta, blood disorders, erysipelas, skin disease, itching, and poison.

children.text: spṛkkāsṛg brāhmaṇo devo marunmālā latā laghuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Spṛkkā</s>, <s>Asṛk</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Deva</s>, <s>Marunmālā</s>, <s>Latā</s>, and <s>Laghu</s>
and also <s>Samudrāntā</s>, <s>Vadhū</s>, <s>Koṭivarṣā</s>, and <s>Laṅkopikā</s> are its names.

children.text: spṛkkā svādvī himā vṛṣyā tiktā nikhiladoṣanut
children.translated_text: <s>Spṛkkā</s> is sweet, cooling, semen-promoting, bitter, and removes all the doṣas.
It removes skin disease, itching, poison, sweating, burning, misfortune, fever, and blood disorders.

children.text: parpaṭī rañjanī kṛṣṇā jatukā jananī janī
children.translated_text: <s>Parpaṭī</s> is <s>Rañjanī</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, <s>Jatukā</s>, <s>Jananī</s>, and <s>Janī</s>.
It is also <s>Jatukṛṣṇā</s>, <s>Agnisaṃsparśā</s>, <s>Jatukṛt</s>, and <s>Cakravartinī</s>.
<s>Parpaṭī</s> is astringent, bitter, cooling, complexion-promoting, and light.
It removes poison and wounds, and it dispels itching, kapha, pitta, blood disorders, and skin disease.
<s>Nalikā</s> is <s>Vidrumalatā</s>, <s>Kapotacaraṇā</s>, <s>Naṭī</s>,
<s>Dhamanī</s>, <s>Añjanakeśī</s>, <s>Nirmedhyā</s>, <s>Suṣirā</s>, and <s>Nalī</s>.
<s>Nalikā</s> is cooling, light, good for the eyes, and removes kapha and pitta.
It dispels dysuria, urinary stones, vāta, thirst, blood disorders, skin disease, itching, and fever.
<s>Prapauṇḍarīka</s> is <s>Pauṇḍarya</s>, <s>Cakṣuṣya</s>, and <s>Pauṇḍarīyaka</s>.

children.text: pauṇḍaryaṃ madhuraṃ tiktaṃ kaṣāyaṃ śukralaṃ himam
children.translated_text: <s>Pauṇḍarya</s> is sweet, bitter, astringent, semen-promoting, and cooling.
It benefits the eyes, is sweet in post-digestive effect, improves complexion, and drives away pitta and kapha.
Then the proud lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, chief of the rākṣasas,
passion-stricken, carried off by force <s>Sītā</s>, the wife of <s>Rāma</s>.
Then mighty <s>Rāma</s> slew that enemy, the abductor of his wife,
on the battlefield, with the army of monkeys as his aid.
When that enemy of the gods, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, proud of his strength, had been killed,
the thousand-eyed king of the gods, <s>Indra</s>, was pleased with <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: tatra ye vānarāḥ kecid rākṣasair nihatā raṇe
children.translated_text: There, whatever monkeys had been slain by the rākṣasas in battle,
<s>Indra</s> brought them back to life by sprinkling them with showers of nectar.
Then in the places where, from the bodies of the monkeys,
drops of ambrosia fell down, <s>Guḍūcikā</s> arose from them.
<s>Guḍūcī</s> is <s>Madhuparṇī</s>, <s>Amṛtā</s>, and <s>Amṛtavallarī</s>.
It is also <s>Chinnā</s>, <s>Chinnaruhā</s>, <s>Chinnodbhavā</s>, and <s>Vatsādanī</s>.

children.text: jīvantī tantrikā somā somavallī ca kuṇḍalī
children.translated_text: It is <s>Jīvantī</s>, <s>Tantrikā</s>, <s>Somā</s>, <s>Somavallī</s>, and <s>Kuṇḍalī</s>.
It is <s>Cakralakṣaṇikā</s>, <s>Dhīrā</s>, <s>Viśalyā</s>, and <s>Rasāyanī</s>.
It is <s>Candrahāsā</s>, <s>Vayaḥsthā</s>, <s>Maṇḍalī</s>, and <s>Devanirmitā</s>.
<s>Guḍūcī</s> is pungent, bitter, sweet in post-digestive effect, and rejuvenating.
It is absorbent, astringent, hot, light, strengthening, and kindles digestive fire.
It removes the three doṣas, āma, thirst, burning, urinary disease, cough, and pallor.
It cures jaundice, skin disease, vāta, blood disorders, fever, worms, and vomiting.
It dispels prameha, dyspnea, cough, piles, dysuria, heart disease, and vāta.
<s>Tāmbūlavallī</s>, <s>Tāmbūlī</s>, <s>Nāginī</s>, and <s>Nāgavallarī</s> are names of <s>Tāmbūla</s>.

children.text: tāmbūlaṃ viśadaṃ rucyaṃ tīkṣṇoṣṇaṃ tuvaraṃ saram ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tāmbūla</s> is cleansing, appetizing, sharp, hot, astringent, and laxative.

children.text: vaśyaṃ tiktaṃ kaṭu kṣāraṃ raktapittakaraṃ laghu
children.translated_text: It is subduing, bitter, pungent, alkaline, light, and produces raktapitta.
It is strengthening and removes phlegm, foul odor of the mouth, wastes, vāta, and fatigue.
<s>Bilva</s> is also <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>, <s>Śailūṣa</s>, <s>Mālūra</s>, and <s>Śrīphala</s>.
<s>Śrīphala</s> is astringent, bitter, absorbent, dry, and produces digestive fire and pitta.
It removes vāta and śleṣma, is strengthening, light, hot, and promotes digestion.
<s>Gāmbhārī</s> is <s>Bhadraparṇī</s>, <s>Śrīparṇī</s>, and <s>Madhuparṇikā</s>.
It is <s>Kāśmīrī</s>, <s>Kāśmarī</s>, <s>Hīrā</s>, <s>Kāśmarya</s>, and <s>Pītarohiṇī</s>.
It is also <s>Kṛṣṇavṛntā</s>, <s>Madhurasā</s>, and <s>Mahākusumikā</s>.

children.text: kāśmarī tuvarā tiktā vīryoṣṇā madhurā guruḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kāśmarī</s> is astringent, bitter, hot in potency, sweet, and heavy.
It kindles digestion, promotes digestion, supports intelligence, opens the bowels, and conquers giddiness and wasting.
It removes doṣas, thirst, āma, colic, piles, poison, burning, and fever.

children.text: tatphalaṃ bṛṃhaṇaṃ vṛṣyaṃ guru keśyaṃ rasāyanam
children.translated_text: Its fruit is nourishing, semen-promoting, heavy, beneficial to the hair, and rejuvenating.
It removes vāta, pitta, thirst, blood disorders, wasting, and obstruction of urine.

children.text: svādu pāke himaṃ snigdhaṃ tuvarāmlaṃ viśuddhikṛt
children.translated_text: It is sweet in post-digestive effect, cooling, unctuous, astringent-sour, and cleansing.
It destroys burning, thirst, vāta, raktapitta, injury, and wasting disease.
<s>Pāṭali</s> is <s>Pāṭalā</s>, <s>Amoghā</s>, <s>Madhudūtī</s>, and <s>Phaleruhā</s>.
It is <s>Kṛṣṇavṛntā</s>, <s>Kuberākṣī</s>, <s>Kālasthālī</s>, and <s>Alivallabhā</s>.
It is said to be <s>Tāmrapuṣpī</s>; another, the white <s>Pāṭalā</s>, is
<s>Muṣkaka</s>, <s>Mokṣaka</s>, <s>Ghaṇṭāpāṭali</s>, and <s>Kāṣṭhapāṭalā</s>.
<s>Pāṭalā</s> is astringent, bitter, not hot, and removes the three doṣas.
It removes loss of appetite, dyspnea, swelling, blood disorders, vomiting, hiccup, and thirst.

children.text: puṣpaṃ kaṣāyaṃ madhuraṃ himaṃ hṛdyaṃ kaphāsranut
children.translated_text: Its flower is astringent, sweet, cooling, heart-friendly, and removes kapha and blood disorders.
It removes pitta and diarrhea and benefits the throat; its fruit removes hiccup, blood disorders, and pitta.

children.text: agnimantho jayaḥ sa syāc chrīparṇī gaṇikārikā
children.translated_text: <s>Agnimantha</s> is <s>Jaya</s>; it is also <s>Śrīparṇī</s> and <s>Gaṇikārikā</s>.
It is <s>Jayā</s>, <s>Jayantī</s>, <s>Tarkārī</s>, <s>Nādeyī</s>, and <s>Vaijayantikā</s>.
<s>Agnimantha</s> removes swelling, is hot in potency, and removes kapha and vāta.
It dispels pallor; it is pungent, bitter, astringent, sweet, and gives digestive fire.
<s>Śyonāka</s> is <s>Śoṣaṇa</s>, <s>Naṭa</s>, <s>Kaṭvaṅga</s>, and <s>Ṭuṇṭuka</s>.
It is <s>Maṇḍūkaparṇa</s>, <s>Pattrorṇa</s>, <s>Śukanāsa</s>, and <s>Kuṭannaṭa</s>.
It is also <s>Dīrghavṛnta</s>, <s>Aralu</s>, <s>Pṛthuśimba</s>, and <s>Kaṭaṃbhara</s>.
<s>Śyonāka</s> kindles digestion; it is pungent in post-digestive effect, astringent, and cooling.
It is absorbent, bitter, and destroys vāta, śleṣma, pitta, and cough.
The young fruit of <s>Ṭuṇṭuka</s> is dry and removes vāta and kapha.

children.text: hṛdyaṃ kaṣāyaṃ madhuraṃ rocanaṃ laghu dīpanam
children.translated_text: It is heart-friendly, astringent, sweet, appetizing, light, and kindles digestion.
When mature, it removes abdominal masses, piles, and worms; it is heavy and aggravates vāta.
<s>Śrīphala</s>, <s>Sarvatobhadra</s>, <s>Pāṭalā</s>, <s>Gaṇikārikā</s>,
and <s>Śyonāka</s>: with these five, the great <s>Pañcamūla</s> is understood.
The great <s>Pañcamūla</s> is bitter and astringent, and removes kapha and vāta.
It is sweet, cures dyspnea and cough, is hot and light, and kindles digestive fire.

children.text: śāliparṇī sthirā saumyā triparṇī pīvarī guhā
children.translated_text: <s>Śāliparṇī</s> is <s>Sthirā</s>, <s>Saumyā</s>, <s>Triparṇī</s>, <s>Pīvarī</s>, and <s>Guhā</s>.
It is also <s>Vidārigandhā</s>, <s>Dīrghāṅgī</s>, <s>Dīrghapattrā</s>, and <s>Aṃśumatī</s>.
<s>Śāliparṇī</s> is heavy and conquers vomiting, fever, dyspnea, and diarrhea.
It removes wasting disease and the three <s>doṣa</s>s, is nourishing, and is a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative).
It is bitter, antitoxic, and sweet, and it drives away wounds, cough, and worms.
<s>Pṛśniparṇī</s> is also <s>Pṛthakparṇī</s>, <s>Citraparṇī</s>, and <s>Ahiparṇī</s>.
It is <s>Kroṣṭuvinnā</s>, <s>Siṃhapucchī</s>, <s>Kalaśī</s>, <s>Dhāvanī</s>, and <s>Guhā</s>.
<s>Pṛśniparṇī</s> destroys the three <s>doṣa</s>s, is aphrodisiac, hot, sweet, and laxative.
It destroys burning, fever, dyspnea, bloody diarrhea, thirst, and vomiting.
<s>Vārttākī</s>, <s>Kṣudrabhaṇṭākī</s>, <s>Mahatī</s>, <s>Bṛhatī</s>, and <s>Kulī</s> are its names.
So too are <s>Hiṅgulī</s>, <s>Rāṣṭrikā</s>, <s>Siṃhī</s>, <s>Mahoṣṭrī</s>, and <s>Duṣpradharṣiṇī</s>.
<s>Bṛhatī</s> is absorbent, cordial, digestive, and acts on <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>.
It is pungent and bitter, and destroys bad taste in the mouth, impurities, and loss of appetite.
It is hot and conquers skin disease, fever, dyspnea, colic, cough, and weak digestive fire.

children.text: kaṇṭakārī tu duḥsparśā kṣudrā vyāghrī nidigdhikā
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṇṭakārī</s> is <s>Duḥsparśā</s>, <s>Kṣudrā</s>, <s>Vyāghrī</s>, and <s>Nidigdhikā</s>.
It is also <s>Kaṇṭālikā</s>, <s>Kaṇṭakinī</s>, <s>Dhāvanī</s>, and <s>Bṛhatī</s>.
The white small variety is <s>Candrahāsā</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇā</s>, and <s>Kṣetradūtikā</s>.
It is <s>Garbhadā</s>, <s>Candramā</s>, <s>Candrī</s>, <s>Candrapuṣpā</s>, and <s>Priyaṃkarī</s>.

children.text: kaṇṭakārī sarā tiktā kaṭukā dīpanī laghuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṇṭakārī</s> is laxative, bitter, pungent, digestive-kindling, and light.
It is dry, hot, and digestive; it destroys cough, dyspnea, fever, <s>kapha</s>, and <s>vāta</s>.
It destroys coryza, pain in the side, worms, and heart diseases.

children.text: tayoḥ phalaṃ kaṭu rase pāke ca kaṭukaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: The fruit of the two is pungent in taste and becomes pungent in post-digestive effect.
It promotes the discharge of semen, is penetrating, bitter, increases <s>pitta</s> and digestive fire, and is light.
It destroys <s>kapha</s>, <s>vāta</s>, itching, cough, fat, worms, and fever.

children.text: tadvat proktā sitā kṣudrā viśeṣād garbhakāriṇī ||
children.translated_text: The white small variety is said to be the same, and is especially conception-promoting.
<s>Gokṣura</s> is also <s>Kṣuraka</s>, <s>Trikaṇṭa</s>, and <s>Svādukaṇṭaka</s>.
It is also called <s>Gokaṇṭaka</s>, <s>Gokṣuraka</s>, and <s>Vanaśṛṅgāṭa</s>.

children.text: palaṃkaṣā śvadaṃṣṭrā ca tathā syād ikṣugandhikā
children.translated_text: So too it is <s>Palaṃkaṣā</s>, <s>Śvadaṃṣṭrā</s>, and <s>Ikṣugandhikā</s>.
<s>Gokṣura</s> is cooling, sweet, strength-giving, and cleansing for the bladder.
It is sweet, kindles digestion, is aphrodisiac, gives nourishment, and removes urinary stones.
It lessens <s>prameha</s> (urinary disorder), dyspnea, cough, piles, dysuria, heart disease, and <s>vāta</s>.
<s>Śāliparṇī</s>, <s>Pṛśniparṇī</s>, <s>Vārttākī</s>, <s>Kaṇṭakārikā</s>,
and <s>Gokṣura</s>: with these five there is the lesser <s>pañcamūla</s> (five-root group).
This <s>pañcamūla</s> is light, sweet, strengthening, and removes <s>pitta</s> and <s>vāta</s>.
It is not excessively hot, is nourishing and absorbent, and drives away fever, dyspnea, and urinary stones.
With the two <s>pañcamūla</s> groups, <s>daśamūla</s> (the ten-root group) is declared.
<s>Daśamūla</s> destroys the three <s>doṣa</s>s and removes dyspnea, cough, headache,
drowsiness, swelling, fever, abdominal distension, pain in the side, and loss of appetite.
<s>Jīvantī</s> is <s>Jīvanī</s>, <s>Jīvā</s>, <s>Jīvanīyā</s>, and <s>Madhusravā</s>.
It also has the auspicious name <s>Śākaśreṣṭhā</s> and is called <s>Payasvinī</s>.
<s>Jīvantī</s> is cooling, sweet, unctuous, and removes the three <s>doṣa</s>s.
It is a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative), gives strength, benefits the eyes, is absorbent, and is light.
<s>Mudgaparṇī</s> is <s>Kākaparṇī</s>, <s>Sūryaparṇī</s>, <s>Alpikā</s>, and <s>Sahā</s>.

children.text: kākamudgā ca sā proktā tathā mārjāragandhikā
children.translated_text: It is called <s>Kākamudgā</s> and also <s>Mārjāragandhikā</s>.

children.text: mudgaparṇī himā rūkṣā tiktā svāduśca śukralā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mudgaparṇī</s> is cold, dry, bitter, sweet, and semen-promoting.
It benefits the eyes, destroys wounds and swelling, is absorbent, and removes fever and burning.
It removes the three <s>doṣa</s>s, is light, and conquers <s>grahaṇī</s> disorder, piles, and diarrhea.

children.text: svarṇaṃ rūpyaṃ ca tāmraṃ ca raṅgaṃ yaśadameva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Svarṇa</s> (gold), <s>rūpya</s> (silver), <s>tāmra</s> (copper), <s>raṅga</s> (tin), and <s>yaśada</s> (zinc),

children.text: sīsaṃ lauhaṃ ca saptaite dhātavo girisambhavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: together with <s>sīsa</s> (lead) and <s>lauha</s> (iron), are these seven metals born from mountains.
Because they ward off wrinkles, gray hair, baldness, emaciation, weakness, old age, and diseases,

children.text: nivārya dehaṃ dadhati nṛṇāṃ taddhātavo matāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and sustain the bodies of people, they are regarded as <s>dhātu</s>s (supporting metals).
Long ago, <s>Jātavedas</s> saw the wives of the self-controlled <s>Saptarṣi</s>s staying in their own hermitage-sites.
They were endowed with the splendor of beauty and full youth.
<s>Jātavedas</s>' mind was overthrown by the pride of <s>Kandarpa</s>.
The semen that fell onto the surface of the earth became gold.
Artificial gold also comes about through the transmuting action of <s>rasendra</s> (mercury).

children.text: svarṇaṃ suvarṇaṃ kanakaṃ hiraṇyaṃ hema hāṭakam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Svarṇa</s>, <s>Suvarṇa</s>, <s>Kanaka</s>, <s>Hiraṇya</s>, <s>Hema</s>, and <s>Hāṭaka</s> are names for gold.

children.text: tapanīyaṃ ca gāṅgeyaṃ kaladhautaṃ ca kāñcanam
children.translated_text: So too are <s>Tapanīya</s>, <s>Gāṅgeya</s>, <s>Kaladhauta</s>, and <s>Kāñcana</s>.
Also <s>Cāmīkara</s>, <s>Śātakumbha</s>, and <s>Kārtasvara</s> are names for it.
<s>Jāmbūnada</s>, <s>Jātarūpa</s>, and <s>Mahārajata</s> are also names for gold.

children.text: dāhe raktaṃ sitaṃ chede nikaṣe kuṅkumaprabham
children.translated_text: Genuine gold is red when heated, white when cut, and saffron-colored on the touchstone.

children.text: tāraṃ śulbojjhitaṃ snigdhaṃ komalaṃ guru hema sat ||
children.translated_text: It is bright, free from copper, unctuous, soft, heavy, and true gold.

children.text: tacchvetaṃ kaṭhinaṃ rūkṣaṃ vivarṇaṃ samalaṃ dalam
children.translated_text: That gold which is white, hard, dry, discolored, impure, and brittle,

children.text: dāhe chede'sitaṃ śvetaṃ kaṣe tyājyaṃ laghu sphuṭam ||
children.translated_text: black when heated or cut, white on the touchstone, light, and cracked, should be rejected.

children.text: suvarṇaṃ śītalaṃ vṛṣyaṃ balyaṃ guru rasāyanam
children.translated_text: <s>Suvarṇa</s> is cooling, aphrodisiac, strengthening, heavy, and a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative).

children.text: svādu tiktaṃ ca tuvaraṃ pāke ca svādu picchilam ||
children.translated_text: It is sweet, bitter, and astringent; in post-digestive effect it is sweet and slimy.
It is nourishing, benefits the eyes, and gives intellect, memory, and understanding.
It is cordial, lengthens life, and produces luster, purity of speech, and firmness.
It conquers both kinds of poison, wasting, insanity, the three <s>doṣa</s>s, fever, and consumption.

children.text: balaṃ savīryaṃ harate narāṇāṃ rogavrajān poṣayatīha kāye
children.translated_text: Impure gold takes away people's strength along with their virility and nourishes hosts of diseases in the body.

children.text: asaukhyakṛccāpi sadā suvarṇamaśuddham etanmaraṇaṃ ca kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: It always causes discomfort, and this impure gold may also cause death.

children.text: asamyaṅmāritaṃ svarṇaṃ balaṃ vīryyaṃ ca nāśayet
children.translated_text: Gold that has not been properly incinerated destroys strength and virility.
It causes diseases and death; therefore one should incinerate it carefully.
For the destruction of <s>Tripura</s>, with unblinking eyes,
<s>Śiva</s>, filled with anger, gazed steadily.
At that time fire fell from one of his eyes.

children.text: tato rudraḥ samabhavad vaiśvānara iva jvalan ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rudra</s> arose, blazing like <s>Vaiśvānara</s>.
From the second eye, the left one, a tear-drop fell.
From that silver arose; it should be used in the prescribed operations.
It can also be artificial, for that results from admixture with tin and other metallic substances.

children.text: rūpyaṃ tu rajataṃ tāraṃ candrakānti sitaprabham ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rūpya</s> is <s>rajata</s> and <s>tāra</s>, moon-bright and white-shining.

children.text: snigdhaṃ mṛdu śvetaṃ dāhe chede ghanakṣamam
children.translated_text: It is unctuous, soft, white, and capable of withstanding burning, cutting, and hammering.

children.text: varṇāḍhyaṃ candravat svacchaṃ rūpyaṃ navaguṇaṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: Rich in color and clear like the moon, such auspicious <s>rūpya</s> has nine qualities.

children.text: kaṭhinaṃ kṛtrimaṃ rūkṣaṃ raktaṃ pītadalaṃ laghu
children.translated_text: Hard, artificial, rough, red, yellow-flaked, and light,
and spoiled by burning, cutting, and hammering: this is declared to be bad <s>rūpya</s>.
<s>Rūpya</s> is cooling, astringent and sour, has a sweet post-digestive taste, and is mobile/laxative.
It sustains youth, is unctuous and scraping, and conquers vāta and pitta.
It surely destroys prameha and related diseases very quickly.

children.text: tāraṃ śarīrasya karoti tāpaṃ vidhvaṃsanaṃ yacchati śukranāśam
children.translated_text: Impure <s>tāra</s> heats the body, brings destruction, and causes loss of semen.

children.text: vīryaṃ balaṃ hanti tanośca puṣṭiṃ mahāgadānpoṣayati hyaśuddham ||
children.translated_text: It destroys virility, strength, and bodily nourishment, and indeed nourishes grave diseases.
The semen of <s>Kārttikeya</s> that fell upon the surface of the earth,
from that <s>tāmra</s> arose: so say those who know ancient lore.
<s>Tāmra</s> is remembered as <s>audumbara</s>, <s>śulba</s>, and also <s>udumbara</s>.
It is <s>ravipriya</s>, <s>mlecchamukha</s>, and is named with synonyms of the sun.
Copper resembling a hibiscus flower, unctuous, soft, and able to withstand hammering,
free from iron and lead, is praised for calcination.

children.text: kṛṣṇaṃ rūkṣam atistabdhaṃ śvetaṃ cāpi ghanāsaham
children.translated_text: Black, rough, very rigid, white, and unable to withstand hammering,
and mixed with iron and lead: such <s>śulba</s> is declared defective.

children.text: tāmraṃ kaṣāyaṃ madhuraṃ ca tiktamamlaṃ ca pāke kaṭu sārakaṃ ca
children.translated_text: <s>Tāmra</s> is astringent, sweet and bitter, sour, pungent in post-digestive effect, and purgative.

children.text: pittāpahaṃ śleṣmaharaṃ ca śītaṃ tadropaṇaṃ syāllaghu lekhanaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: It removes pitta and phlegm, is cooling, heals wounds, and is light and scraping.
It removes anemia, abdominal disease, piles, fever, skin disease, cough, dyspnea, wasting, coryza, and acid dyspepsia.

children.text: śothaṃ kṛmiṃ śūlamapākaroti prāhuḥ pare bṛṃhaṇam alpametam ||
children.translated_text: It removes swelling, worms, and colic; others say that it is slightly nourishing.

children.text: eko doṣo viṣe tāmre tvasamyaṅmārite'ṣṭa te
children.translated_text: In improperly calcined <s>tāmra</s> there is a poisonous fault; these eight effects arise:
burning, sweating, loss of appetite, fainting, excess moisture, purging, vomiting, and dizziness.

children.text: raṅgaṃ vaṅgaṃ trapu proktaṃ tathā piccaṭamityapi
children.translated_text: <s>Raṅga</s>, <s>vaṅga</s>, and <s>trapu</s> are stated, and likewise <s>piccaṭa</s>.
<s>Vaṅga</s> is said to be of two kinds: <s>kṣuraka</s> and <s>miśraka</s>.

children.text: uttamaṃ kṣurakaṃ tatra miśrakaṃ tvavaraṃ matam ||
children.translated_text: Of these, <s>kṣuraka</s> is best, while <s>miśraka</s> is considered inferior.
<s>Raṅga</s> is light, mobile/laxative, dry, and hot; it destroys urinary disorders, kapha, and worms.

children.text: nihanti pāṇḍuṃ saśvāsaṃ cakṣuṣyaṃ pittalaṃ manāk ||
children.translated_text: It removes anemia accompanied by dyspnea, is good for the eyes, and slightly increases pitta.

children.text: siṃho yathā hastigaṇaṃ nihanti tathaiva vaṅgo'khilamehavargam
children.translated_text: Just as a lion kills a herd of elephants, so <s>vaṅga</s> kills the whole class of urinary disorders.

children.text: dehasya saukhyaṃ prabalendriyatvaṃ narasya puṣṭiṃ vidadhāti nūnam ||
children.translated_text: It surely brings bodily ease, strong senses, and nourishment to a person.
<s>Yasada</s> resembles <s>raṅga</s> and is considered the cause of <s>rīti</s> (brass).
<s>Yasada</s> is astringent, bitter, cooling, and removes kapha and pitta.

children.text: cakṣuṣyaṃ paramaṃ mehānpāṇḍuṃ śvāsaṃ ca nāśayet ||
children.translated_text: It is supremely good for the eyes and destroys urinary disorders, anemia, and dyspnea.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā bhogisutāṃ ramyāṃ vāsukistu mumoca yat ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Vāsuki</s> saw the lovely daughter of a serpent, he emitted his semen.
From that semen <s>nāga</s> arose, remover of all diseases of men.

children.text: sīsaṃ bradhnaṃ ca vapraṃ ca yogeṣṭaṃ nāganāmakam
children.translated_text: <s>Sīsa</s>, <s>bradhna</s>, <s>vapra</s>, and <s>yogeṣṭa</s> are names of <s>nāga</s>.
<s>Sīsa</s> should be known to have the qualities of <s>raṅga</s>, with special power to destroy urinary disorders.

children.text: nāgastu nāgaśatatulyabalaṃ dadāti vyādhiṃ vināśayati jīvanamātanoti
children.translated_text: <s>Nāga</s> gives strength equal to a hundred nāgas, destroys disease, and extends life.

children.text: vahniṃ pradīpayati kāmabalaṃ karoti mṛtyuṃ ca nāśayati saṃtatasevitaḥ saḥ ||
children.translated_text: When used continually, it kindles digestive fire, produces sexual power, and destroys death.

children.text: pākena hīnau kila vaṅganāgau kuṣṭhāni gulmāṃśca tathātikaṣṭān
children.translated_text: If <s>vaṅga</s> and <s>nāga</s> are deficient in processing, they cause skin diseases and very painful gulma tumors.
When administered, they also cause itching, prameha, vāta debility, swelling, fistula-in-ano, and the like.
In ancient times, when the <s>Lomin</s> demons were slain by the gods in battle,
various forms of iron arose from their bodies.
The word <s>loha</s> is not feminine; it is called <s>śastraka</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, <s>piṇḍa</s>, <s>kālāyasa</s>, and <s>āyasī</s>.
Heaviness, hardness, excessive moistening, <s>jammala</s> impurity, and burning action,
stone-like defect and very bad smell: these are the seven defects of iron.

children.text: lohaṃ tiktaṃ saraṃ śītaṃ madhuraṃ tuvaraṃ guru
children.translated_text: <s>Loha</s> is bitter, mobile/laxative, cooling, sweet, astringent, and heavy.

children.text: rūkṣaṃ vayasyaṃ cakṣuṣyaṃ lekhanaṃ vātalaṃ jayet ||
children.translated_text: It is dry, age-sustaining, good for the eyes, and scraping; it conquers vāta disorders.
It conquers kapha, pitta, poison, colic, swelling, piles, spleen disease, and anemia,
as well as fat disorders, urinary disorders, worms, and skin disease; its slag acts just the same.
Impure <s>loha</s> causes impotence, skin disease, illness, and death; it produces heart disease, colic, and stones.

children.text: nānārujānāṃ ca tathā prakopaṃ karoti hṛllāsamaśuddhaloham ||
children.translated_text: It also provokes many kinds of pain and causes nausea.

children.text: jīvahāri madakāri cāyasaṃ ced aśuddhimadasaṃskṛtaṃ dhruvam
children.translated_text: If iron is impure and unprocessed, it is surely life-taking and intoxicating.

children.text: pāṭavaṃ na tanute śarīrake dāruṇāṃ hṛdi rujāṃ ca yacchati ||
children.translated_text: It does not produce sharpness in the body and gives terrible pain in the heart.

children.text: kuṣmāṇḍaṃ tilatailaṃ ca māṣānnaṃ rājikāṃ tathā
children.translated_text: One who uses <s>loha</s> should avoid ash gourd, sesame oil, food of black gram, and mustard,
as well as liquor and sour flavors.
When pieces of iron smeared with sour liquid have forms like mountain peaks,
and fine particles appear there in the iron, that is called <s>sāra</s>.
Iron called <s>sāra</s> destroys grahaṇī disease and diarrhea.

children.text: ardhaṃ sarvāṅgajaṃ vātaṃ śūlaṃ ca pariṇāmajam
children.translated_text: It removes vāta affecting half the body or the whole body, and colic arising at digestion,

children.text: chardiṃ ca pīnasaṃ pittaṃ śvāsaṃ kāsaṃ vyapohati ||
children.translated_text: as well as vomiting, coryza, pitta disorders, dyspnea, and cough.

children.text: yatpātre na prasarati jale tailabinduḥ pratapte hiṅgurgandhaṃ tyajati ca nijaṃ tiktatāṃ nimbavalkaḥ
children.translated_text: In a vessel in which a drop of oil does not spread on water, heated asafoetida gives up its own smell and neem bark its bitterness;

children.text: taptaṃ dugdhaṃ bhavati śikharākārakaṃ naiti bhūmikṛṣṇāṅgaḥ syātsajalacaṇakaḥ kāntalohaṃ taduktam ||
children.translated_text: heated milk becomes peak-shaped and does not sink to the ground, and a wet chickpea becomes black-bodied: that is called <s>kānta-loha</s>.
<s>Kānta</s> iron removes gulma tumors, abdominal disease, piles, colic, āma, āmavāta, and fistula-in-ano,
as well as jaundice, swelling, skin diseases, and wasting disease.
It overcomes splenic disease, amlapitta, liver disease, and headache as well;

children.text: sarvān rogān vijayate kāntalohaṃ na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kāntaloha</s> conquers all diseases, without doubt.
It gives strength, virility, and bodily nourishment, and it increases digestive fire.
The slag of iron that is being smelted is called <s>Maṇḍūra</s>.
<s>Lohasiṃhānikā</s>, <s>Kiṭṭī</s>, and <s>Siṃhāna</s> are also named for that iron slag.
For whatever metal has whatever qualities described, its slag too has those same qualities.
The seven sub-metals are <s>Svarṇamākṣika</s>, <s>Tāramākṣika</s>,

children.text: tutthaṃ kāṃsyaṃ ca rītiśca sindūraśca śilājatu ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tuttha</s>, <s>Kāṃsya</s>, <s>Rīti</s>, <s>Sindūra</s>, and <s>Śilājatu</s>.
In all the sub-metals, the qualities of the corresponding metals are also present;
but in them those qualities are secondary, because the share of that metal is small.
<s>Svarṇamākṣika</s> is called <s>Tāpīja</s> and <s>Madhumākṣika</s>.
It is remembered as <s>Tāpya</s>, <s>Mākṣikadhātu</s>, and <s>Madhudhātu</s>.
Because of a slight association with gold, it is called <s>Svarṇamākṣika</s>.
It is a sub-metal of gold, endowed with some of gold's qualities.
Thus, when gold is unavailable, <s>Svarṇamākṣika</s> is administered.
But because it is only a substitute for it, its qualities are somewhat inferior to that.
Not merely the qualities of gold exist in <s>Svarṇamākṣika</s>;
for, because of association with another substance, there are other qualities as well.
<s>Svarṇamākṣika</s> is sweet, bitter, aphrodisiac, and rejuvenating.
It benefits the eyes and removes bladder pain, skin disease, pallor, urinary disorders, poison, and abdominal disease;
it destroys piles, swelling, poison, itching, and even the three doṣas.
This <s>Tāpīja</s>, when unpurified, causes weak digestive fire, severe loss of strength, constipation, eye disorders together with skin diseases,

children.text: tathaiva mālāṃ vraṇapūrvikāṃ ca karoti tāpījamaśuddhametat ||
children.translated_text: and likewise glandular lesions preceded by sores.
<s>Tāramākṣika</s> is another kind; it is like silver.
Because of a slight association with silver, it is called <s>Tāramākṣika</s>.
Since it is a substitute for it, its qualities are therefore remembered as inferior.
For <s>Tāramākṣika</s> does not have only the qualities of silver.

children.text: svādu pāke rase kiṃcit tiktaṃ vṛṣyaṃ rasāyanam
children.translated_text: It is sweet in post-digestive effect and taste, slightly bitter, aphrodisiac, and rejuvenating.
It benefits the eyes and removes bladder pain, skin disease, pallor, urinary disease, poison, and abdominal disease;

children.text: arśaḥ śothaṃ kṣayaṃ kaṇḍūṃ tridoṣamapi nāśayet ||
children.translated_text: it destroys piles, swelling, wasting disease, itching, and even the three doṣas.
This <s>Tāpīja</s> too, when unpurified, causes weak digestive fire, severe loss of strength, constipation, eye disorders together with skin diseases,

children.text: tathaiva mālāṃ vraṇapūrvikāṃ ca karoti tāpījamidaṃ ca tadvat ||
children.translated_text: and likewise glandular lesions preceded by sores; it acts in that same way.
<s>Tuttha</s> is also <s>Vitunnaka</s>, <s>Śikhigrīva</s>, and <s>Mayūraka</s>.
<s>Tuttha</s> is indeed the sub-metal of copper, for it has some copper in it.

children.text: kiṃcit tāmraguṇaṃ tasmād vakṣyamāṇaguṇaṃ ca tat
children.translated_text: Therefore it has some copper qualities, and also the qualities that are about to be stated.

children.text: tutthakaṃ kaṭukaṃ kṣāraṃ kaṣāyaṃ vāmakaṃ laghu ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tutthaka</s> is pungent, alkaline, astringent, emetic, and light.
It is scraping, breaking, cooling, beneficial to the eyes, and removes kapha and pitta.
It destroys poison, stones, skin disease, and itching; <s>Kharpara</s> too has those same qualities.
<s>Kāṃsya</s>, born from copper and tin, is called <s>Ghoṣa</s> and <s>Kaṃsaka</s>.
<s>Kāṃsya</s> is a sub-metal belonging to the two, copper and tin.

children.text: kāṃsyasya tu guṇā jñeyāḥ svayonisadṛśā janaiḥ
children.translated_text: People should understand the qualities of <s>Kāṃsya</s> as similar to the sources from which it comes;
through the effect born of their combination, other qualities of it are remembered as well.

children.text: kāṃsyaṃ kaṣāyaṃ tiktoṣṇaṃ lekhanaṃ viśadaṃ saram
children.translated_text: <s>Kāṃsya</s> is astringent, bitter, hot, scraping, clear, and flowing.
It is heavy, beneficial for the eyes, dry, and an excellent remover of kapha and pitta.

children.text: pīttalaṃ tvārakūṭaṃ syād ārī rītiśca kathyate
children.translated_text: <s>Pittala</s> is <s>Ārakūṭa</s>; it is called <s>Ārī</s> and <s>Rīti</s>.
It is also <s>Rājarīti</s>, <s>Brahmarīti</s>, <s>Kapilā</s>, and <s>Piṅgalā</s>.
<s>Rīti</s> too is a sub-metal of copper and zinc.
People should understand the qualities of <s>Pittala</s> as similar to its sources;
through the effect born of combination, other qualities of it too are remembered.

children.text: rītikāyugalaṃ rūkṣaṃ tiktaṃ ca lavaṇaṃ rase
children.translated_text: The two varieties of <s>Rītikā</s> are dry, and bitter and salty in taste.
They are purifying, cure pallor, kill worms, and are not excessively scraping.
<s>Sindūra</s> is <s>Raktareṇu</s>, <s>Nāgagarbha</s>, and <s>Sīsaja</s>, born from lead.
<s>Sindūra</s> is the sub-metal of lead; by its qualities it is considered like that lead.
Through the effect born of combination, other qualities of it too are remembered.
<s>Sindūra</s> is hot and removes erysipelas, skin disease, itching, and poison.
It causes the joining of fractures and cleanses and heals wounds.
In summer, when mountains are heated by the heat, they release the essence of metals
like an exudation; that is called <s>Śilājatu</s>.
It is fourfold: gold, silver, copper, and iron.
It is also called <s>Śilājatu</s>, <s>Adrijatu</s>, and <s>Śailaniryāsa</s>.
It is <s>Gaireya</s>, <s>Aśmaja</s>, <s>Girija</s>, and <s>Śailadhātuja</s> as well.
<s>Śilāja</s> is pungent, bitter, hot, pungent in post-digestive effect, and rejuvenating.
It is cutting and a carrier of other medicines; it destroys kapha, urinary disease, stones, and gravel,

children.text: mūtrakṛcchraṃ kṣayaṃ śvāsaṃ vātārśāṃsi ca pāṇḍutām ||
children.translated_text: dysuria, wasting disease, dyspnea, vāta-type piles, and pallor,
as well as epilepsy, madness, swelling, skin disease, abdominal disease, and worms.
The gold variety has the color of a hibiscus flower because of that essence.

children.text: madhuraṃ kaṭu tiktaṃ ca śītakaṃ kaṭupāki ca ||
children.translated_text: It is sweet, pungent, and bitter, cooling, and pungent in post-digestive effect.

children.text: rājataṃ pāṇḍuraṃ śītaṃ kaṭukaṃ svādupāki ca
children.translated_text: The silver variety is pale, cooling, pungent, and sweet in post-digestive effect.
The copper variety has the appearance of a peacock's neck and is sharp and hot.
The iron variety has the appearance of <s>Jaṭāyu</s>'s wing; it is bitter and salty.
It is pungent in post-digestive effect, cooling, and declared the best of all.
Because <s>Pārada</s> is used as <s>rasa</s> by people seeking <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation),

children.text: tato rasa iti proktaḥ sa ca dhāturapi smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore it is called <s>Rasa</s>; it too is remembered as a metal.
The semen that slipped from <s>Śiva</s>'s body fell upon the surface of the earth;
because it arose from the essence of his body, it became white and clear.
<s>Śivavīrya</s> should be understood as fourfold according to the difference of its source.

children.text: śvetaṃ raktaṃ tathā pītaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ tattu bhavetkramāt ||
children.translated_text: It is white, red, yellow, and black, respectively.

children.text: brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo vaiśyaḥ śūdraśca khalu jātitaḥ
children.translated_text: By birth it is indeed <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Kṣatriya</s>, <s>Vaiśya</s>, and <s>Śūdra</s>.

children.text: śvetaṃ śastaṃ rujāṃ nāśe raktaṃ kila rasāyane
children.translated_text: The white is praised for destroying diseases, and the red, it is said, for <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation).

children.text: dhātuvāde tu tatpītaṃ khegatau kṛṣṇameva ca ||
children.translated_text: The yellow is for <s>dhātuvāda</s> (metal transmutation), and the black precisely for <s>khegati</s> (aerial motion).
<s>Pārada</s>, <s>rasadhātu</s>, <s>rasendra</s>, and <s>mahārasa</s> are names for mercury.
<s>Capala</s>, <s>Śivavīrya</s>, <s>rasa</s>, <s>sūta</s>, and <s>Śivāhvaya</s> are also names for it.
<s>Pārada</s> has the six tastes, is unctuous, destroys the three <s>doṣa</s>s, and is a <s>rasāyana</s>.
It carries the effect of compounds, is highly aphrodisiac, and always gives eyesight and strength.
It is said to remove every disease, and especially to destroy all kinds of <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin disease).

children.text: svastho raso bhavedbrahmā baddho jñeyo janārdanaḥ
children.translated_text: Mercury in its normal state is <s>Brahmā</s>; when bound, it should be known as <s>Janārdana</s>.
When colored and made to penetrate, it is the god <s>Maheśvara</s> himself.

children.text: mūrchito harati rujaṃ bandhanamanubhūya khegatiṃ kurute
children.translated_text: When stupefied, it removes disease; after undergoing binding, it produces <s>khegati</s>.

children.text: ajarīkaroti hi mṛtaḥ ko'nyaḥ karuṇākaraḥ sūtāt ||
children.translated_text: When killed, it makes one free from old age; what other benefactor is there besides <s>sūta</s>?

children.text: asādhyo yo bhavedrogo yasya nāsti cikitsitam
children.translated_text: Whatever disease may be incurable, for which there is no treatment,
<s>rasendra</s> destroys that disease in humans, elephants, and horses.

children.text: malaṃ viṣaṃ vahnigiritvacāpalaṃ naisargikaṃ doṣamuśanti pārade
children.translated_text: In mercury they declare impurity, poison, fire, <s>giri</s>, and instability to be natural defects.

children.text: upādhijau dvau trapunāgayogajau doṣau rasendre kathitau munīśvaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The lordly sages have described two adventitious defects in <s>rasendra</s>, born from contact with tin and lead.

children.text: malena mūrcchā maraṇaṃ viṣeṇa dāho'gninā kaṣṭataraḥ śarīre
children.translated_text: From impurity comes stupor; from poison, death; from fire, a very painful burning in the body.

children.text: dehasya jāḍyaṃ giriṇā sadā syāccāñcalyato vīryahṛtiśca puṃsām
children.translated_text: From <s>giri</s> there is always dullness of the body, and from instability there is loss of virility in men.

children.text: vaṅgena kuṣṭhaṃ bhujagena ṣaṇḍho bhavedato'sau pariśodhanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From tin comes <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and from lead one becomes impotent; therefore this mercury must be thoroughly purified.

children.text: vahnir viṣaṃ malaṃ ceti mukhyā doṣāstrayo rase
children.translated_text: Fire, poison, and impurity: these are the three principal defects in mercury.

children.text: ete kurvanti santāpaṃ mṛtiṃ mūrchāṃ nṛṇāṃ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: They cause burning distress, death, and stupor in people, respectively.

children.text: anye'pi kathitā doṣā bhiṣagbhiḥ pārade yadi
children.translated_text: Even if other defects in mercury have been described by physicians,
nevertheless these three defects in particular must be removed.

children.text: saṃskārahīnaṃ khalu sūtarājaṃ yaḥ sevate tasya karoti bādhām
children.translated_text: The king <s>sūta</s>, when devoid of processing, surely causes affliction to the person who consumes it.

children.text: dehasya nāśaṃ vidadhāti nūnaṃ kaṣṭāṃśca rogāñjanayennarāṇām ||
children.translated_text: It certainly brings about destruction of the body and produces severe diseases in people.

children.text: gandho hiṅgulamabhratālakaśilāḥ sroto'ñjanaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ rājāvartakacumbakau sphaṭikayā śaṅkhaḥ khaṭīgairikam
children.translated_text: Sulfur, cinnabar, mica, orpiment, realgar, collyrium, borax, <s>rājāvarta</s>, lodestone, crystal, conch shell, chalk, and red ocher,

children.text: kāsīsaṃ rasakaṃ kapardasikatābolāśca kaṅkuṣṭhakaṃ saurāṣṭrī ca matā amī uparasāḥ sūtasya kiṃcidguṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: green vitriol, calamine, cowrie, sand, <s>bolā</s>, <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, and <s>saurāṣṭrī</s>: these are considered the subsidiary minerals of <s>sūta</s>, possessing some of its qualities.
<s>Hiṅgula</s> is called <s>darada</s>, <s>mleccha</s>, <s>hiṅgulī</s>, and <s>cūrṇapārada</s>.
<s>Darada</s> is said to be threefold: <s>carmāra</s> and <s>śukatuṇḍaka</s>,
with <s>haṃsapāda</s> as the third; each later one is better in quality.
<s>Carmāra</s> is white in color, while <s>śukatuṇḍaka</s> is yellowish.
<s>Haṃsapāda</s>, resembling a hibiscus flower, is the very best.

children.text: tiktaṃ kaṣāyaṃ kaṭu hiṅgulaṃ syānnetrāmayaghnaṃ kaphapittahāri
children.translated_text: <s>Hiṅgula</s> is bitter, astringent, and pungent; it destroys eye diseases and removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
It destroys nausea, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, fever, jaundice, spleen disease, <s>āmavāta</s>, and <s>gara</s> poison.
When <s>hiṅgula</s> is cooked in a <s>ḍamaru</s> apparatus by the method of upward sublimation,

children.text: hiṅgulaṃ tasya sūtaṃ tu śuddhameva na śodhayet ||
children.translated_text: the mercury from it is already pure and should not be purified further.
Long ago on <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>, as <s>Devī</s> was playing, her silk garment was stained with menstrual blood.
With that garment she bathed in the ocean of milk.
From the menstrual fluid that flowed from it, sulfur then came into being.
<s>Gandhaka</s>, <s>gandhika</s>, and <s>gandhapāṣāṇa</s> are names for sulfur.
It is also called <s>saugandhika</s>, <s>bali</s>, and <s>balarasa</s>.

children.text: caturdhā gandhakaḥ prokto raktaḥ pītaḥ sito'sitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Sulfur is said to be fourfold: red, yellow, white, and black.
The red is fit for making gold, and the yellow for <s>rasāyana</s>.
The white is for application on wounds and the like; the black is the best and very hard to obtain.
Sulfur is pungent and bitter, hot in potency, astringent, and mobile.
It increases <s>pitta</s>, is pungent in post-digestive effect, and conquers worms, itching, and erysipelas.
As a <s>rasāyana</s>, it destroys <s>kuṣṭha</s>, wasting, spleen disease, <s>kapha</s>, and <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: aśodhito gandhaka eṣa kuṣṭhaṃ karoti tāpaṃ viṣamaṃ śarīre
children.translated_text: This sulfur, when unpurified, causes <s>kuṣṭha</s> and irregular burning heat in the body.

children.text: saukhyaṃ ca rūpaṃ ca balaṃ tathaujaḥ śukraṃ nihantyeva karoti cāsram ||
children.translated_text: It destroys ease, beauty, strength, vigor, and semen, and it also causes bleeding.

children.text: purā vadhāya vṛtrasya vajriṇā vajram uddhṛtam
children.translated_text: Long ago, for the killing of <s>Vṛtra</s>, the <s>Vajrin</s> raised his thunderbolt.
Then sparks from it moved about through the sky.
With a dense roar they fell upon the peaks of mountains.
From those very sparks, mica arose in those various mountains.
It is called <s>vajra</s> because it is born from the thunderbolt, and <s>abhra</s> because it arose from the roar of clouds.

children.text: gaganātskhalitaṃ yasmād gaganaṃ ca tato matam ||
children.translated_text: Since it slipped down from the sky, it is therefore also called <s>gagana</s>.
By the divisions of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Kṣatriya</s>, <s>Vaiśya</s>, and <s>Śūdra</s>, it is fourfold.

children.text: krameṇaiva sitaṃ raktaṃ pītaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ ca varṇataḥ ||
children.translated_text: In color, respectively, it is white, red, yellow, and black.

children.text: praśasyate sitaṃ tāre raktaṃ tattu rasāyane
children.translated_text: The white is praised for silver, and the red for <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: pītaṃ hemani kṛṣṇaṃ tu gadeṣu drutaye'pi ca ||
children.translated_text: The yellow is for gold, while the black is for diseases and also for liquefaction.

children.text: pinākaṃ darduraṃ nāgaṃ vajraṃ ceti caturvidham
children.translated_text: It is fourfold as <s>pināka</s>, <s>dardura</s>, <s>nāga</s>, and <s>vajra</s>.
<s>Pināka</s>, when thrown into fire, releases a mass of flakes.
Eating it out of ignorance causes severe <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
<s>Dardura</s>, when thrown into fire, makes a frog-like sound.
After forming many globules, it becomes a giver of death.
<s>Nāga</s>, like a serpent, emits a hiss in the fire.

children.text: tad bhakṣitam avaśyaṃ tu vidadhāti bhagandaram
children.translated_text: When eaten, it certainly produces fistula-in-ano.
<s>Vajra</s> stands firm like a diamond and does not undergo alteration in fire.
Among all kinds of <s>abhra</s> (mica), <s>vajra</s>-mica is the best; it removes disease, old age, and death.
Mica produced in the northern mountains has abundant essence and is superior in qualities.
That which comes from the southern mountain has little essence and bestows few qualities.

children.text: abhraṃ kaṣāyaṃ madhuraṃ suśītamāyuṣkaraṃ dhātuvivarddhanaṃ ca
children.translated_text: <s>Abhra</s> is astringent, sweet, very cooling, life-promoting, and increases the bodily tissues.
It destroys the three <s>doṣa</s>s, wounds, fat-disorders, skin disease, spleen disease, abdominal disease, tumors, poison, and worms.

children.text: rogān hanti draḍhayati vapur vīryavṛddhiṃ vidhatte tāruṇyāḍhyaṃ ramayati śataṃ yoṣitāṃ nityameva
children.translated_text: Incinerated <s>abhra</s> destroys diseases, strengthens the body, increases virility, and, endowed with youthfulness, enables one constantly to enjoy a hundred women.

children.text: dīrghāyuṣkāñjanayati sutān vikramaiḥ siṃhatulyān mṛtyorbhītiṃ harati satataṃ sevyamānaṃ mṛtābhram ||
children.translated_text: It produces long-lived sons equal to lions in valor and continually removes the fear of death when it is used.

children.text: pīḍāṃ vidhatte vividhāṃ narāṇāṃ kuṣṭhaṃ kṣayaṃ pāṇḍugadaṃ ca śotham
children.translated_text: Impure <s>abhra</s> causes various pains in people, skin disease, wasting, pallor, and swelling.

children.text: hṛtpārśvapīḍāṃ ca karotyaśuddhamabhraṃ tvaśuddhaṃ guru tāpadaṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: It also causes pain in the heart and sides; impure mica is heavy and a giver of suffering.
<s>Haritāla</s> is also called <s>tāla</s>, <s>āla</s>, and <s>tālaka</s>.
<s>Haritāla</s> is said to be of two kinds: the leaf-like kind and the lump-like kind.

children.text: tayorādyaṃ guṇaiḥ śreṣṭhaṃ tato hīnaguṇaṃ param
children.translated_text: Of these, the first is superior in qualities; the other is inferior in qualities.
It is golden in color, heavy, unctuous, and layered like sheets of mica.
One should know this quality-rich <s>tālaka</s> as the leaf-like kind; it is a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative).
The sheetless, lump-like kind has little essence and is likewise heavy.
That lump-like <s>tālaka</s> suppresses women's menstrual flow and has few qualities.
<s>Haritāla</s> is pungent, unctuous, astringent, and hot, and it removes poison.
It removes itching, skin disease, mouth diseases, blood disorders, <s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, scalp disorders, and wounds.

children.text: harati ca haritālaṃ cārutāṃ dehajātāṃ sṛjati ca bahutāpaṃ cāṅgasaṅkocapīḍām
children.translated_text: Impure <s>haritāla</s>, or that which has been incinerated improperly, takes away the body's natural beauty and produces great heat and pain from contraction of the limbs.

children.text: vitarati kaphavātau kuṣṭharogaṃ vidadhyādidamaśitamaśuddhaṃ māritaṃ cāpyasamyak ||
children.translated_text: It increases <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s> and brings about skin disease.
<s>Manaḥśilā</s> is remembered as <s>manoguptā</s>, <s>manohvā</s>, and <s>nāgajihvikā</s>,

children.text: naipālī kunaṭī golā śilā divyauṣadhiḥ smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: and also as <s>naipālī</s>, <s>kunaṭī</s>, <s>golā</s>, <s>śilā</s>, and <s>divyauṣadhi</s>.
<s>Manaḥśilā</s> is heavy, complexion-promoting, mobile, hot, scraping, and pungent.
It is bitter and unctuous, and it removes poison, dyspnea, cough, possession disorders, <s>kapha</s>, and blood disorders.

children.text: manaḥśilā mandabalaṃ karoti jantuṃ dhruvaṃ śodhanam antareṇa
children.translated_text: Without purification, <s>manaḥśilā</s> certainly weakens a living being.

children.text: malānubandhaṃ kila mūtrarodhaṃ saśarkaraṃ kṛcchragadaṃ ca kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: It may cause retention of feces, urinary obstruction with gravel, and the disease of painful urination.
<s>Añjana</s> is also called <s>yāmuna</s> and <s>kāpotāñjana</s>.
Of it, the black variety is called <s>srotoñjana</s>, while the white is called <s>sauvīra</s>.
That which has the form of the peak of an anthill and, when broken, resembles collyrium,

children.text: ghṛṣṭaṃ tu gaurikākāram etat sroto'ñjanaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: but when rubbed has the appearance of yellow ochre, is remembered as <s>sroto'ñjana</s>.
<s>Sauvīra</s> should be known as similar to <s>srotoñjana</s>, but it is pale.
<s>Srotoñjana</s> is considered sweet, beneficial for the eyes, and a remover of <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
It is astringent, scraping, unctuous, absorbent, and removes vomiting and poison.
It removes <s>sidhmā</s>, wasting, and blood disorders; it is cooling and should always be used by the wise.
All the qualities of <s>srotoñjana</s> are also accepted by the wise in <s>sauvīra</s>.
But of the two collyriums, <s>srotoñjana</s> is remembered as the better.
<s>Ṭaṅkaṇa</s> kindles the digestive fire, is dry, destroys <s>kapha</s>, and increases <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>.

children.text: sphaṭī ca sphaṭikā proktā śvetā śubhrā ca raṅgadā
children.translated_text: <s>Sphaṭī</s> is also called <s>sphaṭikā</s>, <s>śvetā</s>, <s>śubhrā</s>, and <s>raṅgadā</s>.
It is also called <s>dṛḍharaṅgā</s>, <s>raṅgadṛḍhā</s>, and <s>raṅgāṅgā</s>.
<s>Sphaṭikā</s> is astringent and hot, and it destroys <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, and wounds.
It destroys white leprosy and erysipelas and causes contraction of the vagina.
<s>Rājāvarta</s> is also <s>nṛpāvarta</s> and <s>rājanyāvartaka</s>,
and it is likewise named <s>āvartamaṇi</s> and <s>āvartta</s>.
<s>Rājāvarta</s> is pungent, bitter, cooling, and destroys <s>pitta</s>.
<s>Rājāvarta</s> destroys <s>prameha</s> and prevents vomiting and hiccup.
<s>Cumbaka</s> is <s>kāntapāṣāṇa</s>, <s>ayaskānta</s>, and <s>lohakarṣaka</s>.
<s>Cumbaka</s> is scraping and cooling, and it removes fat, poison, and chronic toxin.
<s>Gairika</s> is also <s>raktadhātu</s>, <s>gaireya</s>, and <s>girija</s>.
Another kind is <s>suvarṇagairika</s>, and it is redder than that.
Both kinds of <s>gairika</s> are unctuous, sweet, astringent, and cooling.
They benefit the eyes and remove burning, <s>pitta</s>, blood disorders, <s>kapha</s>, hiccup, and poison.

children.text: khaṭikā kaṭhinī cāpi lekhanī ca nigadyate
children.translated_text: <s>Khaṭikā</s> is also called <s>kaṭhinī</s> and <s>lekhanī</s>.
<s>Khaṭī</s> is cooling, conquers burning and blood disorders, is sweet, and conquers poison and swelling.
These qualities are stated for external application; when eaten, it is like clay.

children.text: khaṭī gaurakhaṭī dve ca guṇaistulye prakīrtite ||
children.translated_text: The two kinds, <s>khaṭī</s> and <s>gaurakhaṭī</s>, are said to be equal in qualities.

children.text: vālukā sikatā proktā śarkarā retajāpi ca
children.translated_text: <s>Vālukā</s> is called <s>sikatā</s>, <s>śarkarā</s>, and also <s>retajā</s>.
<s>Vālukā</s> is scraping and cooling, and it destroys wounds and injuries of the chest.

children.text: kharparī tutthakaṃ tutthād anyat tad rasakaṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: <s>Kharparī</s> is <s>tutthaka</s>; that which is different from <s>tuttha</s> is remembered as <s>rasaka</s>.

children.text: ye guṇāstutthake proktāste guṇā rasake smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The qualities that are stated for <s>tutthaka</s> are remembered as the qualities of <s>rasaka</s>.
<s>Kāśīśa</s> is also <s>dhātukāśīśa</s> and <s>pāṃśukāśīśa</s>.
That same substance, when somewhat yellow, is called <s>puṣpakāśīśa</s>.

children.text: kāśīśamamlamuṣṇaṃ ca tiktaṃ ca tuvaraṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Kāśīśa</s> is sour, hot, bitter, and also astringent.
It removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>, benefits the hair, and dispels eye disorders, itching, and poison.
It is declared to destroy dysuria, urinary stones, and white leprosy.
<s>Saurāṣṭrī</s> is called <s>tuvarī</s>, <s>kālī</s>, <s>mṛttālaka</s>, and <s>surāṣṭrajā</s>.

children.text: āḍhakī cāpi sā khyātā mṛtsnā ca suramṛttikā
children.translated_text: It is also known as <s>āḍhakī</s>, <s>mṛtsnā</s>, and <s>suramṛttikā</s>.

children.text: sphaṭikāyā guṇāḥ sarve saurāṣṭryā api kīrtitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: All the qualities of <s>sphaṭikā</s> are also taught for <s>saurāṣṭrī</s>.
<s>Mṛd</s>, <s>mṛdā</s>, <s>mṛttikā</s>, <s>mṛtsnā</s>, <s>kṣetrajā</s>, and <s>kṛṣṇamṛttikā</s> are names for clay.
Black clay removes wounds, burning, blood disorders, vaginal discharge, <s>śleṣman</s>, and <s>pitta</s>.
<s>Paṅka</s> is also <s>jalakalka</s>, <s>culuka</s>, <s>kardama</s>, and <s>mala</s>.
<s>Cikila</s>, <s>Palita</s>, <s>Drāpa</s>, <s>Palala</s>, and <s>Niṣadvara</s> are names of <s>Kardama</s>.
<s>Kardama</s> removes burning, <s>pitta</s>, blood disorders, and swelling; it is cooling and laxative.
<s>Kapardaka</s>, <s>Varāṭa</s>, <s>Kapardī</s>, and <s>Varāṭikā</s>
are names of <s>Kapardikā</s>, which is cooling, beneficial to the eyes, and removes eruptions and wasting.
It destroys ear discharge, weak digestion, <s>pitta</s>, blood disorders, and <s>kapha</s>.
<s>Śaṅkha</s>, <s>Samudraja</s>, <s>Kambu</s>, <s>Sunāda</s>, and <s>Pāvanadhvani</s> are names of conch.

children.text: śaṅkho netryo himaḥ śīto laghuḥ pittakaphāsrajit ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śaṅkha</s> benefits the eyes, is cooling, cold, and light, and conquers <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, and blood disorders.
<s>Bola</s>, <s>Gandharasa</s>, <s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>Piṇḍa</s>, and <s>Goparasa</s> are the same substance.
<s>Bola</s> removes blood disorders, is cooling, promotes intellect, kindles appetite, and aids digestion.
It is sweet, pungent, and bitter, and conquers burning, sweating, and the three <s>doṣa</s>s.
It removes fever, epilepsy, and skin disease, and purifies the womb.
<s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s> grows on the lower peaks of the <s>Himavat</s>.
Of it, one kind is red-black, while the other is remembered as <s>Aṇḍaka</s>.
The first <s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, yellow in appearance, heavy, and unctuous, is the best.

children.text: śyāmaṃ pītaṃ laghu tyaktasattvaṃ neṣṭaṃ tathāṇḍakam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Aṇḍaka</s>, dark or yellow, light, and devoid of essence, is not desired.
<s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, <s>Kākakuṣṭha</s>, <s>Viraṅga</s>, and <s>Kolakākula</s> are its names.
<s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is purgative, bitter, pungent and hot, and improves the complexion.
It removes worms, swelling, abdominal disease, distension, <s>gulma</s> (abdominal lump), constipation, and <s>kapha</s>.
Because all people who seek wealth take very great delight in it,
therefore experts in the science of words have called it <s>ratna</s> (gem).

children.text: ratnaṃ klībe maṇiḥ puṃsi striyāmapi nigadyate
children.translated_text: <s>Ratna</s> is neuter, <s>maṇi</s> is masculine, and it is also stated in the feminine.
It is a kind of stone, and pearl and the like are so called.
The gems are <s>Gārutmata</s>, <s>Puṣparāga</s>, and <s>Māṇikya</s>,
as well as <s>Indranīla</s>, <s>Gomeda</s>, and also <s>Vaidūrya</s>;
with <s>Mauktika</s> and <s>Vidruma</s>, these are indeed declared to be the nine gems.
<s>Muktāphala</s>, <s>Hīraka</s>, <s>Vaidūrya</s>, and <s>Padmarāga</s>,

children.text: puṣparāgaṃ ca gomedaṃ nīlaṃ gārutmataṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Puṣparāga</s>, <s>Gomeda</s>, <s>Nīla</s>, and likewise <s>Gārutmata</s>,
together with <s>Pravāla</s>: these indeed are the nine great gems.

children.text: hīrakaḥ puṃsi vajro'strī candro maṇivaraśca saḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Hīraka</s> is masculine, <s>Vajra</s> is not feminine, and it is also <s>Candra</s> and <s>Maṇivara</s>.

children.text: sa tu śvetaḥ smṛto vipro lohitaḥ kṣattriyaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: That diamond, when white, is remembered as a <s>vipra</s> (Brahmin); when red, it is remembered as a <s>kṣattriya</s>.
When yellow it is a <s>vaiśya</s>, when black a <s>śūdra</s>; thus it has the nature of the four classes.
In <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative therapy), the <s>vipra</s> type is approved and grants all accomplishments.
The <s>kṣattriya</s> type destroys disease and is remembered as removing old age and death.
The <s>vaiśya</s> type is said to give wealth and to make the body firm.

children.text: śūdro nāśayati vyādhīn vayaḥstambhaṃ karoti ca ||
children.translated_text: The <s>śūdra</s> type destroys diseases and arrests aging.
Here the male, female, and neuter types are to be recognized by their marks.
Those that are well rounded, complete in body, endowed with brilliance, and rather large
are called male, being free from lines and spots.
Those provided with lines and spots and having six angles are remembered as female.
Those that are triangular and very long are to be known as neuter.
Among these, the male ones are best and effect the binding of <s>rasa</s> (mercury).

children.text: striyaḥ kurvanti kāyasya kāntiṃ strīṇāṃ sukhapradāḥ
children.translated_text: The female ones produce radiance of the body and give pleasure to women.
The neuter ones are without potency, without desire, and devoid of essence.

children.text: striyaḥ strībhyaḥ pradātavyāḥ klībaṃ klībe prayojayet
children.translated_text: Female ones should be given to women; the neuter should be applied to neuters.
Male ones, which increase virility, should always be given to everyone.

children.text: aśuddhaṃ kurute vajraṃ kuṣṭhaṃ pārśvavyathāṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Unpurified diamond produces skin disease and pain in the side,
as well as pallor and lameness; therefore one should purify it and incinerate it.

children.text: āyuḥ puṣṭiṃ balaṃ vīryaṃ varṇaṃ saukhyaṃ karoti ca
children.translated_text: When used, incinerated diamond produces long life, nourishment, strength, virility, complexion, and comfort.

children.text: sevitaṃ sarvarogaghnaṃ mṛtaṃ vajraṃ na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It removes all diseases; of this there is no doubt.
<s>Gārutmata</s>, <s>Marakata</s>, <s>Aśmagarbha</s>, and <s>Harinmaṇi</s> are names of emerald.
<s>Māṇikya</s> is <s>Padmarāga</s>, the red gem, and <s>Lohita</s>.
<s>Puṣparāga</s> is <s>Mañjumaṇi</s> and is dear to <s>Vācaspati</s>.
<s>Nīla</s> is also <s>Indranīla</s>, and <s>Gomeda</s> is <s>Pītaratnaka</s>.
<s>Vaidūrya</s> is the distant-born gem, dear to the planet <s>Ketu</s>.

children.text: mauktikaṃ śauktikaṃ muktā tathā muktāphalaṃ ca tat
children.translated_text: <s>Mauktika</s>, <s>Śauktika</s>, <s>Muktā</s>, and <s>Muktāphala</s> are names of pearl.

children.text: śuktiḥ śaṅkho gajaḥ kroḍaḥ phaṇī matsyaśca darduraḥ
children.translated_text: Oyster shell, conch, elephant, boar, snake, fish, and frog,
and bamboo: these are named by experts as the sources of pearls.
Pearl is cooling, aphrodisiac, good for the eyes, and gives strength and nourishment.

children.text: puṃsi klībe pravālaḥ syātpumāneva tu vidrumaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pravāla</s> may be masculine or neuter, while <s>Vidruma</s> is only masculine.
Gems, when eaten, are sweet and laxative.

children.text: cakṣuṣyāṇi ca śītāni viṣaghnāni dhṛtāni ca
children.translated_text: They are good for the eyes, cooling, and antidotal; when worn too,
they are auspicious, pleasing, and remove afflictions caused by planets.

children.text: kiṃ ratnaṃ kasya grahasya prītikāritvena doṣaharaṃ bhavatīti praśne taduttaramāha ratnamālāyām
children.translated_text: To the question, 'Which gem removes the affliction of which planet by pleasing it?', he gives the answer in the <s>Ratnamālā</s>.

children.text: māṇikyaṃ taraṇeḥ sujātamamalaṃ muktāphalaṃ śītagor māheyasya tu vidrumo nigaditaḥ saumyasya gārutmatam
children.translated_text: A pure, well-born ruby belongs to the Sun, a pearl to the Moon, coral is stated for Mars, and emerald for Mercury.

children.text: devejyasya ca puṣparāgamasurācāryasya vajraṃ śaner nīlaṃ nirmalam anyayor nigadite gomedavaidūryake ||
children.translated_text: Yellow sapphire belongs to Jupiter, diamond to Venus, spotless blue sapphire to Saturn, and hessonite and cat's-eye are prescribed for the other two.
The secondary gems are glass and <s>Karpūrāśman</s>,
as well as pearl-oyster and conch, and many others too.
The qualities that belong to gems are likewise present in secondary gems.
But they are somewhat inferior to them; this distinction has been stated.

children.text: viṣaṃ tu garalaḥ kṣveḍastasya bhedān udāhare
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣa</s> (poison) is also <s>Garala</s> and <s>Kṣveḍa</s>; I shall state its varieties.
<s>Vatsanābha</s>, <s>Sahāridra</s>, <s>Saktuka</s>, and <s>Pradīpana</s>,
<s>Saurāṣṭrika</s>, <s>Śṛṅgika</s>, and <s>Kālakūṭa</s> as well.
<s>Hālāhala</s> and <s>Brahmaputra</s>: these are the nine varieties of poison.
With leaves resembling <s>sinduvāra</s>, and likewise having the shape of <s>vatsanābhi</s>,

children.text: yatpārśve na tarorvṛddhir vatsanābhaḥ sa bhāṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: near which no tree grows: that is called <s>Vatsanābha</s>.
That whose root is like turmeric is called <s>Hāridra</s>.
That knot whose middle is filled as if with <s>saktuka</s> meal is <s>Saktuka</s>.
That which is red in color, brilliant, and has the splendor of fire,
and causes intense burning: that first one is said to be <s>Pradīpana</s>.
That which occurs in the region of <s>Surāṣṭra</s> is called <s>Saurāṣṭrika</s>.
When it is tied in a cow's horn and milk becomes red,
experts in the principles of substances call that <s>Śṛṅgika</s>.
In the battle between gods and asuras, from <s>Pṛthumālin</s>, who was slain by the gods,
from the blood of that Daitya there arose a tree resembling an <s>aśvattha</s>.
Its exudation is celebrated by the sages as <s>Kālakūṭa</s>.
It occurs in <s>Ahikṣetra</s>, <s>Śṛṅgavera</s>, <s>Koṅkaṇa</s>, and <s>Malaya</s>.
It has clustered fruits like cow's teats or navels, and a covering like palm leaves.
By its fiery power, nearby trees and the like are burned.
This should be known as <s>Hālāhala</s>; it occurs in <s>Kiṣkindhā</s> and the <s>Himālaya</s>,
on the shore of the southern ocean, and also in <s>Koṅkaṇa</s>.

children.text: varṇataḥ kapilo yaḥ syāttathā bhavati sārataḥ
children.translated_text: That which is tawny in color, and likewise so in its essential substance,
should be known as <s>Brahmaputra</s>; it arises on Mount <s>Malaya</s>.
Among these, the Brāhmaṇa is pale, the Kṣatriya has a red luster,
the Vaiśya is yellow, and the Śūdra is black: poison is said to be fourfold.
For <s>rasāyana</s> one should give Brāhmaṇa poison, and Kṣatriya poison for bodily nourishment;
Vaiśya poison should be given for destroying skin disease, and Śūdra poison indeed for killing.

children.text: viṣaṃ prāṇaharaṃ proktaṃ vyavāyi ca vikāśi ca
children.translated_text: Poison is said to be life-destroying, <s>vyavāyi</s> (pervasive before digestion), and <s>vikāśi</s> (diffusive).
It is fiery, removes vāta and kapha, is <s>yogavāhi</s> (a catalytic carrier), and produces intoxication.
But that very poison, when properly prepared, gives life and is a <s>rasāyana</s>.
It is a <s>yogavāhi</s>, destroys the three doṣas, nourishes, and increases virility.

children.text: ye durguṇā viṣe'śuddhe te syurhīnā viśodhanāt
children.translated_text: The bad qualities present in unpurified poison become diminished through purification.
Therefore, in applications, poison should be purified and then employed.
The latex of <s>arka</s>, the latex of <s>snuhī</s>, <s>lāṅgalī</s>, and <s>karavīraka</s>,
<s>guñjā</s>, <s>ahiphena</s>, and <s>dhattūra</s> are the seven kinds of <s>upaviṣa</s> (subsidiary poison).

children.text: dāhe raktaṃ sitaṃ chede nikaṣe kuṅkumaprabham
children.translated_text: Red when burned, white when cut, and saffron-colored on the touchstone,

children.text: tāraśulbojjhitaṃ snigdhaṃ komalaṃ guru hema sat ||
children.translated_text: free from silver and copper, smooth, soft, and heavy: such gold is genuine.

children.text: tacchede kaṭhinaṃ rūkṣaṃ vivarṇaṃ samalaṃ dalam
children.translated_text: If, when cut, it is hard, rough, discolored, impure, and flaky,

children.text: dāhe chede sitaṃ śvetaṃ kaṣe sphuṭaṃ laghu tyajet ||
children.translated_text: or if, when burned and cut, it is pale white, cracked on the touchstone, and light, one should reject it.
Gold leaves beaten into thin sheets should be heated in the fire.
When they are heated again and again, one should quench them in oil, buttermilk, and sour gruel,

children.text: gomūtre ca kulatthānāṃ kaṣāye tu tridhā tridhā
children.translated_text: and also in cow's urine and in a decoction of horse gram, three times in each.

children.text: evaṃ hemnaḥ pareṣāṃ ca dhātūnāṃ śodhanaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Thus the purification of gold and of the other metals is effected.

children.text: balaṃ savīryaṃ harate narāṇāṃ rogavrajaṃ poṣayatīha kāye
children.translated_text: Unpurified gold takes away the strength and vitality of men, and nourishes a host of diseases in the body here.

children.text: asaukhyakāryeva sadā suvarṇamaśuddham etanmaraṇaṃ ca kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: This unpurified gold, always producing discomfort, can also cause death.
One should triturate mercury, twice the amount of the gold, together with an acid substance.
One should place sulfur equal to that pellet both below and above it.
Then, after sealing the pellet in a firm covered pair of earthen saucers,
one should give heatings with thirty forest cow-dung cakes; in this way, fourteen <s>puṭas</s> are given.

children.text: nirutthaṃ jāyate bhasma gandho deyaḥ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: An irreducible <s>bhasma</s> (ash) is produced; sulfur should be supplied again and again.
When gold has melted, one should add lead at one-sixteenth part.

children.text: cūrṇayitvā tathāmlena ghṛṣṭvā kṛtvā tu golakam ||
children.translated_text: After powdering it, rubbing it with sour liquid, and then making it into a pellet,
one should add sulfur equal to the pellet, both below and above.
Placing it in a covered pair of saucers, one should heat it with thirty forest cow-dung cakes.

children.text: evaṃ saptapuṭair hema nirutthaṃ bhasma jāyate ||
children.translated_text: By seven such <s>puṭas</s>, gold becomes an irreducible <s>bhasma</s>.
After grinding with juices of <s>kāñcanāra</s>, one should make a <s>kajjalī</s> from equal parts mercury and sulfur.
One should smear the gold leaves evenly with that.
With pastes of <s>kāñcanāra</s> bark one should prepare a pair of crucibles.

children.text: dhṛtvā satsaṃpuṭe golaṃ mṛṇmūṣāsampuṭe ca tat ||
children.translated_text: Placing the pellet in a good sealed vessel, and that within a clay crucible enclosure,

children.text: nidhāya sandhirodhaṃ ca kṛtvā saṃśoṣya golakam
children.translated_text: after setting it down, sealing the joint, and drying the pellet,

children.text: vahniṃ kharataraṃ kuryād evaṃ dattvā puṭatrayam ||
children.translated_text: one should make a very fierce fire; in this way, after giving three <s>puṭas</s>,
an irreducible <s>bhasma</s> is produced, and it may be used in all operations.
By the <s>kāñcanāra</s> procedure, <s>lāṅgalī</s> kills, that is, calcines, gold.

children.text: jvālāmukhī tathā hanyād yathā hanti manaḥśilā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Jvālāmukhī</s> likewise kills it, just as <s>manaḥśilā</s> does.
Powder of <s>śilā</s> and <s>sindūra</s>, in equal parts, with the milk of <s>arka</s>,
should be given seven <s>bhāvanās</s> (triturating infusions) and dried again and again.

children.text: tatastu galite hemni kalko'yaṃ dīyate samaḥ
children.translated_text: Then this paste is added in equal quantity to melted gold.
One should blow on it again very strongly, until the paste melts.
In this way, when the paste is applied three times, the calcination of gold is accomplished.

children.text: suvarṇaṃ śītalaṃ vṛṣyaṃ balyaṃ guru rasāyanam
children.translated_text: Gold is cooling, aphrodisiac, strengthening, heavy, and a <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: svādu tiktaṃ ca tuvaraṃ pāke ca svādu picchilam ||
children.translated_text: It is sweet, bitter, and astringent, sweet in post-digestive effect, and mucilaginous.
It is purifying, nourishing, good for the eyes, and grants intelligence, memory, and understanding.
It is good for the heart, promotes life, and produces beauty, clarity of speech, and firmness of skin.
It conquers both kinds of poison, consumption, insanity, fever from the three doṣas, and wasting.

children.text: asamyaṅmāritaṃ svarṇaṃ balaṃ vīryaṃ ca nāśayet
children.translated_text: Improperly incinerated gold destroys strength and virility,
and causes diseases and death; therefore one should calcine it carefully.
The non-return of iron and the like to their former metallic state, acquisition of its qualities, abundance of qualities,
and also floating on water: these constitute its successful preparation through <s>puṭa</s>-heating.
In a deep, broad, square pit measuring two hastas...
In a chamber filled with a thousand cow-dung cakes, the medicine to be heated in a <s>puṭa</s>,
carefully sealed in a furnace, should be placed over cow dung;
one should put half a thousand cow-dung cakes on top of the small furnace.
One should set fire there; this is remembered as the <s>mahāpuṭa</s>.
In a pit one and a quarter hastas in measure, both deep and wide,
filled with a thousand cow-dung cakes, one should place in the middle
the small chamber containing the substance to be heated, with its mouth sealed.
One should put half of the portions below and half above;
this is called the <s>gajapuṭa</s>, famed as the best of all <s>puṭa</s>s.
In a pit of an <s>aratni</s> in measure, the heating is called the <s>vārāhapuṭa</s>;
in a pit of a span, it is taught as the <s>kaukkuṭapuṭa</s>.
According to some, the <s>kaukkuṭapuṭa</s> is in a pit sixteen <s>aṅgula</s>s deep.

children.text: yat puṭaṃ dīyate khāte hyaṣṭasaṅkhyair vanopalaiḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>puṭa</s> that is given in a pit with eight cow-dung cakes
is called the <s>kapotapuṭa</s> by experts in <s>puṭa</s>s.
Dried cow dung, trampled by cows' hooves inside a cowshed and powdered,
is called <s>govara</s>, the best material for accomplishing <s>rasa</s> operations.
Where a <s>puṭa</s> is applied with <s>govara</s> placed in a large vessel,
physicians call that the <s>govarapuṭa</s> for the ash of <s>sūta</s> (mercury).

children.text: bṛhadbhāṇḍe tuṣaiḥ pūrṇe madhye mūṣāṃ vidhārayet
children.translated_text: In a large vessel filled with husks, one should place a crucible in the middle;
after setting fire to it, one should seal the vessel; that is called the <s>bhāṇḍapuṭa</s>.
In a vessel a span deep, with a flask set in the middle
and filled with sand up to the neck of the flask,
where the medicine contained in the flask is cooked by fire,
that apparatus is remembered by the learned as the <s>vālukāyantra</s>.

children.text: nibaddham auṣadhaṃ sūtaṃ bhūrje tattriguṇe vare
children.translated_text: Medicine and <s>sūta</s> (mercury) are wrapped in excellent birch bark in three layers,

children.text: rasapoṭalikāṃ kāṣṭhe dṛḍhaṃ baddhvā guṇena hi ||
children.translated_text: and the <s>rasa</s> packet is tied firmly to a stick with a cord.
It is suspended by its own support inside a pot filled with fermenting liquid;
one should light a fire below, in each case according to the prescribed procedure.
This is called the <s>dolāyantra</s>; it is the very procedure named steaming.

children.text: sāmbusthālīmukhe baddhe vastre svedyaṃ nidhāya ca
children.translated_text: When the substance to be steamed is placed in cloth tied over the mouth of a pot containing water,

children.text: pidhāya pacyate yatra tadyantraṃ svedanaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: covered, and cooked, that apparatus is remembered as <s>svedana</s> (steaming).
Having put <s>rasa</s> in the lower pot, one should place over its mouth
another pot facing upward, sealing it properly with soft clay.
After putting water in the upper pot and carefully setting it on the stove,
one should light a fire beneath it for five watches.
Then, once it has cooled by itself, one should take the excellent <s>rasa</s> from the apparatus.
Experts declare this apparatus to be called <s>Vidyādhara</s>.
In a pit, one should surround on every side with sand a crucible containing <s>rasa</s>,
and cover it with blazing cow-dung cakes; the apparatus is named <s>Bhūdhara</s>.
An apparatus is known as <s>Ḍamaru</s> when the mouth of its pot is sealed.

children.text: guru snigdhaṃ mṛdu śvetaṃ dāhe chede ghanakṣamam
children.translated_text: Heavy, unctuous, soft, white, able to withstand burning, cutting, and hammering,
rich in color and clear like the moon: such auspicious silver has nine qualities.

children.text: kaṭhinaṃ kṛtrimaṃ rūkṣaṃ raktaṃ pītadalaṃ laghu
children.translated_text: Hard, artificial, rough, red, yellow-flaked, light,
and ruined by burning, cutting, or hammering: such silver is declared defective.
The leaves of silver, made thin, should be heated in fire;
while they are very hot, one should quench them in oil, buttermilk, and sour gruel,

children.text: gomūtre ca kulatthānāṃ kaṣāye ca tridhā tridhā
children.translated_text: and also in cow urine and in a decoction of horse gram, three times in each.
In this way the purification of silver leaves is accomplished.

children.text: rūpyaṃ tvaśuddhaṃ prakaroti tāpaṃ vibandhakaṃ vīryabalakṣayaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Unpurified silver produces heat, obstruction, and loss of virility and strength;

children.text: dehasya puṣṭiṃ harate tanoti rogāṃstataḥ śodhanamasya kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: it removes bodily nourishment and spreads diseases; therefore one should perform its purification.
One part of <s>tālaka</s> (orpiment) should be ground for one watch with some sour liquid;
with that, one should coat three parts of silver leaves.
After placing them in a crucible-<s>puṭa</s>, sealing them, one should cook them in a <s>puṭa</s> of thirty cow-dung cakes.

children.text: samuddhṛtya punastālaṃ dattvā ruddhvā puṭe pacet
children.translated_text: Having taken them out, one should again add <s>tālaka</s>, seal them, and cook them in a <s>puṭa</s>.
Thus, by fourteen <s>puṭa</s>s, silver becomes <s>bhasma</s> (ash).
<s>Mākṣika</s> (pyrite), ground with the latex of <s>snuhī</s>, should be used to coat them.
The intelligent person should process the silver leaves according to the method for <s>tālaka</s>,
with fourteen <s>puṭa</s>s; silver becomes <s>bhasma</s>.

children.text: raupyaṃ śītaṃ kaṣāyaṃ ca svādupākarasaṃ saram
children.translated_text: Silver is cooling, astringent, sweet in post-digestive effect and taste, and laxative;
it stabilizes age, is unctuous and scraping, and conquers <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>;
it certainly destroys diseases such as <s>prameha</s> without delay.
Copper that is like a hibiscus blossom, unctuous, heavy, and able to withstand hammering,
and free from iron and lead, is recommended for incineration.
Black, rough, excessively clear, white, unable to withstand hammering,
or mixed with iron and lead: such copper is declared defective.
The leaves of copper, made thin, should be heated in fire;

children.text: niṣiñcet taptataptāni taile takre ca kāñjike ||
children.translated_text: while they are very hot, one should quench them in oil, buttermilk, and sour gruel,

children.text: gomūtre ca kulatthānāṃ kaṣāye ca tridhā tridhā
children.translated_text: and also in cow urine and in a decoction of horse gram, three times in each.
In this way the purification of copper leaves is accomplished.

children.text: eko doṣo viṣe tāmre tvaśuddhe'ṣṭau bhramo vamiḥ
children.translated_text: There is one fault in poison, but in unpurified copper there are eight: dizziness and vomiting,
purging, sweating, nausea, fainting, burning, and loss of appetite.
They say, 'Poison is poison'; but copper is called poison.

children.text: eko doṣo viṣe tāmre tvaṣṭau doṣāḥ prakīrtitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In poison one fault is stated, but in copper eight faults are proclaimed.
Having made the copper leaves fine, the learned person should steam them
Then one should place it in a mortar with sour liquid for three days.
Adding a quarter part of <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury), one should triturate it with sour liquid for one <s>yāma</s>.
Then, having taken out the sheets, one should coat them with twice as much
sulfur rubbed with sour liquid, and should make a ball of it.

children.text: tataḥ piṣṭvā ca mīnākṣīṃ cāṅgerīṃ vā punarnavām ||
children.translated_text: Then, after grinding <s>Mīnākṣī</s>, <s>Cāṅgerī</s>, or <s>Punarnavā</s>,
one should coat the outside of the ball with that paste to the measure of one finger-breadth.

children.text: dhṛtvā tadgolakaṃ bhāṇḍe śarāveṇa ca rodhayet ||
children.translated_text: Having placed that ball in a vessel, one should seal it with an earthen dish.
Then, after filling it with sand, ash, salt, and water,
and applying a seal at the mouth of the vessel, one should cook it on a hearth.
The fire should be gradually increased properly for as long as four <s>yāmas</s>.
After taking it out when it has cooled by itself, one should triturate it with the juices of <s>śūraṇa</s>.
One should triturate that ball for one <s>yāma</s> and place it inside a <s>śūraṇa</s> tuber.
An earthen coating should be made all around, about the thickness of a thumb.

children.text: pācyaṃ gajapuṭe kṣiptaṃ mṛtaṃ bhavati niścitam ||
children.translated_text: When placed in a <s>gajapuṭa</s> and cooked, it certainly becomes properly incinerated.

children.text: vamanaṃ ca virekaṃ ca bhramaṃ klamamathārucim
children.translated_text: It never causes vomiting, purgation, dizziness, fatigue, or loss of appetite,
nor burning, sweating, or nausea at any time.

children.text: tāmraṃ kaṣāyaṃ madhuraṃ satiktamamlaṃ ca pāke kaṭu sārakaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Copper is astringent, sweet, somewhat bitter, and sour; in post-digestive effect it is pungent and laxative.

children.text: pittāpahaṃ śleṣmaharaṃ ca śītaṃ tadropaṇaṃ syāllaghu lekhanaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: It removes <s>pitta</s> and <s>kapha</s>, is cooling, and is healing, light, and scraping.
It removes pallor, abdominal disease, piles, fever, skin disease, cough, dyspnea, consumption, chronic rhinitis, and acid-pitta,
as well as swelling, worms, and colic; the wise call it only slightly nourishing.

children.text: eko doṣo viṣe tāmre tvasamyaṅmārite punaḥ
children.translated_text: But when copper has been improperly incinerated, there is a poison-like defect in it:

children.text: dāhaḥ svedo'rucir mūrcchā kledo reko vamirbhramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: burning, sweating, loss of appetite, fainting, excess secretion, purgation, vomiting, and dizziness.

children.text: vaṅgaṃ ca girijaṃ tacca khurakaṃ miśrakaṃ dvidhā
children.translated_text: <s>Vaṅga</s> (tin), also called <s>Girija</s>, is of two kinds: <s>khuraka</s> and <s>miśraka</s>.

children.text: tayostu khurakaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ miśrakaṃ tvahitaṃ matam ||
children.translated_text: Of those two, <s>khuraka</s> is best, while <s>miśraka</s> is considered unwholesome.

children.text: vaṅgaṃ vidhatte khalu śuddhihīnamākṣepakampau ca kilāsagulmau
children.translated_text: Tin lacking purification indeed produces convulsions and tremors, leucoderma and abdominal tumors,

children.text: kuṣṭhāni śūlaṃ kila vātaśothaṃ pāṇḍuṃ pramehaṃ ca bhagandaraṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: skin diseases, colic, vāta-type swelling, pallor, <s>prameha</s>, and fistula-in-ano.

children.text: viṣopamaṃ raktavikāravṛndaṃ kṣayaṃ ca kṛcchrāṇi kaphajvaraṃ ca
children.translated_text: It also produces a poison-like group of blood disorders, wasting, urinary difficulties, and kapha-fever,
and urinary disease, stones, abscesses, and testicular disorders; lead too causes the disorders that have been stated.

children.text: vaṅganāgau prataptau ca galitau tau niṣecayet
children.translated_text: Tin and lead, heated until molten, should be quenched

children.text: tridhā tridhā viśuddhiḥ syādravidugdhe'pi ca tridhā ||
children.translated_text: three times each; purification also occurs by doing this three times in <s>ravidugdha</s>.
When tin has been melted in an earthen vessel, powder of tamarind and <s>Aśvattha</s> bark,
ground to one quarter the amount of the tin, should be stirred with an iron ladle.
Then, within just two <s>yāmas</s>, the tin becomes <s>bhasma</s> (ash).
Next, adding <s>tāla</s> equal to the bhasma, one should triturate it with sour liquid.
Then, after cooking it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>, one should again triturate it with sour liquid.
After that, with a tenth part of <s>tāla</s>, one should heat it in a <s>puṭa</s> for one <s>yāma</s>.

children.text: evaṃ daśapuṭaiḥ pakvaṃ vaṅgaṃ bhavati māritam ||
children.translated_text: Tin cooked in this way with ten <s>puṭas</s> becomes incinerated.

children.text: vaṅgaṃ laghu saraṃ rūkṣaṃ kuṣṭhaṃ mehakaphakrimīn
