children.translated_text: Tin is light, laxative, and dry; it destroys skin disease, urinary disorders, kapha, and worms,

children.text: nihanti pāṇḍuṃ saśvāsaṃ netryam īṣattu pittalam ||
children.translated_text: and it destroys pallor together with dyspnea; it is good for the eyes and is slightly pitta-provoking.

children.text: siṃho gajaughaṃ tu yathā nihanti tathaiva vaṅgo'khilamehavargam
children.translated_text: Just as a lion destroys a herd of elephants, so tin destroys the whole class of urinary disorders.

children.text: dehasya saukhyaṃ prabalendriyatvaṃ narasya puṣṭiṃ vidadhāti nūnam ||
children.translated_text: It surely brings bodily ease, strong senses, and nourishment to a person.
<s>Yaśada</s> (zinc), also called <s>Girija</s>: its defects, purification, and incineration
are to be understood just as for tin; now I shall enumerate its qualities.

children.text: yaśadaṃ ca saraṃ tiktaṃ śītalaṃ kaphapittahṛt
children.translated_text: Zinc is laxative, bitter, cooling, and removes kapha and pitta.

children.text: cakṣuṣyaṃ paramaṃ mehān pāṇḍuṃ śvāsaṃ ca nāśayet ||
children.translated_text: It is supremely good for the eyes and destroys urinary disorders, pallor, and dyspnea.
Its innate defects have been shown to be just like those of tin.

children.text: śodhanaṃ cāpi tasyeva bhiṣagbhir gaditaṃ purā ||
children.translated_text: And physicians of old have said that its purification too is the same as that.
Through repeated coating with <s>śilā</s> ground in betel juice,
lead becomes a non-revivifiable <s>bhasma</s> after thirty-two <s>puṭas</s>.
One should add powder of <s>Aśvattha</s> and tamarind bark in a quarter part,
when lead has been melted in an earthen vessel and stirred with an iron ladle.
In one <s>yāma</s> it becomes <s>bhasma</s>; <s>manaḥśilā</s> should be equal to it.
Having ground the two with <s>kāñjika</s>, one should cook them in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.

children.text: svāṅgaśītaṃ punaḥ piṣṭvā śilayā kāñjikena ca
children.translated_text: When it has cooled by itself, one should again grind it with <s>śilā</s> and <s>kāñjika</s>,
and cook it again between two dishes; thus incineration is achieved with sixty <s>puṭas</s>.
Lead should be known as having the qualities of tin, and especially as destroying urinary disorders.

children.text: nāgastu nāgaśatatulyabalaṃ dadāti vyādhiṃ ca nāśayati jīvanamātanoti
children.translated_text: Lead gives strength equal to that of a hundred elephants, destroys disease, and extends life.

children.text: vahniṃ pradīpayati kāmabalaṃ karoti mṛtyuṃ ca nāśayati saṃtatasevitaḥ saḥ ||
children.translated_text: When used continually, it kindles the digestive fire, creates sexual vigor, and destroys death.
Unpurified iron causes lameness, skin disease, illness, and death; it produces heart disease, colic, and stones,

children.text: nānārujānāṃ ca tathā prakopaṃ kuryācca hṛllāsamaśuddhalauham ||
children.translated_text: and also an aggravation of many pains; unpurified iron also causes nausea.
One should heat the flattened sheets of iron in the fire,
and quench them, while repeatedly heated, in oil, buttermilk, and <s>kāñjika</s>,

children.text: gomūtre ca kulatthānāṃ kaṣāye ca tridhā tridhā
children.translated_text: and also in cow urine and in a decoction of horse gram, three times each.
In this way the purification of the iron sheets is produced.
Powder made from purified iron should be triturated with the juices of <s>Pātālagaruḍī</s>,
and heated in the fire; in this way one should give three <s>puṭas</s>.
Three <s>puṭas</s> should be given with the juices of <s>Kumārī</s> and <s>Kuṭhāracchinnikā</s>,
then six <s>puṭas</s> should be given; thus incineration of <s>tīkṣṇa</s> iron is achieved.
One should add <s>darada</s> in a twelfth part relative to the powder of <s>tīkṣṇa</s> iron,
triturate it with the liquids of <s>kanyakā</s> for two <s>yāmas</s>, and then heat it in a <s>puṭa</s>.
In this way, through seven <s>puṭas</s>, iron powder attains death, that is, calcination.
Another procedure for calcining iron, true and experienced by master practitioners,
is now told by <s>Rāmarāja</s> with an inquiring mind.

children.text: sūtakād dviguṇaṃ gandhaṃ dattvā kuryācca kajjalīm ||
children.translated_text: Having added sulfur in twice the quantity of mercury, one should make a <s>kajjalī</s>.
One should triturate iron powder equal to the two with the juices of <s>kanyakā</s>,

children.text: yāmayugmaṃ tataḥ piṇḍaṃ kṛtvā tāmrasya pātrake ||
children.translated_text: for two <s>yāmas</s>; then, making it into a pellet, in a copper vessel,
the wise should keep it in the heat and cover it with leaves of <s>rubūka</s>.
After two <s>yāmas</s> it becomes hot; then one should place it in a heap of grain.
Having put an earthen saucer over it, one should take it out after three days.
After grinding it, one should sift it through cloth; in this way it becomes water-floating.
Having pounded pomegranate leaves with four times as much water,
one should mix iron powder with that juice and soak it, so it is said.
One should dry it in the sun and give <s>puṭa</s>-heating again and again.
By twenty-one repetitions it is calcined; there is no doubt about this.
In this way one should calcine all metals, even gold and the rest.

children.text: lauhaṃ tiktaṃ saraṃ śītaṃ kaṣāyaṃ madhuraṃ guru
children.translated_text: Iron is bitter, flowing, cooling, astringent, sweet, and heavy.

children.text: rūkṣaṃ vayasyaṃ cakṣuṣyaṃ lekhanaṃ vātalaṃ jayet ||
children.translated_text: It is dry, age-sustaining, good for the eyes, scraping, and vāta-provoking; it overcomes
kapha, pitta, artificial poison, colic, swelling, piles, spleen disease, and jaundice,
as well as obesity, urinary disease, worms, and skin disease; its slag has just the same properties.
Beginning with one <s>guñjā</s> and up to nine <s>raktikās</s>,
a person should consume that much iron according to the doṣas and the digestive fire.

children.text: kūṣmāṇḍaṃ tilatailaṃ ca māṣānnaṃ rājikāṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Gourd, sesame oil, food made from black gram, and mustard,
as well as liquor and sour flavors, should be avoided by one who uses iron.
All metals, beginning with gold, when smeared with <s>śilā</s>, sulfur, and the latex of <s>arka</s>,
are calcined by twelve <s>puṭas</s>; this is true, just as the teacher's statement says.
Weakness of digestion, severe loss of strength, constipation, eye diseases, and skin diseases,

children.text: mālāṃ tathaiva vraṇapūrvikāṃ ca kuryādaśuddhaṃ khalamākṣikaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: and likewise a garland-like eruption preceded by sores: impure <s>mākṣika</s> certainly causes these.

children.text: mākṣikasya trayo bhāgā bhāgaikaṃ saindhavasya ca
children.translated_text: Three parts of <s>mākṣika</s> and one part of rock salt
should be cooked with the juices of citron or else with the juices of lemon.
One should stir it in an iron vessel until the vessel becomes very red.
Then complete purification is obtained by the gold-<s>mākṣika</s>.

children.text: kulatthasya kaṣāyeṇa ghṛṣṭvā talena vā puṭet
children.translated_text: After rubbing it with a decoction of horse gram, or with oil, one should give <s>puṭa</s>-heating.
Or, with buttermilk or goat urine, gold-<s>mākṣika</s> is calcined.
The defects in silver-<s>mākṣika</s> should be understood as like those in gold-<s>mākṣika</s>.
Therefore its purification is described for the purpose of pacifying those defects.
For a day, with fluids from <s>karkoṭī</s> and <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, and with lemon juices,
one should give <s>bhāvanā</s> in strong sunlight; <s>vimalā</s> is certainly purified.

children.text: kulatthasya kaṣāyeṇa ghṛṣṭvā tailena vā puṭet
children.translated_text: After rubbing it with a decoction of horse gram, or with oil, one should give <s>puṭa</s>-heating.
With horse urine, silver-<s>mākṣika</s> attains calcination.
Not only the qualities of gold and silver are recognized in the two <s>tāpīja</s> ores;
because of contact with other substances, they also have other qualities.

children.text: mākṣikaṃ madhuraṃ tiktaṃ svayaṃ vṛṣyaṃ rasāyanam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s> is sweet and bitter; by itself it is aphrodisiac and a <s>rasāyana</s>.
It is good for the eyes; bladder pain, skin disease, jaundice, urinary disease, poison, and abdominal disease,

children.text: arśaḥ śophaṃ kṣayaṃ kaṇḍūṃ tridoṣaṃ ca niyacchati ||
children.translated_text: as well as piles, swelling, wasting, itching, and the three doṣas, it restrains.
One should triturate <s>tuttha</s> with the feces of a cat and of a pigeon.
After adding one-tenth part <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, one should then cook it in a small <s>puṭa</s>.
A <s>puṭa</s> with curd and a <s>puṭa</s> with honey should be given for the purification of <s>tuttha</s>.

children.text: tutthakaṃ kaṭukaṃ kṣāraṃ kaṣāyaṃ vāmakaṃ laghu ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tutthaka</s> is pungent, alkaline, astringent, emetic, and light.
It is scraping, breaking, cooling, good for the eyes, and removes kapha and pitta.
It destroys poison, stone disease, skin disease, and itching; <s>kharpara</s> is considered to have the same properties.
The thinly beaten sheets of bronze should be heated in the fire.
One should quench them, when very hot, in oil, buttermilk, and sour gruel,

children.text: gomūtre ca kulatthānāṃ kaṣāye'tra tridhā tridhā
children.translated_text: and in cow urine and a decoction of horse gram, three times each here.
In this way the purification of bronze and brass is produced.
Sulfur, ground with the latex of <s>arka</s>, should be used to smear
the purified bronze sheets in equal quantity, repeatedly with sour liquids.
Then, placing them in a crucible enclosure, one should cook them with a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
In this way, by two <s>puṭas</s>, bronze and brass are certainly calcined.

children.text: kāṃsyaṃ kaṣāyaṃ tīkṣṇoṣṇaṃ lekhanaṃ viśadaṃ saram
children.translated_text: Bronze is astringent, sharp, hot, scraping, clear, and flowing.
It is heavy, beneficial for the eyes, dry, and excellent at removing kapha and pitta.

children.text: rītikā tu bhaved rūkṣā satiktā lavaṇā rase
children.translated_text: Brass, however, is dry, slightly bitter, and salty in taste.
It is purifying, destroys jaundice, removes worms, and is not excessively scraping.
Combination with milk and sour liquids is said by the wise to be its purification.
<s>Sindūra</s> is hot and removes erysipelas, skin disease, itching, and poison.
It causes the joining of fractures and cleanses and heals wounds.
That iron which smells like cow urine, is black, unctuous, soft, and also heavy,

children.text: tiktaṃ kaṣāyaṃ śītaṃ ca sarvaśreṣṭhaṃ tadāyasam ||
children.translated_text: bitter, astringent, and cooling: that iron is the best of all.

children.text: vindhyādau bahulaṃ tattu tatra lohaṃ yato'dhikam
children.translated_text: It is plentiful in the Vindhya region and elsewhere, because iron is abundant there.
Without purification it is useless, because it is mixed with many impurities.

children.text: śilājatu samānīya sūkṣmaṃ khaṇḍaṃ vidhāya ca
children.translated_text: Having procured <s>śilājatu</s> and made it into small pieces,
the wise should put it into very hot water and let it stand for one <s>yāma</s>.
Then, after rubbing it, one should collect the water filtered through cloth.
Having placed it in an earthen vessel, the wise should keep it in the sun.
Whatever thick substance is on top should be put into another vessel.
Thus, when repeatedly processed for two months, the <s>śilājatu</s>...
It becomes fit for operations; when put into fire, it should become like a <s>liṅga</s>.

children.text: nirdhūmaṃ ca tataḥ śuddhaṃ sarvakarmasu yojayet ||
children.translated_text: And it should be smokeless. Then, when purified, one should use it in all operations.

children.text: tatra prathamatastasya bahirmalamapākartuṃ kevalajalena prakṣālanaṃ kartavyaṃ tatas tadantargatamṛttikāsikatādidoṣadūrīkaraṇāya vakṣyamāṇakvāthena tatra bhāvanā deyetyatra vāgbhaṭasya matamāha
children.translated_text: In that connection, first, to remove its external dirt, it should be washed with plain water. Then, in order to remove defects such as earth and sand contained within it, <s>bhāvanā</s> (triturating infusion) should be given there with the decoction that will be stated; on this point he states the opinion of <s>Vāgbhaṭa</s>:
Following the disease, the patient, and what is suitable, one should subject it to <s>bhāvanā</s> in an iron vessel;
first washed with plain water and dried, it should then be treated with decoctions.

children.text: tulyaṃ girijena jale vasuguṇite bhāvanauṣadhaṃ kvāthyam
children.translated_text: The drug for <s>bhāvanā</s>, equal to the <s>girija</s>, should be decocted in eight times as much water.
When that decoction is reduced to a quarter, filtered, and warm, one should put the <s>girija</s> into it.

children.text: tat samarasatāṃ yātaṃ saṃśuṣkaṃ prakṣipedrase bhūyaḥ
children.translated_text: When it has become homogeneous and dried, one should again put it into the liquid.

children.text: svaiḥ svairevaṃ kvāthair bhāvyaṃ vārān bhavetsapta ||
children.translated_text: In this way it should be treated with its respective decoctions seven times.
Then, after the patient has been oleated and purified, one should administer <s>girija</s> with ghee prepared from bitter drugs for three days,
and likewise for three days with each one separately,
with a broth of the three fruits, and with that of <s>paṭolī</s> and <s>madhuka</s>.
<s>Śilājatu</s> used in this way becomes extremely beneficial for the body.
One should properly subject it, kept in an iron vessel, to <s>bhāvanā</s> with <s>nimba</s>, <s>guḍūcī</s>, ghee, and barley,
in order to remove faults from surface film, insects, moths, bites, and spoiled medicinal plants.

children.text: evaṃ bhāvanāṃ dattvā saṃśoṣya kevalena jalena śodhanaṃ kartavyaṃ tatprakāramāhāgniveśaḥ
children.translated_text: After giving <s>bhāvanā</s> in this way and drying it, purification with plain water should be performed. <s>Agniveśa</s> states its method:

children.text: uṣṇe ca kāle ravitāpayukte vyabhre nivāte samabhūmibhāge
children.translated_text: In the hot season, when the sun is scorching, in a cloudless, windless, level place,
one should set four black-iron vessels in the sun, carefully attending to them there.

children.text: śilājatu śreṣṭhamavāpya pātre prakṣipya tasmāddviguṇaṃ ca toyam
children.translated_text: Having obtained excellent <s>śilājatu</s>, one should put it in a vessel and add twice as much water,

children.text: uṣṇaṃ tadardhaṃ kvathitaṃ ca dattvā viśodhayettanmṛditaṃ yathāvat ||
children.translated_text: hot and boiled down by half; then one should purify it, after rubbing it properly.
Then whatever black material, heated by the sun's rays, rises upward like a surface film,

children.text: pātre tadanyatra tato nidadhyāttatrāparaṃ koṣṇajalaṃ kṣipecca ||
children.translated_text: one should place that in another vessel; into that one should add more lukewarm water.

children.text: punaśca tasmādaparatra pātre paścācca pātrādaparatra bhūyaḥ
children.translated_text: Again from that into another vessel, and afterwards once more from that vessel into another,

children.text: yadā viśuddhaṃ jalamevamūrdhvaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ samastaṃ malametyadhastāt
children.translated_text: when, in this way, the water above is clear and all the black impurity has gone below,

children.text: tadā tyajettatsalilaṃ malaṃ ca śilājatu syājjalaśuddhamevam ||
children.translated_text: then one should discard that water and the impurity; thus <s>śilājatu</s> is purified by water.

children.text: śilājatu smṛtaṃ tiktaṃ kaṭūṣṇaṃ kaṭupāki ca
children.translated_text: <s>Śilājatu</s> is said to be bitter, pungent, hot, and pungent in post-digestive effect.
It is a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative) and a <s>yogavāhi</s> (catalytic carrier); it removes phlegm, <s>meha</s>, stones, and gravel,

children.text: mūtrakṛcchraṃ kṣayaṃ śvāsaṃ śotham arśāṃsi pāṇḍutām
children.translated_text: dysuria, wasting, asthma, swelling, hemorrhoids, and anemia,
as well as <s>vātarakta</s>, skin disease, epilepsy, and abdominal disease.
With various grains as available, freed from husks and mixed with water,
one should fill an earthen pot and keep it until it becomes sour.
Into it, <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>, <s>muṇḍī</s>, <s>viṣṇukrāntā</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>,
and <s>mīnākṣī</s>, <s>sarpākṣī</s>, <s>sahadevī</s>, and <s>śatāvarī</s>,

children.text: triphalā girikarṇī ca haṃsapādī ca citrakam
children.translated_text: <s>triphala</s>, <s>girikarṇī</s>, <s>haṃsapādī</s>, and <s>citraka</s>,
pounded together with their roots, should be added according to availability.
When this is in the former sour pot, it is known as <s>dhānyāmlaka</s>.
One should use it everywhere in steaming and the other procedures for <s>rasarāja</s> (mercury);
or, if it is unavailable, one should use very sour <s>āranāla</s>.
<s>Tryūṣaṇa</s>, salt, <s>rājī</s>, <s>rajanī</s>, <s>triphala</s>, and fresh ginger,
<s>mahābalā</s>, <s>nāgabalā</s>, <s>meghanāda</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>,

children.text: meṣaśṛṅgī citrakaṃ ca navasāraṃ samaṃ samam
children.translated_text: <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, <s>citraka</s>, and <s>navasāra</s>, each in equal quantity:
all these together, or separately, should be ground with the previous sour liquid.
With that paste one should smear a cloth to a thickness of one finger.

children.text: tanmadhye nikṣipet sūtaṃ baddhvā tattridinaṃ pacet
children.translated_text: One should put <s>sūta</s> (mercury) in its middle, bind it, and cook it for three days;
in a <s>dolāyantra</s> with sour liquid, the <s>rasa</s> becomes steamed.
<s>Mūlaka</s>, <s>anala</s>, <s>sindhūttha</s>, <s>tryūṣaṇa</s>, fresh ginger, and <s>rājikā</s>:

children.text: rasasya ṣoḍaśāṃśena dravyaṃ yuñjyāt pṛthak pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: each substance should be applied separately at one-sixteenth of the <s>rasa</s>.
For substances whose measure is not stated, the learned consider this to be the measure.
After wrapping these in cloth and placing <s>sūta</s> in <s>kāñjika</s>,
a wise person should steam it for one day by means of a <s>dolāyantra</s>.
Through steaming <s>sūta</s> becomes sharp; through trituration it becomes very pure.
At first <s>rasa</s> should be rubbed with brick powder and pulverized material; thereafter,
with curd, jaggery, <s>sindhūttha</s>, <s>rājikā</s>, and household soot;
with decoctions made from <s>kumārī</s>, <s>citraka</s>, and red mustard, mixed with <s>bṛhatī</s>,
and also with <s>triphala</s>: <s>rasa</s> triturated for three days is freed from all impurities.
<s>Tryūṣaṇa</s>, <s>triphala</s>, the tubers of <s>vandhyā</s>, together with the two <s>kṣudrā</s>s,
<s>citraka</s>, <s>ūrṇā</s>, <s>niśā</s>, alkali, <s>kanyā</s>, <s>arka</s>, and the liquids of <s>kanaka</s>:
one should triturate <s>sūta</s> seven times with a broth prepared from these.
Thus made to coalesce, <s>sūta</s> casts off all seven coverings.
With <s>mayūragrīva</s> and <s>tāpya</s>, when it has been made into a <s>naṣṭapiṣṭī</s>,
one should perform upward sublimation of <s>rasendra</s> in the <s>Vidyādhara</s> apparatus.
With <s>triphala</s>, <s>śigru</s>, and <s>śikhi</s>, together with salt and <s>āsurī</s>,
having made <s>rasa</s> into a <s>naṣṭapiṣṭa</s>, one should smear the upper vessel.
Then one should cause its downward distillation with glowing cakes below.

children.text: yantre bhūdharasaṃjñe tu tataḥ sūto viśudhyati ||
children.translated_text: In the apparatus called <s>Bhūdhara</s>, <s>sūta</s> then becomes purified.
When it has been purified by steaming and the other procedures,
then it performs the operations and may be used in all processes.

children.text: gṛhakanyā harati malaṃ triphalāgniṃ citrako viṣaṃ hanti
children.translated_text: <s>Gṛhakanyā</s> removes the impurity; <s>triphalā</s> removes the fiery defect; <s>citraka</s> destroys the poison.
Therefore, with these ingredients mixed together, one should subject it to <s>mūrchana</s> seven times.
With decoctions made from <s>kumārī</s>, <s>citraka</s>, and red mustard, mixed with <s>bṛhatī</s>,
mercury, rubbed also with the three fruits, is freed from all impurities in three days.
One should triturate <s>sūta</s> for a day with <s>kumārī</s> and powders of <s>niśā</s>.

children.text: evaṃ kadarthitaḥ sūtaḥ ṣaṇḍho bhavati niścitam ||
children.translated_text: Thus abused, <s>sūta</s> certainly becomes impotent.
Steamed with a decoction of many medicines, it becomes strong.
Steamed with <s>sarpākṣī</s>, <s>ciñcikā</s>, <s>vandhyā</s>, <s>bhṛṅga</s>, and <s>abda</s>, it becomes strong.
Then, when steamed with fiery liquids, it becomes exceedingly brilliant.
One should take <s>dhūmasāra</s>, mercury, <s>torī</s>, sulfur, and <s>navasādara</s>,

children.text: yāmaikaṃ mardayed amlabhāgaṃ kṛtvā samaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: make each in equal quantity with an acidic portion, and triturate them for one <s>yāma</s>.
After placing the mixture in a glass bottle, one should coat it all around with a seal of clay and cloth,

children.text: vilipya parito vaktre mudrāṃ dattvā viśoṣayet ||
children.translated_text: apply a seal at the mouth, and dry it.
One should set the bottle down inside a lower pot that has holes,
and, filling the pot with sand up to the neck of the bottle,
place it on the stove and make a fire beneath it very gradually.
After that, one should kindle the fire somewhat more intensely, step by step.
In this way, in twelve <s>yāmas</s>, the excellent mercury is killed.
When it has cooled by itself, one should break it open and discard the sulfur that has gone upward.

children.text: adhasthaṃ ca mṛtaṃ sūtaṃ gṛhṇīyāttaṃ tu mātrayā
children.translated_text: One should take the dead <s>sūta</s> that remains below, in the proper dose,
and employ it in all operations with the appropriate accompanying vehicle.
One should prepare a pair of crucibles from seeds of <s>apāmārga</s>.
In that covered capsule one should place <s>sūta</s> mixed with the milk of <s>malayū</s>.
Flowers of <s>droṇapuṣpī</s>, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, and <s>arimedaka</s>
should be made into powder and placed below and above; then a seal is applied.
One should set that pellet properly in a covered earthen crucible and cook it.
In this way, by just one <s>puṭa</s>, the <s>sūtaka</s> becomes <s>bhasma</s>.
It should be applied according to the proper place, dose, and rule.
One should triturate mercury a little with the milk of <s>kākodumbarikā</s>.
With <s>hiṅgu</s> rubbed in that milk, one should prepare a pair of crucibles.

children.text: kṣiptvā tatsampuṭe sūtaṃ tatra mudrāṃ pradāpayet
children.translated_text: After placing <s>sūta</s> in that covered capsule, one should have the seal applied there.
Holding that pellet, the wise practitioner should place it in a larger covered earthen crucible,
and cook it with a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; in this way the <s>sūtaka</s> becomes <s>bhasma</s>.
Rubbed with the juices of <s>nāgavallī</s> and enclosed within a tuber of <s>karkoṭī</s>,
<s>sūta</s>, cooked in a covered earthen crucible, certainly becomes <s>bhasma</s>.
The wise physician should take, each equal to the purified <s>sūta</s>, red ochre,
brick, chalk, likewise alum, and rock salt,
anthill earth, alkaline salt, and potter's coloring clay.
All these should be powdered and then purified through cloth.
One should triturate <s>sūta</s> combined with these powders for a full <s>yāma</s>.
The <s>sūta</s> together with that powder should be placed inside a pot.
At the mouth of that pot one should set another pot of the same size.
One should seal the mouths of the two with clay pounded together with cloth.
After drying it, one should seal it again; after drying it again and again, seal it again.

children.text: samyagviśoṣya mudrāṃ tāṃ sthālīṃ cullyāṃ vidhārayet ||
children.translated_text: When that seal has been thoroughly dried, one should set the pot on the stove.
One should apply fire continuously for four days,
and carefully guard that apparatus upon the embers day and night.
One should open the apparatus slowly and take the mercury that has gone into the upper pot,
very pure like camphor and superior in qualities.
When that is mixed with <s>devakusuma</s>, sandalwood, musk, and saffron,

children.text: khādan harati phiraṅgaṃ vyādhiṃ sopadravaṃ sapadi ||
children.translated_text: and eaten, it quickly removes <s>phiraṅga</s> disease together with its complications.

children.text: vindati vahnerdīptiṃ puṣṭiṃ vīryaṃ balaṃ vipulam
children.translated_text: The constant user of <s>rasakarpūra</s> obtains a blazing digestive fire, nourishment, virility, and abundant strength,
and delights a hundred women.
The physician should take four parts of purified <s>sūta</s>,
one part of purified sulfur, and the same amount of artificial sulfur.
Or else one should take purified sulfur equal to half the mercury.
One should make a <s>kajjalikā</s> from the two and triturate it for one day.
One should pound clay together with cloth with very great care.
With that, one should coat a glass bottle properly three times.

children.text: mṛttikāṃ śoṣayitvā tu kūpyāṃ kajjalikāṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: After drying the clay, one should put the <s>kajjalikā</s> into the bottle.

children.text: tāṃ kūpīṃ vālukāyantre sthāpayitvā rasaṃ pacet ||
children.translated_text: Having placed that bottle in a sand apparatus, one should cook the mercury.
One should apply fire continuously for four days,
and take the mercury adhering above, resembling vermilion.
<s>Pārada</s> destroys worms and skin disease, grants victory, and improves sight; it is excellent.
It removes death, is very powerful, acts as a <s>yogavāhī</s>, and takes away fever.
It gives memory, vigor, and beauty, is aphrodisiac, promotes growth, and increases the bodily tissues.
It destroys impotence, is potent, moves through the sky, and is the supreme giver of accomplishments.
<s>Pārada</s> is remembered as the remover of every disease, possessing the six tastes and carrying every formulation.
It is declared to be made of the five elements; therefore it shines with their groups of qualities.

children.text: yasya rogasya yo yogastenaiva saha yojitaḥ
children.translated_text: For whatever disease there is a particular formulation, when combined with that very formulation,
<s>Rasendra</s> destroys that disease in men, elephants, and horses.
<s>Darada</s>, treated with ewe's milk and with the acidic group,
carefully for seven times, certainly attains purification.

children.text: tiktaṃ kaṣāyaṃ kaṭu hiṅgulaṃ syānnetrāmayaghnaṃ kaphapittahāri
children.translated_text: <s>Hiṅgula</s> is bitter, astringent, and pungent; it destroys eye diseases and removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
It also destroys nausea, itching, fever, jaundice, spleen disease, <s>āmavāta</s>, and poison.
Or, with lemon juice or neem-leaf juice, for the duration of one <s>yāma</s>,
one should rub <s>darada</s> and cause it to sublime upward, as in the procedure used with <s>sūta</s>.
There one should collect the excellent <s>rasa</s> adhering to the upper pot.

children.text: śuddhameva hi taṃ sūtaṃ sarvakarmasu yojayet ||
children.translated_text: That purified <s>sūta</s> alone should be used in all procedures.
Unpurified <s>gandhaka</s> causes skin disease, disorders of <s>pitta</s>, and dizziness.

children.text: hanti vīryyaṃ balaṃ rūpaṃ tasmācchuddhaḥ prayujyate ||
children.translated_text: It destroys virility, strength, and appearance; therefore it is used only when purified.
One should put ghee into an iron vessel and heat it over the fire.
When the ghee is hot, one should add an equal quantity of powder produced from <s>gandhaka</s>.
Seeing that the <s>gandhaka</s> has melted, one should pour it into a thin cloth.
In such a way that, after passing out through the cloth, all of it falls into milk,

children.text: evaṃ sa gandhakaḥ śuddhaḥ sarvakarmocito bhavet ||
children.translated_text: that <s>gandhaka</s> becomes purified and suitable for all procedures.
<s>Gandhaka</s> is pungent and bitter, hot in potency, astringent, and moving.
It increases <s>pitta</s>, is pungent in post-digestive effect, and conquers itching, erysipelas, and parasites.
As a <s>rasāyana</s>, it destroys skin disease, consumption, spleen disease, <s>kapha</s>, and <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: pīḍāṃ vidhatte vividhāṃ narāṇāṃ kuṣṭhaṃ kṣayaṃ pāṇḍugadaṃ ca kuryāt
children.translated_text: Unpurified <s>abhra</s> inflicts various pains on people and causes skin disease, consumption, and pallor disease.

children.text: hṛtpārśvapīḍāṃ ca karotyasahyām aśuddham abhraṃ guru vahnihṛtsyāt ||
children.translated_text: It causes unbearable pain in the heart and flanks; unpurified <s>abhra</s> is heavy and destroys the digestive fire.
One should blow black <s>abhraka</s> in the fire and then throw it into milk.
Having made its sheets split apart, one should treat it with the liquids of <s>taṇḍulīya</s> and sour gruel.
One should steep it for eight <s>yāmas</s>; in this way the <s>abhra</s> is purified.
After making that into <s>dhānyābhraka</s> and drying it, one should then triturate it.
In a mortar, with the latex of <s>arka</s> and cooked rice, one should make it into disk shapes.
One should wrap it with <s>arka</s> leaves and cook it properly in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.

children.text: punar mardyaṃ punaḥ pācyaṃ saptavārānpunaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It should be triturated again and cooked again, repeatedly, seven times.
Then, in the same way, three <s>puṭas</s> should be given with decoctions of banyan aerial roots.
It is calcined; there is no doubt of this. It may be used in all procedures.
One should cook ghee equal in quantity to calcined <s>abhra</s> in an iron vessel.

children.text: ghṛte jīrṇe tadabhraṃ tu sarvayogeṣu yojayet ||
children.translated_text: When the ghee has been absorbed, that <s>abhra</s> should be used in all formulations.
One should combine <s>abhra</s> with a quarter part of rice and then tie it in a blanket.
One should keep it in water for three nights; when it is soaked, one should rub it with the hands.
The fine material that has passed through the blanket and is free of sand,
that is called <s>dhānyābhra</s>, for the successful calcination of <s>abhra</s>.

children.text: abhraṃ kaṣāyaṃ madhuraṃ suśītamāyuṣkaraṃ dhātuvivarddhanaṃ ca
children.translated_text: <s>Abhra</s> is astringent and sweet, very cooling, life-promoting, and increasing to the bodily tissues.
It destroys the three <s>doṣas</s>, wounds, urinary disorders, skin disease, spleen and abdominal disease, tumors, poison, and worms.

children.text: rogān hanti draḍhayati vapurvīryavṛddhiṃ vidhatte tāruṇyāḍhyaṃ ramayati śataṃ yoṣitāṃ nityameva
children.translated_text: Calcined <s>abhra</s>, when used, destroys diseases, strengthens the body, produces an increase of virility, and, rich in youthfulness, always enables one to delight a hundred women.

children.text: dīrghāyuṣkāñjanayati sutān siṃhatulyaprabhāvānmṛtyor bhītiṃ harati sutarāṃ sevyamānaṃ mṛtābhram ||
children.translated_text: It gives rise to long-lived sons with lion-like power and very greatly removes the fear of death.
Unpurified <s>tāla</s> takes away life and causes disorders of <s>kapha</s>, <s>māruta</s>, and urinary disease.
It causes burning, eruptions, and contraction of the limbs; therefore one should purify it.

children.text: tālakaṃ kaṇaśaḥ kṛtvā taccūrṇaṃ kāñjike pacet
children.translated_text: One should break <s>tālaka</s> into small particles and cook that powder in sour gruel.
By means of a <s>dolāyantra</s>, for one month, and then with liquids produced from ash gourd,
one should cook it in sesame oil for one <s>yāma</s> and in <s>triphala</s> water for one <s>yāma</s>.

children.text: evaṃ yantre caturyāmaṃ pakvaṃ śudhyati tālakam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, when cooked in the apparatus for four <s>yāmas</s>, the <s>tālaka</s> is purified.
Purified layered <s>tālaka</s> should be treated with the juice of <s>paunarnava</s>.
One should triturate it in a mortar for one day and purify it afterward.
Then one should fill half of a pot with the alkalis of <s>punarnavā</s>.
Having placed that pellet there, one should fill it again with the same material.

children.text: ā kaṇṭhaṃ piṭharaṃ tasya pidhānaṃ dhārayenmukhe
children.translated_text: Up to the neck of that vessel, one should place a lid over its mouth.
One should set the pot on a stove and gradually increase the fire.
One should apply fire continuously for five days.
In this way that <s>tāla</s> is calcined; its dose is one <s>raktikā</s>.
Many after-drinks may be used, according to what is appropriate.
<s>Haritāla</s> is pungent, unctuous, astringent, and hot; it removes poison.
It removes itching, skin disease, diseases of the mouth and blood, <s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, scalp disorders, and wounds.
<s>Tālaka</s> removes diseases and takes away skin disease, death, and fever.
When purified, it produces complexion, an increase of virility, and also length of life.
There is another variety of <s>tālaka</s>, namely <s>manaḥśilā</s>; this is the difference between them.
<s>Tālaka</s> is very yellow, while <s>manaḥśilā</s> is red.

children.text: manaḥśilā mandabalaṃ karoti jantuṃ dhruvaṃ śodhanam antareṇa
children.translated_text: Without purification, <s>manaḥśilā</s> certainly makes a person weak.

children.text: malasya bandhaṃ kila mūtrarodhaṃ saśarkaraṃ kṛcchragadaṃ ca kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: It causes obstruction of feces, urinary retention, gravel, and the painful disease of dysuria.
One should cook <s>manaḥśilā</s> in goat urine for three days in a <s>dolāyantra</s>.
One should steep it seven times with goat bile; it becomes purified.

children.text: gurvī manaḥśilā varṇyā saroṣṇā lekhanī kaṭuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Manaḥśilā</s> is heavy, complexion-promoting, flowing, hot, scraping, and pungent.
It is bitter and unctuous, and removes poison, dyspnea, cough, spirit affliction, <s>kapha</s>, and blood disorders.

children.text: naramūtre ca gomūtre saptāhaṃ rasakaṃ pacet
children.translated_text: One should cook <s>rasaka</s> in human urine and cow urine for seven days.
By means of a <s>dolāyantra</s> it becomes purified; after that it should be used in procedures.

children.text: kharparaṃ kaṭukaṃ kṣāraṃ kaṣāyaṃ vāmakaṃ laghu
children.translated_text: <s>Kharpara</s> is pungent, alkaline, astringent, emetic, and light.
It is scraping, splitting, cooling, good for the eyes, and removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
It is regarded as the supreme destroyer of poison, stone disease, skin disease, and itching.
<s>Sūryāvarta</s>, <s>vajrakanda</s>, <s>kadalī</s>, and <s>devadālikā</s>,

children.text: śigruḥ kośātakī vandhyā kākamācī ca bālakam ||
children.translated_text: <s>śigru</s>, <s>kośātakī</s>, <s>vandhyā</s>, <s>kākamācī</s>, and <s>bālaka</s>:
with the juice of any one of these, together with the three alkalis and salts,
One should carefully steep them with the acidic group for one day.
Then the wise physician should cook them for a day in a <s>dolāyantra</s> with those liquids.

children.text: evaṃ śudhyanti te sarve proktā uparasā hi ye ||
children.translated_text: In this way all those substances that are called <s>uparasa</s> become purified.

children.text: kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ gairikaṃ śaṅkhaḥ kāsīsaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, <s>gairika</s> (red ochre), <s>śaṅkha</s> (conch shell), <s>kāsīsa</s>, and likewise <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,
<s>Nīlāñjana</s>, the varieties of <s>śukti</s> (oyster shell), small shells, together with cowries,
when steamed with water of <s>jambīra</s> and washed with warm water,
these attain purification and are to be used by physicians for the success of formulations.

children.text: aśuddhaṃ kurute vajraṃ kuṣṭhaṃ pārśvavyathāṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Unpurified <s>vajra</s> produces skin disease and pain in the side,
as well as pallor and lameness; therefore one should purify it and calcine it.
One should cook <s>vajra</s> placed inside a <s>vyāghrī</s> tuber in a <s>dolāyantra</s>, in a decoction of <s>kulattha</s> and <s>kodrava</s>.
After three days that becomes purified.
Having taken <s>vajra</s> on an auspicious day, one should put it inside a <s>vyāghrī</s> tuber.
After smearing it with buffalo dung, one should cook it in a fire of dung cakes.
After three <s>yāmas</s>, in the fourth <s>yāma</s> at the end of the night, one should sprinkle it with horse urine.
Cooked in this way, it is purified in seven nights.
One should put the repeatedly heated <s>vajra</s> into a decoction of <s>kulattha</s> mixed with <s>hiṅgu</s> and rock salt.
After being heated again and again twenty-one times, the <s>vajra</s> becomes <s>bhasma</s>.
Ram's horn, snake bone, turtle shell, and <s>amlavetasa</s>,
together with hare's tooth in equal measure, should be ground with the milk of <s>vajrī</s> and made into a pellet.

children.text: kṛtvā tanmadhyagaṃ vajraṃ mriyate dhmātameva hi ||
children.translated_text: With the <s>vajra</s> placed in the middle of that, it is indeed calcined when heated by blowing.

children.text: āyuḥ puṣṭiṃ balaṃ vīryaṃ varṇaṃ saukhyaṃ karoti ca
children.translated_text: Consumed as calcined <s>vajra</s>, it produces long life, nourishment, strength, virility, complexion, and well-being.

children.text: sevitaṃ sarvarogaghnaṃ mṛtaṃ vajraṃ na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Calcined <s>vajra</s> destroys all diseases, without doubt.
Like <s>vajra</s>, one should purify and calcine all gems as well.

children.text: śuddhānāṃ māritānāṃ ca teṣāṃ śṛṇu guṇānapi ||
children.translated_text: Hear also the qualities of those when they have been purified and calcined.
Gems are cooling in potency, and in taste they are sweet and astringent.
They benefit the eyes, are scraping, are laxative, and counteract poison.
When worn, they are auspicious and also remove the hostile glance of planets.
That which has leaves resembling <s>sindhuvāra</s> and likewise the shape of a calf's navel,
and beside which no tree grows, is called <s>vatsanābha</s>.

children.text: gomūtre tridinaṃ sthāpyaṃ viṣaṃ tena viśudhyati
children.translated_text: Poison should be kept in cow's urine for three days; by that the poison is purified.
Likewise, it should be kept in a cloth smeared with red-mustard oil.

children.text: ye guṇā garale proktāste syurhīnā viśodhanāt
children.translated_text: The qualities that are stated for poison become diminished through purification.
Therefore, when poison is to be used, one should use it only after purifying it.

children.text: viṣaṃ prāṇaharaṃ proktaṃ vyavāyi ca vikāśi ca
children.translated_text: Poison is said to take life; it is <s>vyavāyi</s> (quickly diffusive) and <s>vikāśi</s> (loosening).
It is fiery, removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>, acts as a <s>yogavāhī</s>, and causes intoxication.
That very poison, when properly combined, is life-giving and a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative).
It is the supreme <s>yogavāhī</s>, conquers <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>, and removes <s>sannipāta</s>.
The latex of <s>arka</s>, the latex of <s>snuhī</s>, <s>lāṅgalī</s>, and <s>karavīra</s>,
<s>guñjā</s>, <s>ahiphena</s>, and <s>dhattūra</s>: these are the seven classes of <s>upaviṣa</s> (secondary poison).
After more than a year, a medicine in its natural form becomes deficient in qualities.
Likewise, after two months a powder loses its potency.
Pills and electuaries become deficient if a year has passed.
Similarly, ghee, oil, and the like become deficient after more than four months.
Cooked ghee, after more than a year, comes to have diminished potency.
Oil, whether cooked or uncooked, lasts a long time and is richer in qualities.
Herbs that are quick to process become devoid of potency after more than a year.

children.text: purāṇāḥ syurguṇair yuktā āsavo dhātavo rasāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When old, <s>āsava</s> preparations, metals, and <s>rasa</s> substances are endowed with good qualities.
